title: Our NFL Week 11 crystal ball: Five analysts make predictions, from upsets to TD scorers
summary: Eagles upsetting the Steelers? Big receiving day for Christian McCaffrey? Touchdown for Josh Downs? Let's predict 15 things for Week 11.
full_text:
Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Texans defeated the Colts on Thursday night . But what will happen in the remaining 12 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.
First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs that could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.
Could the Eagles pull off an upset over the Steelers? Is 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey in for a big receiving day against the Vikings? Does Titans quarterback Cam Ward have fantasy potential against the Cowboys? Will we see another touchdown for wide receiver Josh Downs in a Chiefs uniform?
Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.
Jump to: Upset picks | Projected stat lines Fantasy sleepers, surprises TD scorers | Other predictions
Philadelphia Eagles +4.5 (+180 moneyline) vs. Pittsburgh Steelers
Quarterback Aaron Rodgers hasn't given much reason to trust Pittsburgh laying points on the road Sunday . Philadelphia's specialty is playing more man coverage and sending extra rushers, both of which have bothered Rodgers in 2026. Plus, defensive tackle Jalen Carter can attack an offensive line that just lost guard Mason McCormick ( ankle ).
Eagles backup QB Joe Milton taking sacks is the main concern for their offense, but he can still get positive yards as a scrambler. With wide receiver DeVonta Smith potentially returning from a hamstring injury, the Eagles have enough to win this by a field goal.
Minnesota Vikings +3 (+138 moneyline) vs. San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City
Minnesota's defense remains the strength in this Sunday night matchup . Coordinator Brian Flores brings pressure from different places, and 49ers QB Brock Purdy took five sacks against Dallas in Week 10 . The Vikings have also been excellent at forcing field goals near the end zone.
Quarterback Kirk Cousins faces a tough matchup himself in his second start for Minnesota, but he gives it a more reliable offense than before. In Mexico City, I trust the Vikings' defense to keep this tight and give Cousins a shot to win it late.
George Karlaftis , Edge, Kansas City Chiefs : 2.5 sacks, 7 pressures, 31% pass rush win rate
It's hard to imagine a better matchup to record a sack than this. Karlaftis typically lines up opposite the left tackle, which means he'll face Arizona's Jayden Williams -- who ranks dead last in pass block win rate at tackle but has missed the past two weeks with a knee injury -- or Williams' backup Josh Fryar .
Karlaftis will be chasing down rookie QB Carson Beck in his second career start -- Beck took five sacks (at over a 20% sack rate) in his debut against the Rams -- or veteran journeyman Josh Johnson . Plus, the Chiefs are 15.5-point favorites , so the Cardinals almost certainly will be behind and need to pass.
Christian McCaffrey , RB, San Francisco 49ers : 9 receptions, 74 receiving yards, 1 receiving touchdown
I'm focusing on McCaffrey's receiving production because I think that will be the headline here. He is already an elite receiving back, but this Vikings matchup should result in heavy usage through the air.
All running backs catch passes more frequently against zone coverage compared to man (almost twice as often), and Minnesota plays the second-highest rate of zone coverage in the league (74%). It also blitzes the most of any team, which would cause most running backs to stay in and block most of the time. But not McCaffrey, as he still runs a route 65% of the time when the opponent blitzes.
So when Minnesota brings the heat in Mexico City, Purdy is going to be looking for his star running back ... a lot.
Joe Burrow , QB, Cincinnati Bengals : 31-of-39, 378 passing yards, 3 touchdowns, 0 sacks, 91 QBR
I know this is chalky considering the heater Burrow is on, but I feel especially confident that he will put up numbers against the Commanders .
Washington blitzes 42% of the time, the third-highest rate in the league, but somehow has a below average pass rush win rate. That is quite the indictment on its ability to disrupt the opposing quarterback. And it's an especially bad combination against Burrow, who is thriving even more when blitzed (86 QBR) than when not (77 QBR) in 2026.
Burrow has also become quite adept at sack avoidance (4.4% sack rate), which is partially a reflection of better pass protection this season. Plus, the Commanders have the most pass-inducing defense in the league, based on NFL Next Gen Stats' opponent pass rate over expected.
Ryan Flournoy , WR, Dallas Cowboys (37.8% rostered in ESPN leagues)
It's easy to overlook Flournoy as the Cowboys' WR3 behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , but he has been productive. Over the past six games, Flournoy has averaged 5.1 targets and 13.2 fantasy points per game.
The Titans-Cowboys matchup has one of the highest totals on the slate. And Tennessee's defense has allowed the most receptions and fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.
Cam Ward , QB, Tennessee Titans (26.0%)
Let's stick with the same game and go with Ward, who has scored at least 19 fantasy points in each of his past two games. He'll be without wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson ( ankle ) but could get back rookie Carnell Tate , who has missed the past two games due to a shoulder injury . Ward is a dual-threat quarterback with an excellent matchup against a Cowboys defense that has allowed the third-most fantasy points and third-most rushing yards per game to quarterbacks.
Justice Hill , RB, Baltimore Ravens (18.7%)
Ravens running back Derrick Henry has struggled recently, averaging just 3.0 yards per carry over his past five games. Hill, on the other hand, had at least eight touches and scored at least 8.0 fantasy points in each of those games, including 18.2 fantasy points against the Jaguars in Week 9 .
Hill could continue to be more involved Sunday against the Panthers . Carolina has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to running backs this season.
Josh Downs , WR, Kansas City Chiefs
After getting traded from the Colts , Downs caught a touchdown pass in his Chiefs debut against the Falcons . He finished with 53 receiving yards on five targets, operating as an outlet from slot alignments for quarterback Patrick Mahomes . Plus, Downs can attack the third level on seams or wheel routes.
Downs has a great matchup in Week 11 versus a Cardinals defense that has allowed 22 touchdown passes (tied for most in the league) and plays zone coverage on 67.5% of opponent dropbacks. Chiefs coach Andy Reid will have answers to scheme open Downs for a score.
Javonte Williams , RB, Dallas Cowboys
While Williams has found the end zone only once in the past three games, he has nine rushing scores on the year and at least one goal-to-go carry in nine games. I'm expecting him to cash in on a low red zone attempt Sunday against the Titans. Tennessee has allowed 10 rushing touchdowns this season, tied for the 10th most in the NFL.
Courtland Sutton , WR, Denver Broncos
Let's take Sutton in a positive matchup versus the Raiders' defense . He has only two touchdown receptions this season, but he has seen seven end zone targets from quarterback Bo Nix , including one in two of his past three games. And Las Vegas has given up 22 touchdown passes in 2026, tied with the Cardinals for the most in the league.
The Titans will beat the Cowboys
I don't particularly love the Cowboys changing defensive playcallers the week before they play the Titans, who have gone no-huddle on a whopping 40% of their snaps since Week 7. The Titans' willingness to speed up Dallas will strain its communication with a new coach on the mic, and WR Carnell Tate 's return to practice Thursday (albeit in a limited fashion) could foretell a return to the starting lineup.

title: Week 11 matchup previews, predictions, picks and nuggets
summary: There are 12 more games in Week 11, and we have picks, predictions and more for all of them.
full_text:
Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season is here! The Eagles are hosting the Steelers in the Battle of Pennsylvania, and Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins makes his second start against the 49ers in two weeks. The Chargers will face off against the Jets, looking for their second win on a short week, and Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza will get his second career start when Las Vegas meets Denver. The Jaguars look to keep rolling against the Giants, and the Ravens travel to Carolina.
We're here to get you ready for the action. First, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside the locker room with the best thing they heard this week, and ESPN Research provides a key stat to know. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder makes a bold prediction for each matchup, fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Walder all give us final score picks for every game.
Let's get into the full Week 11 slate, which culminates with a "Monday Night Football" matchup between the Bengals and Commanders on ESPN . (Game times are Sunday unless otherwise noted, and all odds are via DraftKings.)

What we're hearing on the Cardinals: Sunday will be quarterback Carson Beck 's second career start, but it'll be his first chance to build on his NFL debut. His goal is to get to "elite communication," which he described as being better at relaying the plays to the huddle, knowing what the plays are within the first few words and having a better understanding of what defenses are trying to do. "Being that level of prepared and having elite communication and then ultimately just going out and letting it rip," Beck said. "I think that's something that I did decent in the last game, but that's something that I want to build up to my standard where I see the defense, I see the play and you already know the ball's coming out." -- Josh Weinfuss
What we're hearing on the Chiefs: Much of Sunday's game for the Chiefs is about managing injuries, especially before their Thanksgiving showdown against the Bills. Several veterans are not expected to play against the Cardinals, including right tackle Jaylon Moore (right ankle), right guard Trey Smith (concussion protocol) and running back Kenneth Walker III ( groin ). "He had a sore groin [last week]," coach Andy Reid said Wednesday of Walker. "It's getting better. We just don't want to do something stupid and put him out there. It's still bugging him a little bit, but he's feeling a lot better than he was." -- Nate Taylor
Stat to know: The Cardinals ran season-high 82% of plays out of shotgun in Beck's first start. The Chiefs' defense has the second-best touchdown-to-interception rate (three passing TDs, six INTs) against shotgun in the NFL behind Vikings (4 TDs, 10 INTs, 0.4), per NFL Next Gen Stats. -- ESPN Research
Bold prediction: Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat will sack quarterback Patrick Mahomes . Moore sat out last week's game because of an ankle injury and his status is in question for Week 11. But even if he plays, Moore has just a ninth percentile pass block win rate this season. And Sweat has a 72nd percentile pass rush win rate despite having only three sacks. -- Walder
Injuries: Cardinals | Chiefs
Fantasy nugget: The Chiefs' defense has scored at least nine fantasy points in each of its past two games and has another favorable matchup against the Cardinals with Beck under center. The Cardinals rank near the bottom of the league in both total yards and points scored per game, setting the stage for another dominant performance by Kansas City's defense. See Week 11 rankings . -- Moody
Betting insight: Under Reid since 2013, Chiefs' games are 14-37-2 O/U as home favorites of at least seven points, including six straight unders. Beck struggled to keep Arizona moving in his debut, and Kansas City's defense has been tough at home. Mahomes can build a lead before the Chiefs lean on the run, depriving a struggling Arizona offense chances to score points. Read more . -- Maldonado
Maldonado's pick: Chiefs 27, Cardinals 10 Moody's pick: Chiefs 30, Cardinals 10 Walder's pick: Chiefs 26, Cardinals 20 FPI prediction: KC, 88.3% (by an average of 12 points)
Matchup must-reads: Source: Cardinals' QB Minshew has surgery to repair right UCL ... Kelce's 100th game at Arrowhead: His most memorable moments ... Mahomes not concerned about elbow leading into Week 11

What we're hearing on the Ravens: The run defense is confident heading into Sunday's game even though Baltimore gave up its first 100-yard rusher in 24 games. Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard has had at least 75 rushing yards in six games this season, which is the second most in the NFL. "[Hubbard] has to worry about us as a defense," linebacker Trenton Simpson said. "I believe that if every guy on our defense does our 1-of-11, he has to deal with us." -- Jamison Hensley
What we're hearing on the Panthers: Interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash has a notable familiarity with Ravens running back Derrick Henry . Wash said Henry "was a damn thorn in our side" in the AFC South when Wash was the coordinator in Jacksonville (2016 to 2020), and Henry was leading the Titans' backfield. Henry was held to only 10 rushing yards (but had two rushing touchdowns) against the Chargers on Monday, and Wash's unit has limited opponents to just 2.6 yards per carry over the past two games. But Wash is still mindful that "anytime Derrick Henry steps on the field, you're concerned, as a coach." -- Mike Kaye
Stat to know: The Panthers are 10-1 over the past 20 seasons against teams on a five-plus game losing streak (lone loss: 2012 Week 13 at Chiefs). -- ESPN Research
Bold prediction: Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan will record 100-plus receiving yards. It has been more than a month since McMillan recorded at least 60 receiving yards in a game, but I'm betting on a bounce back -- especially with Marlon Humphrey not playing for the Ravens. -- Walder

He still finished with 15 touches and 19.0 fantasy points thanks to two rushing touchdowns. Henry has averaged only 44.6 rushing yards per game over his past five games, but the arrival of quarterback Jacoby Brissett has revived the Ravens' passing game. title: Sources: Nacua needs 4-5 months to recover from knee surgery, out for playoffs
summary: Puka Nacua's recovery time from his MCL surgery is considered to be 4-5 months, sources told ESPN, meaning he will miss the playoffs.
full_text:
Puka Nacua 's recovery time from his MCL surgery is considered to be four to five months, sources told ESPN, meaning the Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver will miss the rest of this season, including the playoffs.
Sources told ESPN that three doctors recommended that Nacua undergo the surgery, which is expected to have him healthy for the 2027 season.
Nacua's knee checked out clean aside from the MCL, according to a source. The operation was performed by team doctor Neal ElAttrache, a source told ESPN.
Rams coach Sean McVay said Friday that Nacua, who is serving a three-game suspension while on injured reserve, will likely miss at least the rest of the regular season after undergoing the MCL surgery Tuesday.
McVay added that the possibility of Nacua returning for the postseason was a scenario that the Rams "haven't thought about."
The NFL was unaware that Nacua had already undergone surgery when it imposed its suspension, a source told ESPN on Friday.
In seven games this season, Nacua had 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns. The two-time Pro Bowler suffered the knee injury, along with a turf toe injury, on the Rams' final offensive snap of their Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders and was placed on IR on Nov. 12.
Nacua, 25, is playing on the final season of his rookie deal and is scheduled to be an unrestricted free agent this season.
author: Adam Schefter

title: New Cardinals QB Johnson, on 15th team, set to start with Beck out
summary: Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck has been downgraded to out, paving the way for 40-year-old Josh Johnson to start against the Chiefs.
full_text:
Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs , paving the way for 40-year-old Josh Johnson to get his first start for Arizona.
Coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that Arizona was preparing Johnson to start after Beck experienced back spasms again this week. Beck didn't practice Thursday or Friday after being a limited participant Wednesday.
Sunday against the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium will be Johnson's first start since Week 18 of last season and just his 12th career start after being a fifth-round pick in 2008. He is 2-9 overall.
Although he doesn't have a lot of starting experience compared with his longevity in the league -- Arizona is his 15th NFL team -- the situation Johnson is in feels "familiar."
"It's kind of my testimony my whole life, just the unknown, what can happen," Johnson said. "And so just always just being in the moment, being prepared for myself. I've been in this situation, particularly in the NFL, a lot. So more excited than nerves, I would say."
Johnson said he is in a constant state of staying ready, which has been a factor in him playing into his 40s. At this point in his career, he's used to it.
Last season, Johnson replaced injured Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota in Week 16 and then started the final two games of the season after not starting since 2021.
"My job is to always be ready no matter what, no matter how the situation," Johnson said. "So I focus more on that than what's not ideal. And so this is just the next step of that process, and it keeps happening and so you just keep accepting it. You don't fight it, you embrace it, and you just go with it."
Johnson said his experience working with LaFleur in 2020 when LaFleur was the San Francisco 49ers ' receivers coach and in 2021 with the New York Jets when LaFleur was the offensive coordinator will help "tremendously" on Sunday.
"Just understanding how he calls the game first and foremost is very important because you don't have to get antsy, like, 'Oh, what is he going to do in these moments?'" Johnson said. "And Mike is pretty consistent. He's been consistent. I've always been a big fan of him as a playcaller, as a coach, just in general."
Johnson is also familiar with Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo, having played against him and being on the Giants when Spagnuolo was New York's defensive coordinator in 2016.
Despite a familiarity and comfort with LaFleur, Johnson is also realistic about how Sunday can go after spending less than two weeks learning the offense.
"I also understand that everything ain't going to be perfect," Johnson said. "I'm not trying to go out there and be perfect. I'm trying to go out there and play winning football."
author: Josh Weinfuss

title: Colts cut ties with QB Jones, turn to Richardson for next start
summary: The Colts have cut quarterback Daniel Jones after a challenging 11-game stint in 2026 and are turning to Anthony Richardson Sr. to start going forward.
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Daniel Jones ' tenure in Indianapolis is over.
The Colts waived the veteran quarterback Friday, one day after one of the worst performances of his career in a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans .
Coach Shane Steichen announced the franchise's decision to move on from his handpicked quarterback, who re-signed in March to a two-year, $88 million contract with $50 million fully guaranteed at signing that confirmed his place as the team's starter heading into the 2026 season.
After an ugly 11 games following a torn Achilles tendon he sustained late last season, Jones is out and 2023 fourth overall draft pick Anthony Richardson Sr. is in as the Colts' starting quarterback moving forward.
Daniel Jones, who was released by the Colts on Friday, is the second quarterback this century to start each of his team's first 11 games of a season and never throw for multiple touchdown passes (Cam Ward, 2025 Titans).
"Can't say enough good things about Daniel," Steichen said. "Just the ultimate competitor, ultimate teammate, the toughness that he brought to our football team. Can't say enough good things about him. I mean, guy played on a broken leg for us last year for three or four games. Snaps his Achilles, came back in 8½ months and gave this organization everything he had, and couldn't be more thankful for the time I had with him."
Steichen was referring to a hairline fibula fracture that slowed Jones last season before he sustained the Achilles tear.
The Colts elected to not just bench Jones, going the extra step to waive him. Asked to elaborate, Steichen, who had vociferously defended Jones in previous weeks, didn't offer much clarity but said the quarterback did not ask to be released.
"It's really just the best for both parties," Steichen said.
The Colts' offensive struggles reached a new low Thursday. The Jones-led unit failed to score a touchdown for the first time this season, with Jones completing 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards with one interception. It was the seventh game in 11 starts this season that Jones completed less than 60% of his attempts.
Jones, 29, leads the NFL with 13 interceptions and had career lows in completion rate (58.4%), QBR (29.1) and yards per attempt (5.6).
So a season that will be remembered for a series of difficult decisions -- including the firing of general manager Chris Ballard last month and the recent trades of four starters -- adds another casualty.
Jones' contract contained an injury guarantee of $10.5 million that would have been owed by the Colts if he sustained an injury, even in practice. Waiving him eliminates the potential for that to happen.
Jones will need to clear waivers before he can become a free agent. That should happen by Monday afternoon unless a team claims him. There was interest in Jones before last week's NFL trade deadline, but the Colts did not make concerted effort to deal him, sources told ESPN.
The Jones chapter could not have started and ended in more disparate fashion. Last season, in his first year in Indianapolis, Jones and the Colts' offense got off to a sizzling start. Jones ranked second in QBR, third in completion rate and third in yards per attempt through the first eight weeks of 2025, when the Colts were 7-1. Since then, he ranks near the bottom in each of those categories.
"There's a lot of factors," Steichen said. "I don't think it was just on one person. I think there's a lot of factors that played into it. Obviously, the quarterback takes a lot of the blame. Obviously, that's the business that we're in. But things just didn't work out."
Now, Richardson gets another shot in the twilight of his rookie contract, which expires after the season. He started for parts of two seasons in 2023 and 2024 but never established any consistency and struggled to be a consistent passer.
It has been nearly two years since he started a game, and the Colts will hope for some growth as they attempt to figure out what their future looks like at the position. Richardson is in his fourth season but just 24.
"I think, obviously, he's matured and grown over the last couple years," Steichen said of Richardson. "He's had some unfortunate situations, some injuries that he's had to deal with. But again, it's another opportunity to go out and compete and go show what he's about. And I'm excited for that opportunity for him moving forward."
author: Stephen Holder

title: Melo calls out Humphrey for Baltimore remark: Back your apology with action
summary: Former NBA star Carmelo Anthony challenged Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey to do more than apologize after he said Baltimore was "best at making criminals."
full_text:
Basketball Hall of Famer Carmelo Anthony criticized the Ravens ' Marlon Humphrey for his disparaging remark about Baltimore, accepting the cornerback's apology but challenging him to do more for the city he represents.
Anthony, who grew up in West Baltimore, addressed Humphrey in a lengthy statement on Instagram on Friday, two days after the four-time Pro Bowler made a quip on his podcast that Baltimore was "best at making criminals."
In his post, Anthony described growing up on Myrtle Avenue, losing friends to violence and watching people he loved be "swallowed by a system that was built to swallow them." He said Humphrey's remarks were especially hurtful coming from a player who wears a Baltimore uniform.
"I've been sitting with this one for a couple of days, because Baltimore isn't a talking point to me. It's in my blood," wrote Anthony, a 10-time All-Star who played 19 seasons in the NBA.
"When one of our own stands on our name and says the best thing Baltimore makes is criminals, and then laughs that it'll get cut out, that doesn't get cut out for me," he wrote. "It doesn't get cut out for the kid in Baltimore who heard it. It doesn't get cut out for the mother working two jobs to keep her son off the corner."
Humphrey made the remark on an episode of "The Marlon Humphrey Show" that was released Wednesday. Asked what Baltimore was best at making, he mentioned "The Star-Spangled Banner" and National Bohemian beer before answering, "They're best at making criminals."
He received heavy fan backlash on social media Wednesday afternoon, and the podcast episode featuring Humphrey's "criminals" comment has since been deleted from his YouTube page. After Wednesday's practice, Humphrey said he regretted the remark.
The Ravens sent Humphrey home from the team facility Thursday and announced that he would be inactive for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers . Coach Jesse Minter said the punishment was for one game only and that Humphrey would not practice the rest of the week.
"He's very remorseful," Minter said Thursday. "I think he understands that words mean a lot, especially to people in this city."
In addressing Humphrey's apology, Anthony wrote: "Baltimore has been apologized to its whole life. Apologies don't build anything. Presence does."
Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott also was critical of Humphrey's remark, saying an apology was not enough. He invited Humphrey to sit down with him and some Baltimore citizens "who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made."
In his Instagram post Friday, Anthony urged Humphrey to accept Scott's invitation and even offered to accompany him.
"The Mayor opened a door. Walk through it," Anthony wrote. "And when you do, call me. I'll meet you there."

title: Titans DL Harrell hospitalized after car accident in Tampa
summary: Titans defensive lineman Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident Friday and remains hospitalized, according to the team.
full_text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Tennessee Titans defensive lineman Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident Friday and remains hospitalized, according to the team.
Harrell, 24, was a passenger in an Uber in Tampa, Florida, when the accident occurred. No further details were available.
"Yesterday, Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident that resulted in him being taken to the hospital in his hometown of Tampa, Florida," the Titans said in a statement. "We have been in constant communication with Jaylen's family and are still working to gather more information.
"At this time, Jaylen remains in the hospital and continues to receive care. We ask that Jaylen and his family's privacy be respected at this time. We will provide an update when appropriate."
Harrell tore his ACL in the preseason and was placed on season-ending injured reserve. The Titans selected Harrell in the seventh round of the 2024 draft, and he finished his rookie season with 13 combined tackles.
He started two games for Tennessee in 2025 and 25 combined tackles, including 4.5 sacks and a forced fumble.
author: Turron Davenport

title: Steelers activate WR Wilson off IR for Eagles game
summary: The Steelers have activated wide receiver Roman Wilson from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles.
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Steelers have activated wide receiver Roman Wilson from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles .
Fellow wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. , though, was not activated from injured reserve. The Steelers will also be without outside linebacker Nick Herbig , who was downgraded to out with a hip/ribs injury Saturday.
The Steelers elevated practice squad wide receiver Max Hurleman after the former undrafted free agent earned votes of confidence from quarterback Aaron Rodgers and coach Mike McCarthy over the past two weeks. They also signed linebacker KJ Henry to the active roster to help replace Herbig.
Wilson has been out since fracturing one finger and dislocating another in the Steelers' Week 5 win against the Indianapolis Colts . His return figures to boost the Steelers' sluggish passing game and could help alleviate the attention on top receiver DK Metcalf , who has struggled throughout the season.
A 2024 third-round pick, Wilson was developing into a reliable deep threat prior to his injury, with touchdowns in back-to-back games for the first time in his career.
"Instead of having four receivers up, we'll probably have five or six," Metcalf said Thursday. "So I mean a lot more rotation, a lot of fresh bodies. But just watching them out there at practice these past couple days, they look fresh, they look ready to go to me."
Wilson had his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve opened earlier this week and was a full participant in practice each day this week.
author: Brooke Pryor

title: Raiders owner Davis upset by 'Madden' version of his father: 'Totally unfair'
summary: Saying "I did the best I could to protect him," Raiders owner Mark Davis expressed frustration with the depiction of his father, the late Al Davis, in the new movie "Madden."
full_text:
Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis said he was "hurt" by the depiction of his father, the late Al Davis, in the movie "Madden" that was released on Prime Video this week.
"I did the best I could to protect him," Mark Davis told USA Today Sports on Friday. "It's absolutely a crime that they're able to treat people that have passed away and characterize them in ways that are unfair, and there's nobody around to protect their legacies. It's just unfair. I don't know what the purpose of the movie was to be real honest."
"Madden" tells the story of legendary football coach, broadcast and video game icon John Madden, with Nicolas Cage in the titular role and Christian Bale as Al Davis. The film has received criticism for some over-the-top portrayals of several notable sports figures, with The Associated Press review describing the performances as running the "gamut from 'SNL'-style parody to earnest drama."
"Cage's prosthetic-aided performance feels more like a well-meaning misfire than any kind of real travesty. This is more like a goofy, unfunny comedy that can't find the end zone, let alone the 50-yard line," AP reviewer Jake Coyle wrote.
Mark Davis echoed some of that review, calling "Madden" a cross between "Pulp Fiction," "Vacation" and "Saturday Night Live" -- and "not in a good way."
He said the filmmakers had reached out to him about aspects of the movie but that he was off-put by how it depicted his father's reaction to a massive injury to New England Patriots wide receiver Darryl Stingley during a 1978 preseason game against the Raiders. Mark Davis said the filmmakers said they wouldn't be able to change the scene.
"For them to put in the Darryl Stingley incident, that my dad was trying to talk John [Madden] out of going to see him -- that was just such a hurt to me personally because that's my father's legacy is how he treated people," Mark Davis told USA Today. "No matter whether they were Raiders or not, he cared about people. That's one of the redeeming qualities of my father throughout his life. And I just thought it was totally unfair for them to portray it that way."
Mark Davis focused his frustration on the filmmakers, saying "I don't blame Christian Bale. I don't blame Nicholas Cage. All they did was what the director and the writers told them to do."
Al Davis served as coach, general manager and owner of the Raiders. Inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1992, Davis became principal owner of the Raiders in 1972 and ran the team until his death in 2011.

title: Chiefs again without RB Walker against Cardinals
summary: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III will not play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals after not participating in practice this week due to a groin injury.
full_text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III has been ruled out of Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals after not participating in any of the team's three practices this week due to a groin injury, it was announced Friday.
The Chiefs will also be without two offensive linemen, as right tackle Jaylon Moore (right ankle) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion protocol) also didn't practice this week.
The Chiefs are optimistic that all three players can be available for the game against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night.
Walker reported tightness in his groin before the Chiefs' final on-field practice ahead of last week's game against the Atlanta Falcons . He was ruled out, paving the way for rookie Emmett Johnson to make his first start.
In eight games this season, Walker has 872 rushing yards and a career-high 11 total touchdowns. He is expected to again be replaced by Johnson, who generated 171 all-purpose yards and two receiving touchdowns in the win over the Falcons.

title: ❤️ Bengals pay tribute to Fiona the hippo after her death
summary: The world-famous hippopotamus passed away Thursday after ingesting a hat that made its way into her enclosure.
full_text:
After news broke Thursday that the Cincinnati Zoo's famous hippo, Fiona, had died, the Queen City's sports teams were quick to pay tribute.
Fiona's death came as a result of health complications following her swallowing of a child's knit cap that had made it into her enclosure. According to zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley, the hat entered Fiona's habitat after it was tossed into the air by a visitor and caught by a ceiling fan that catapulted it through a small opening above the area's viewing windows.
"Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore," Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said . "She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many."
The 9-year-old Nile hippopotamus rose to fame in 2017, when she was born at the Cincinnati Zoo six weeks premature, requiring around-the-clock care to survive. Survive she did, though, becoming beloved as both she and her story grew.
Each of Cincinnati's three major professional sports teams took to social media after news of Fiona's death broke to honor her legacy as an icon of the city.

title: Eight stadiums, seven countries, four continents: NFL field director has earned a break
summary: Nick Pappas is the man charged with making sure international venues are up to standard to host NFL games.
full_text:
Nick Pappas will finally go home soon.
When the NFL's field director steps on a flight Monday night at Benito Juarez International Airport in Mexico City bound for Atlanta, it'll be the last leg of the longest stretch of travel he's done in his role overseeing the fields for all the league's international games.
Eleven weeks. Nine games. Eight stadiums. Seven fields. Seven countries. Four continents. His first regular-season trip was to Melbourne in September. His last was to Mexico City. In between, Pappas went to Brazil, England, France, Spain and Germany. From the time he left Rio de Janeiro on Sept. 28, the night after the Cowboys-Ravens game, Pappas spent just about two weeks at home with his wife and three kids.
This season -- with an NFL-record nine international games -- was an exhausting stretch for Pappas. He survived on coffee -- lots of it -- and two workouts a day.
"The work, it feels effortless, honestly, at times," Pappas said. "It's obviously, for me, it's being away from my family more than anything. I've got three little kids and a rock star of a wife, so I'm very fortunate to be able to be away and commit my time and put the energy into these games that it deserves and it requires."
And that's just the in-season international travel.
He flies to every international market at least once during the offseason. If the league has been there before, like Munich, London or Madrid, Pappas might go once in an offseason, twice maximum.
But for new cities, such as Rio de Janeiro and Paris this year, he might visit anywhere between six and 12 times over the two years before kickoff. He went to Brazil three times before the game this year. On one of those trips, Pappas flew overnight from Atlanta, landed in the morning, spent about 14 hours at Maracana Stadium and then flew back that night, not even getting a hotel. And because of how far Melbourne is, Pappas went once in December 2024, once over the summer and again in September for the game.
How often he visits a stadium depends on how complex adapting the stadiums to NFL standards will be.
In Melbourne, Pappas was working with a massive field suitable for cricket, rugby and Aussie Rules Football, which made the transition to an NFL field easier than most other venues.
However, the fields had to be extended in Rio de Janeiro and Madrid, where the first couple rows of seats had to be removed, and both required a bit of engineering to shape the surfaces to the exact specifications of the NFL.
Perhaps the biggest challenge for Pappas when it comes to international games is "trying to provide a surface globally that meets our compliance standards first and foremost, but then also meets the preference of our athletes. Preference isn't always captured in compliance."
In an ideal world, Pappas would ship Bermuda grass to every venue that hosts an NFL game. Well, the world isn't ideal. He has to rely on what's available to him either at the stadium or within driving distance, whether that's from a sod farm in Milan that grows the field for the Munich game or the sod farms in Holland or London that he's had to rely upon in the past to fix quick needs.
"We've seen grass get trucked all over the U.S. I mean, the perspective is pretty similar," Pappas said. "It's just there's always challenges when you're going country to country versus state to state, importation from Italy to Germany."
One of the most notable differences Pappas experiences while preparing the international fields is the amount of paint required. Grounds crews in foreign countries don't deal with the amount of paint that an NFL field requires.
But that's part of what makes Pappas' job stressful and challenging. He needs to provide a playing surface that is playable and doesn't become a topic of conversation after the game, while looking, aesthetically, like every other NFL field that fans see on TV.
"There's a lot of attention paid to this," said Jeff Miller, the NFL's executive vice president for player health and safety. "Nick's performance is measured in front of the millions of viewers who watch the games. That's not unlike many other aspects of this business. Millions of people are watching the officials. Millions of people are watching the coaches. Millions of people are watching the players. Millions of people are evaluating the league's decision to go play in a particular market, and the field is one of those things.
"So Nick certainly has the mettle to be able to deal with all of that and the expertise and the strength of his convictions to know how to go about doing his job really well."
• How Houston has banded together • Bills defense rolling since bye week • Why are the Colts sticking with Daniel Jones? • Falcons back in a familiar place • Freeling, Hunter top Panthers rookie report
Part of Pappas' responsibilities at the league level is to support all the fields at the 30 NFL stadiums. Each stadium has its own field crew responsible for the daily maintenance, but Pappas oversees compliance and testing and can be a resource for all the grounds crews when various situations arise.
He also handles all of the league events. So, Pappas' season started at the Hall of Fame Game in Canton, Ohio, on Aug. 6 and won't end until Super Bowl LXI in Los Angeles is over. He'll be in Los Angeles for a month before, preparing and maintaining the field for SoFi Stadium's second stint hosting the Super Bowl.
In all, out of the 24 weeks between the week of the Melbourne game and the Super Bowl, Pappas will have been on the road for 15 or 16 of them.
For about seven weeks, Pappas will be home, enjoying time with his kids and wife, relaxing, recovering and getting ready for another grueling stretch.
"His air miles are incredible," said Karl Standley, the head of grounds and surface transitions for Wembley Stadium in London. "Don't know how he does it. I really don't."
author: Josh Weinfuss

title: 49ers' Fred Warner will represent his heritage in Mexico City
summary: Warner will represent his heritage again Sunday in Mexico City while in the middle of his best campaign yet.
full_text:
MEXICO CITY -- Taken four years ago to the day, the photo still follows San Francisco 49ers linebacker Fred Warner just about anywhere he goes.
It was a brisk Mexico City night in 2022 when Warner -- clad in his white No. 54 jersey, gold pants and gold helmet -- burst out of the tunnel waving the red, white and green Mexican flag that represents a significant part of his heritage. The Niners were technically the visiting team against the Cardinals. But as the roar of the crowd enveloped him, Warner felt instantly at home.
Since that game, he has come across the image everywhere from autograph lines -- where fans hand him copies to sign -- to his childhood home, where his mother, Laura, keeps a blown-up print. For a player building a Hall of Fame résumé, that pregame sprint remains a defining memory.
His reaction every time he sees it? Goosebumps.
"I don't think I understood the magnitude of the moment," Warner told ESPN on Thursday, his 30th birthday. "Being in Mexico in front of the fans, really representing them and representing that part of me and my family was bigger than I even thought."
Watching from her home in San Diego in 2022, Laura Warner saw her son's arrival with the flag in hand as the ultimate public tribute to the roots her late father passed down to their family.
"I just got chills because it was just, to me, a big moment," Laura Warner said. "Because he was representing that heritage of our family in front of everyone."
Born Federico Anthony Warner on Nov. 19, 1996, in San Marcos, California, the ninth-year linebacker leads the 49ers back to Mexico City for a Sunday night showdown against the Minnesota Vikings (8:20 p.m. ET, NBC) in a game with major implications for the NFC's No. 1 seed . He describes his 2022 trip here as "electric." This time, he carries the weight of a historic pursuit -- becoming the fourth off-ball linebacker in NFL history to win Defensive Player of the Year -- along with the pride of his family's history.
Juan Quiroz, Warner's grandfather, was born in the small village of Arandas in Jalisco, Mexico, the oldest boy in a family of 11. He moved to the Los Angeles area at 16, where he met his future wife, Doris Quiroz. They married and had three children, including Laura.
Juan died in a car accident when Laura was only 7. So Fred, who has Mexican and French-Canadian roots on his mother's side and Panamanian and African American heritage from his father, never had the chance to meet his grandfather.
Yet Juan's influence lived on through the Spanish spoken and the Mexican food shared inside Warner's childhood home. He can still rattle off his favorite staples, from his grandmother's eggs and tortillas every morning to wet burritos and carne asada tacos for dinner -- traditions that Warner said made his Mexican background "a big part of our upbringing."
Warner visited Mexico this summer for the FIFA World Cup , where fans greeted him with so much love and adoration that his eyes still get big when he describes it. With a sharpened perspective on his ancestry, Warner embraces the responsibility that everything he does on the field serves both as a tribute to his family and as a blueprint for the next generation of Mexican diaspora who dreams of an NFL career.
"At the end of the day, if they can look at me and be like, 'If Fred's doing it, then I have a chance to do it,' why wouldn't I try to be the role model that they need me to be to serve in that way? I think that's more impactful than any sort of tackle or interception or anything I can do on the field," Warner said.
WARNER'S CONNECTION TO his roots, including the fighting spirit passed down from his grandfather, is woven directly into the way he plays. Nine games into this season, it has propelled Warner to the top of the list of DPOY candidates -- he currently has the fourth-best odds on DraftKings to win the award.
In the midst of a conversation with ESPN early last season about Warner's place among the game's best defenders, a trivia question came up: Which three off-ball linebackers have won the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year Award? Before the question was out, he rattled off the names: Ray Lewis (2000, 2003), Brian Urlacher (2005) and Luke Kuechly (2013).
The award generally goes to pass rushers or, as 49ers linebackers coach Johnny Holland called it, an honor for "the guy with the most sacks." While Warner has just half a sack, he's making the strongest case of his career to turn that trio into a quartet by leading the NFL in another stat: forced fumbles. He has five already -- an incorrect call in Dallas denied him a sixth -- and his 88 tackles rank sixth in the league.
"It's just the continual progression of my game where I'm not resting on anything I've done," said Warner, who has already surpassed his single-season high for forced fumbles. "It would be so easy four All-Pros in to just say 'I'm good' and keep doing the same things, but it's about finding ways to get better."
Since entering the league in 2018, Warner has always had the "Peanut Punch" -- named after former Bears cornerback Charles "Peanut" Tillman -- as an asset. It's why he has 22 forced fumbles in that span, fourth most in the NFL and most among off-ball linebackers.
Over time, Warner has worked hard to figure out the best way to knock the ball out while ensuring he still makes the tackle. He focuses on carrying his momentum through the ball carrier so even if he doesn't get the ball out, he makes the tackle.
Warner's grandmother might argue that his penchant for Peanut Punch perfection came from his grandfather. Juan had many interests, but among them was boxing. When Warner took up boxing as an offseason training activity a few years ago, it led to Doris speaking about Juan's boxing affinity.
"She's like, 'It runs in our blood,'" Warner said. "She always tells me I'm her Aztec Warrior."
Of course, Warner's improvement at punching the ball out wouldn't carry much weight were it not paired with his preparation. When watching film, he takes meticulous notes on everything from route combinations to running back and quarterback tendencies.
Warner says school "never really clicked" for him, but he has always had a near photographic memory for X's and O's. Still, he likes to take his homework a step further by digging deep into analytics for nuggets that can help.
Each week, Warner receives a scouting report stocked with spreadsheets on the opponent's personnel groupings, formations and how they deploy players out of each look. The reports are so detailed that Warner might recognize a certain personnel grouping lined up a specific way and know that offense is likely to run the ball between the right guard and right tackle.
Warner also studies recent trends, preferring to look at the opponent's past four games, and tries to put himself in the shoes of the offensive coordinator. For example: Has the run game been struggling or nonexistent and the coordinator said in the media that he wants to get it going? It all goes into Warner's planning.
This routine allows Warner to avoid "paralysis analysis," where he's spending so much time studying that he overthinks things. It also gives him total command of the defense on game days to the point that Dallas Cowboys offensive coordinator Klayton Adams said Warner is one of the only linebackers who makes adjustments for the secondary.
"Fred frees up everybody," 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris said. "He frees up me. Fred can make a call in a heartbeat. Fred can probably call the game without me talking to him in his ear. He's that kind of a guy. He's one of those guys you feel like you prepare with, not prepare for."
Warner's rare blend of sideline-to-sideline athleticism, football acumen and nose for the ball is precisely why, a year removed from a fractured and dislocated right ankle , he is forcing voters to rethink a DPOY ballot that has favored edge rushers and cornerbacks since Kuechly won the award in 2013. Nobody understands the…

title: Giants' Abdul Carter on lack of sacks: 'I've got to do more'
summary: On the surface, the lack of sacks and hard numbers seem insufficient, but dig deeper and it's a different story.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The traditional numbers say one thing on New York Giants edge rusher Abdul Carter . The advanced metrics say another. It has put Carter under the microscope about whether he's actually doing enough with the immense talent at his disposal.
Carter, the No. 3 overall pick out of Penn State in the 2025 NFL draft, has two sacks, three tackles for loss and eight quarterback hits this season. That ranks him tied for 99th, 156th and tied for 55th in those categories, respectively. Not exactly impressive.
"At the end of the day, I've got to do more, especially to get more sacks, get more production," Carter said. "But at the same time, as long as my main goal is focusing on winning."
On the surface, the lack of sacks and hard numbers seems insufficient. But dig deeper and a different story gets revealed. Carter has a 29.0% pass rush win rate, 16 forced incompletions, two interceptions created and 17 quick pressures (pressures in under 2.5 seconds). That ranks him second, first, tied for sixth and tied for eighth in those categories, respectively.
The advanced metrics depict a player making a significant impact, much like the coaches' tape.
"I don't go through all those stats and try to dig out every little metric on every guy. We get a general accounting of it," coach John Harbaugh said. "I definitely look at the team stats. But I'm looking at the tape. Myself, I'm grading every single guy. Plus, every coach is grading their position all the time. And he's grading out really well on my sheet, I can tell you that, and the coaches' sheet. He's a disruptive guy. I promise you they're accounting for him. And the sacks are just going to come."
Carter is getting double-teamed on a team-high 41% of opposing quarterback dropbacks. That indicates a level of respect.
But somewhere there seems to be a disconnect between the pressures/disruptive plays and sacks.
"I'm trying to figure that out," Carter said.
It doesn't help that opposing quarterbacks are getting the ball out in 2.70 seconds before the pass. Only the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have seen quarterbacks get the ball out quicker. The Giants also aren't known to have one of the better interior pass rushing groups.
So there aren't a lot of freebies for Carter and the edge rushing group. Fellow outside linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux is still looking for his first sack of the season.
The sacks are the most glaring omission from Carter's résumé. That's where pass rushers make their name and money. Carter has just six sacks in 26 games over his first two seasons.
It's not lost on the 23-year-old edge rusher. He's seen the critiques. Just the other day, he warned on social media that he's heard the noise and to watch out Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars .
Fast forward me to this Sunday💆🏾‍♂️⚔️ a lot of 🗣️ima show yall... https://t.co/KltZnE0DUC
Clearly, he's noticed the critics. And he's not backing down from the critiques.
"I hear everything," Carter told ESPN. "This is New York. This is not somewhere you can hide from the noise or block it out. So I embrace everything and I definitely use it as motivation."
It's commendable that Carter is not backing down from the challenge. That says something about his confidence, which appears to be undented. Carter, who tried to wear Lawrence Taylor's No. 56 upon his arrival in New York, told NJ.com this week he's still "going to be the greatest ever."
He knows that getting sacks is a big part of making that happen.
"I think it should be on my mind," Carter said of getting the quarterback on the ground.
He hasn't done it enough his first two seasons. New York Jets rookie David Bailey has more sacks (7.5) in one fewer year. Rookie inside linebacker Arvell Reese leads the Giants with 4.5 sacks this season.
Carter still needs more fine-tuning to his game to facilitate finishing plays. He's getting the quick pressures, but quarterbacks are getting the ball out quickly as a result. When he's not getting those immediate pressures, that is when it appears to be breaking down. There is no counter that is leading to sacks.
It doesn't seem to worry the Giants much.
"I believe the sacks will come," Harbaugh said. "There is no one answer. They're going to happen. Just go play football."
Former Giants linebacker and current radio host Carl Banks said recently on his podcast that it could benefit Carter if the Giants used him in games (twists, stunts and moving spots) to potentially get free runs at the quarterback. There haven't been many of those for Carter over the first nine games of this season.
The onus is on defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. His defenses have relied heavily on blitzes and Carter for most of their pressure this season. The Giants have blitzed at a 45.3% rate since Week 4, the second highest of any team.
"We're trying to put [Carter] in positions for him to get some touches on the quarterback, but he's doing everything he's supposed to do," Wilson said. "In the run game, he's been excellent. He's holding force. The ball isn't circling outside of him. So, I love where he's at. I just wish the production was a little bit more for him right now because he deserves it, especially the work that he's putting in."
While Carter's coaches are singing his praises, he knows it's going to take more to get the doubters on board. Two sacks in nine games isn't going to do it. Four sacks for the second straight season isn't going to impress any All-Pro or Pro Bowl voters.
The lack of traditional stats is notable. Even to Carter.
"It's definitely frustrating," he said. "But at the end of the day, it's not going to blind me from the main goal. And the main goal is to always going to be to win. But at the same time, I can always have that extra chip on my shoulder. I have to do more. I have to get more production. But I'm not going to chase. I'm not going to do something outside my job.
"As long as I'm doing everything to contribute to winning, I'll be all right. We just got to win. That's all."
author: Jordan Raanan

title: How Steelers' wide receiver corps gets big boost in Week 11
summary: DK Metcalf and the passing game are poised to get a lift this week with the return of Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr.
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf has never had a season like this .
A career-worst 7% drop rate. Catching a career-low 49.3% of his targets. Averaging, you guessed it, a career-low 48 yards per game and 12.3 yards per reception.
Amid the lows, though, the 28-year-old still made a handful of special plays. There was the 22-yard touchdown reception late in the loss to the Cincinnati Bengals and the 32-yard catch-and-run earlier in the game. There was also the 115-yard game against the Cleveland Browns in Week 4 and the 11-catch outing in the overtime win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6.
"This is the first time for real," Metcalf said of his struggles Thursday. "But I don't look at it as inconsistency. It's just new territory that I got to maneuver through. ... I've just got to block out the bulls--- y'all be talking about, basically."
Metcalf, who was acquired by the historically conservative organization in a blockbuster deal that included a second-round pick on the eve of 2025 free agency, was supposed to be a focal point of the offense. Instead, the mercurial wide receiver has been defined more by volatility than reliability, and this season, his 49.3% catch rate is second worst in the league out of 133 qualified players, per ESPN Research.
His teammates, though, have remained vocal in their support of him, and the coaching staff has shouldered some of the blame, saying it has to scheme up better opportunities for Metcalf.
"He's been up and down this season, and he's the first to admit that," tight end Pat Freiermuth said. "We need consistency out of him, but I've never worried about if his mind's in the right place or if he's willing to go out there and play. I think that obviously he's had some struggles, but him going out there -- and if you look at his effort on the run game or just downfield blocking, he doesn't let his situation impact his ability to get other guys open.
"That's something that you can appreciate as a teammate and as a guy, it tells a lot about his character, but we're with him till the end. He's going to get this figured out. We've got a lot of trust in DK and a lot of belief in him."
Compounding Metcalf's struggles this season has been the rash of wide receiver injuries.
But this week, Metcalf and the passing game, which averaged just 158.7 yards in the past three games, are poised to get a boost with the return of receivers Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr . Though neither has been officially activated from injured reserve, each is listed as questionable for Sunday's game in Philadelphia (1 p.m. ET, CBS) after fully participating in practices Thursday and Friday.
"Instead of having four receivers up, we'll probably have five or six," Metcalf said of the pair's impact. "So I mean a lot more rotation, a lot of fresh bodies. Just watching them out there at practice these past couple days, they look fresh, they look ready to go to me."
Both Pittman and Wilson were expected to be complementary players in the Steelers' offense this season, part of the core group of receivers along with rookie Germie Bernard and Metcalf.
But the Steelers have had their complete set of receivers for only three games this season, and Pittman was managing the foot injury that eventually landed him on injured reserve in two of those outings.
Pittman, acquired for a sixth-round pick earlier this year, hasn't contributed the way the Steelers envisioned. Added for his versatility and consistent production in Indianapolis, the veteran has just seven catches for 89 yards in three games this season.
"Just being out there when I'm needed, just those opportunities out there, just create plays, throw some nice blocks and play hard, just bring that physicality and just someone that the guys can depend on and just be there for any situation," Pittman said when asked how he can make a difference. "If it's a run-the-ball type game, hey, I'm in there to block safeties and linebackers, and if it's a pass game, then great. Get out there and let's catch some passes."
Pittman also added that his inclusion Sunday will depend on his ability to still move effectively on his foot.
• How Houston has banded together • Bills defense rolling since bye week • Why are the Colts sticking with Daniel Jones? • Falcons back in a familiar place • Freeling, Hunter top Panthers rookie report
"I don't want to go out there and hurt this team because I can't do something that I should be able to do," he said.
Wilson, meanwhile, was starting to become a dependable deep threat for quarterback Aaron Rodgers when he dislocated one finger and fractured another against the Colts in Week 5. Prior to the injury, he had six targets in each of the first four games and had a touchdown in back-to-back games for the first time in his three-year pro career.
"Obviously it's not ideal, but it's all part of the plan," Wilson said. "It's all part of the process. There's ups and downs. So as long as you just keep going forward, great things are going to happen."
And while Pittman and Wilson have the potential to give the offense its biggest boost, the Steelers could get help from an unexpected contributor: practice squad receiver Max Hurleman . A week ago, Rodgers brought up Hurleman's name unprompted as someone who could contribute, and earlier this week, he advocated for the 5-foot-11 former undrafted free agent, who spent three years of his collegiate career at Colgate, to make plays on special teams.
Like Wilson and Pittman, Hurleman was also sidelined with an undisclosed injury and rejoined the team earlier this week.
"Yeah, 'White Chocolate' is going to give y'all some plays, especially when he's out there on the field," Metcalf said last week, giving Hurleman a spur-of-the-moment nickname. "So I'm looking forward to him making his debut. He's been making plays ever since his rookie year last year, so definitely looking forward to him being out there."
author: Brooke Pryor

title: Jaylen Harrell allegedly assaulted rideshare driver before crash
summary: The Titans announced on Saturday that defensive end Jaylen Harrell was hospitalized in Tampa after a "serious car accident."
full_text: '' The Titans announced on Saturday that defensive end Jaylen Harrell was hospitalized in Tampa after a " serious car accident ." It doesn't sound like it was the usual car accident. Via WTSP, the Tampa Police Department said that Harrell was the passenger in a rideshare and that " he reportedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle was in motion ." The driver then swerved, hitting another car before colliding with a utility pole. The impact caused Harrell to be thrown forward, striking his head against the windshield and losing consciousness. Harrell was already on injured reserve. Per the Titans' statement, he remains hospitalized. Criminal charges are possible for Harrell, obviously. The WTSP story makes no mention of the condition of the driver.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyren Williams has a toe injury, is expected to be ready for Wednesday
summary: Another key offensive player for the Rams is dealing with an injury, but it is not expected to keep him from playing against the Packers on Thanksgiving Eve.
full_text: ' Another key offensive player for the Rams is dealing with an injury, but it is not expected to keep him from playing against the Packers on Thanksgiving Eve. Head coach Sean McVay said on Saturday that running back Kyren Williams has a toe injury. McVay said the team is not concerned about his availability for this week. Williams has run the ball 139 times for 616 yards and six touchdowns this season. He also has 38 catches for 267 yards and a touchdown, so he's played a significant role in both offensive phases this season. The Rams officially designated defensive tackle Kobie Turner and guard Justin Dedich for return from injured reserve Saturday. The team will issue its first Week 12 injury report on Sunday.
author: Josh Alper

title: CeeDee Lamb fined $23,882 for block the league used as a highlight
summary: Lamb was praised for the block by the league's website and by Tom Brady, but the disciplinary process said he used his helmet.
full_text: '' When Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb made a downfield block on a George Pickens touchdown catch Sunday against the 49ers, the league's website was so impressed that the highlight video on NFL.com emphasized Lamb's block over Pickens' touchdown. "Can't-Miss Play: CeeDee Lamb's HUGE block springs Pickens free for 39-yard TD," the caption on the highlight video says. Calling the play on Fox, Tom Brady praised Lamb, immediately recognizing it as a great downfield block. But the league's disciplinary process didn't think it was so great. Lamb has been fined $23,882 for what the NFL deemed "Unnecessary Roughness: Use of the helmet." Lamb confirmed to reporters on Thursday that he had been informed he was getting fined, but he insisted he didn't make contact with his helmet and found it frustrating that receivers take hits routinely but get fined when they make one. "I can block, and I'm real good at doing things like that, but I get fined," Lamb said. "I never touched him with my helmet. . . . I guess as a receiver, we can get hit, but can't deliver the punishment." Lamb will surely appeal the fine for what looked, both to the league's website and the league's all-time greatest player, like a good block.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bengals rule out Dalton Risner, list Dax Hill and Dylan Fairchild as questionable
summary: The Bengals may be without both of their starting guards on Monday night.
full_text: The Bengals may be without both of their starting guards on Monday night. Left guard Dylan Fairchild (oblique) was limited for two days before moving up to full participation Saturday. He's listed as questionable for Monday. Cornerback Dax Hill (illness) didn't practice all week, but a questionable tag leaves the door open for him to play. Linebacker Swayze Bozeman (forearm) and guard Brian Parker (knee) are listed as questionable to come off injured reserve. Wide receiver Andrei Iosivas (thumb) and cornerback Jalen Davis (hamstring) are also on injured reserve, but are listed as doubtful to return this week.

title: 49ers waive WR Brandin Cooks

full_text: ' The 49ers announced a couple of roster moves ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City. Veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks has been waived to make room on the active roster for defensive lineman C.J. West. West was activated from injured reserve on Saturday. Cooks had five catches for 58 yards and a touchdown in five appearances this season. The 49ers hope to have Mike Evans back after missing the last three games with an Achilles injury. title: Panthers activate CB Mike Jackson

full_text: Cornerback Mike Jackson declared himself ready to return to action earlier this week and the Panthers officially added him to the roster on Saturday. Jackson has been activated off of injured reserve after missing six games due to core muscle surgery. Jackson had six tackles while starting the first three games of the season for Carolina. The Panthers did not activate running back Jonathon Brooks or offensive lineman Brady Christensen, so they will remain on injured reserve for the time being. title: Lions place Cade Mays on injured reserve
summary: The Lions placed center Cade Mays on injured reserve for the second time this season on Saturday.
full_text: The Lions placed center Cade Mays on injured reserve for the second time this season on Saturday. Mays has missed the last two games with an ankle injury and he was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers ahead of Saturday's roster move. Mays fractured his wrist in training camp and Mays missed the first five games of the season as a result. Juice Scruggs has started at center when Mays has been out of the lineup this season. The Lions filled the empty roster spot by signing defensive back Nick Whiteside off of the practice squad. He's appeared in two games for the team this season. Linebacker Owen Pappoe was elevated from the practice squad to round out the day's moves.

title: Raiders owner Mark Davis hated the Madden movie
summary: Did anyone read the script before allowing the Raiders' name and logo to be used?
full_text: The new Madden movie includes a brief, fleeting glance of a young Mark Davis. The depiction wasn't flattering. His assessment of the film is far less flattering. The Raiders owner teed off on the Madden movie , in an interview with John Katsolimetes of the Las Vegas Review-Journal . “My comment is, it’s full of turducken," Davis said initially. Is that a good thing or a bad thing? “It depends on whether you like turducken or not, and obviously, I don’t like turducken," Davis said. His biggest concern was the script. “I think it’s really it’s unfair to take people that have passed away and make caricatures out of them, and try to sell it as truth,” Davis said. “They start the movie with a statement saying that all of it’s not true, but some of it is, so it’s confusing what to believe.” That's not an uncommon device. "Based on a true story" means that plenty of liberties will be taken in an effort to make the story more compelling. Mark Davis had one specific concern regarding the shading of the truth. He objected to his father's reaction to the serious neck injury suffered by Patriots receiver Darryl Stingley, during a preseason game in 1978. “So John goes over to the hospital afterwards, you know, and really looks after him," Mark Davis said, "and there’s a scene where my dad is telling John, ‘You don’t need to go over there. You don’t need to take care of other teams’ players. You take care of our players.' "That’s just so far from the truth. Anybody who has ever known him knows my dad always took care of people behind the scenes. If it was a player from another team had an issue that wasn’t being taken care of, my dad would quietly take care of that even if it was players on other teams. I’m serious. . . . It just it felt cheap to me to build up John’s image at the expense of my father’s.” Davis praised Christian Bale for his portrayal of Al Davis. “You can’t blame the script on him," Mark Davis said. "He tried.” Mark Davis also didn't care for the characterization of the iconic John Madden by Nicolas Cage. “You know, he at times did look like John, but he wasn’t John," Davis said. "I mean, they made John to be a pussy, and John was the farthest thing from a pussy.” The end result could be a positive. Mark Davis is now motivated to create something that properly and accurately depicts his father. “I don’t know what this movie’s purpose was, to be honest," Mark Davis said. "But you know, it’s making me more and more realize that I’m going to have to put together something on my dad. It could be a movie, it could be a characterization, but at least it’ll be truthful. . . . “I think I need to do that, or at least let people know that I’m thinking about doing that, so that don’t jump in and think that they can do it first.” The concerns expressed by Mark Davis regarding the script raise the question of whether he or the league or anyone bothered to review it before allowing the producers to use the Raiders name, colors, and logos in the filming of the football sequences. That's a critical aspect when it comes to the overall credibility of a film about pro football. If it looks real, it feels real. Unlike other films that didn't secure the ability to use actual team names and logos ( Any Given Sunday , The Replacements ). And that's the irony of this. Davis and the league allowed the Raiders name and uniforms to be included in the film, giving it the impression of accuracy and authenticity. Which, in turn, makes the story seem accurate and authentic. Which makes it even harder to separate the truth from the fiction. Here's hoping Mark Davis comes up with a way to tell the true story of Al Davis. With no embellishment, fabrication, or Hollywood tricks aimed at making the story seem better than it was. Because the story of Al Davis would be pretty damn compelling if it were indeed confined to the strict parameters of reality.
author: Mike Florio

title: Will Shane Steichen be back in 2027?
summary: After the 2025 season ended, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put both G.M.
full_text: '' After the 2025 season ended, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put both G.M. Chris Ballard and coach Shane Steichen on notice that much was expected in 2026. Then, one day after the Colts lost to the Titans in Week 6, she fired Ballard and kept Steichen. Nearly five weeks later, Steichen remains. After next Sunday's game against the Giants, the Colts will enter their bye. That's typically the best time for an in-season coaching change, since it gives the interim coach maximum time to get up to speed before the next game. Creating a vacancy with six weeks left in the regular season carries a separate benefit. The team can get a head start on searching for the replacement. And if ownership already knows the coach will be fired after the season ends, it makes no sense to delay that part of the process. So here's the question. Will Irsay-Gordon bring Steichen back in 2027? It makes no sense to keep a new G.M. from hiring a new coach. Every G.M. arrives with a wish list of coaches who would be pursued, if/when the position is vacant. It makes plenty of sense to give a new G.M. an immediate vacancy to fill. But what about the Colts this year has made sense? The firing of the G.M. left the team without a seasoned, experienced executive to navigate the strategy of making, or not making, trades. They quickly moved guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. They rejected offers for running back Jonathan Taylor and quarterback Daniel Jones. They moved two starting receivers — Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — on the day of the trade deadline. Now, they've abruptly released Jones. Steichen has been operating for much of the season with one hand tied behind his back. Now, he'll have both wrists secured. Whatever the decision will be as to Steichen, it's unfair to base it on the team's overall performance since the Nelson and Buckner trades. Before that point, they took the Chiefs to overtime in Kansas City. They beat the Texans. They manhandled the Commanders in London. They took the Vikings to the limit in Minnesota. Although the signs point to Steichen eventually being fired, the fact that he's still there now means he could still be there later. The new G.M. may be expected to work with him. It's ultimately the owner's call. And the owner may have strong feelings about Steichen's skills and abilities, based on the fact that she's on the sideline every week. If she was upstairs, she'd likely be hearing criticism of the head coach during the game. Instead, she's watching him in his element. And she hasn't fired him yet. Throw in the fact that a new coach may not be as welcoming to the owner's presence in the bench area, and she may be even more inclined to give Steichen (who's fine with it) another chance. Especially since she systematically began making his job much more difficult the moment the Colts traded Nelson and Buckner. Moving forward, it'll be virtually impossible. The fact that Steichen has survived this long could mean that he'll survive whatever comes next.
author: Mike Florio
