author: Charean Williams

title: NFL didn't know Puka Nacua had surgery when agreeing to suspension
summary: The sudden decision of the NFL to suspend receiver Puka Nacua three games raises plenty of relevant questions.
full_text: ' The sudden decision of the NFL to suspend receiver Puka Nacua three games raises plenty of relevant questions. On Friday, a technically irrelevant question was answered. After Rams coach Sean McVay disclosed to reporters that Nacua had surgery to repair a torn MCL suffered during a Week 9 win over the Commanders, Judy Battista of NFL Network reported this: "The NFL did not know Puka Nacua had had knee surgery on Tuesday when it suspended him yesterday." Surely, that's accurate; Judy is a solid reporter. But that extra fact doesn't matter to the NFL's ultimate handling of Nacua. The report creates the impression that, during the negotiations that resulted in the three-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy, Nacua and/or his representatives withheld material information. That, at some level, the league had been duped by the lack of knowledge that Nacua had undergone surgery that will sideline him for "a couple months." First, the suspension (as the league affirmatively explained on Thursday) is separate from the injury. The NFL listed multiple examples of players who served suspensions while injured. Second, whether Nacua (who had already missed one of the four minimum games he's required to miss while on IR), was already going to serve the entirety of the suspension while on injured reserve with or without surgery. Third, the surgery and the extended absence actually avoids the possibility that Nacua would have returned to action exactly one game after finishing his suspension, resulting in no net games missed due to the suspension. The mere existence of the report represents an implicit acknowledgement by the league that the negotiated suspension, aimed at allowing Nacua to double-dip when it comes to his stint on injured reserve and his suspension, underscores the broader question of whether players should be allowed to serve a suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy when otherwise unable to play. That's a separate issue for the NFL to revisit, if it chooses, through a potential revision to the terms of the policy. As explained on Friday, the league could have refused the deal. It could have insisted on pushing the issue through the full process, with Judge Sue L. Robinson conducting a hearing and the outcome potentially being appealed (by Nacua and/or the league) to the Commissioner. But that would have entailed a non-zero-percent chance that Nacua wouldn't have been suspended at all. For Nacua, the goal was to get the suspension served while injured. The fact that he had surgery before the agreement was reached gave him more of a buffer than the NFL knew about, expanding the window during which the suspension could be fully served before the end of the 2026 season without Nacua missing time due to the suspension. Which would still allow Nacua to have this issue behind him before the 2027 offseason, when he signs a new contract with the Rams, has the franchise tag applied, or becomes a free agent. Of course, Nacua now needs to tread lightly. The league has made it clear that "any further violation of the Personal Conduct Policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, will subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the League." To the extent that the league isn't thrilled by the perception/reality that it allowed Nacua to serve his suspension at a time when he otherwise could not play, the league could be ready to pounce on any opportunity to impose a longer suspension that would apply when Nacua is healthy again.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jerry Jones on fan's death after fight at 49ers-Cowboys game: "We had no record of an incident"
summary: This week, a fan died after falling during a fight at AT&T Stadium.
full_text: '' This week, a fan died after falling during a fight at AT&T Stadium. The fan was there to watch the 49ers-Cowboys game. On Friday, Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones was asked about the incident during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan. " I just got that information , and so we had no record of of an incident, and we'll be obviously looking into that," Jones said. "My understanding is that the individual went to the game and didn't feel good at the game, and then left, and [had] been hospitalized. But we weren't aware of any incident that involved a fan at the game." They know about it now, and they have the resources to fully investigate. "We really do have quite a — eons above what it was 10, 15 years ago," Jones said. "We have quite a surveillance of what's going on at every aspect of our game. And so it is really rare if we didn't know of any incident. We've got too many people out there. We have 6,000 workers on game day." Jones said he'll pass along any surveillance footage the Cowboys have to investigators. A full and complete investigation could potentially create liability for the venue. It all depends on the facts. And, frankly, it requires the authorities not to sit and wait for whatever is voluntarily provided but to use the subpoena power to go get anything and everything that will allow the complicated puzzle to be put together as to what happened to Marco Narro, whether it could have or should been prevented, and whether the aftermath could have or should have been handled differently.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals downgrade Carson Beck to out; Josh Johnson will start
summary: As expected, Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck won't be making his second career start on Sunday at Kansas City.
full_text: As expected, Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck won't be making his second career start on Sunday at Kansas City. Beck has been downgraded from questionable to out, due to back spasms. He'll be replaced by Josh Johnson, who will be making the 12th career start in a career that dates back to 2009. He'll be the fourth quarterback to start a game for the 3-7 Cardinals, joining Jacoby Brissett, Gardner Minshew, and Beck. title: 49ers WR Mike Evans is "set for his return" on Sunday
summary: Evans last played in Week 6, due to an Achilles injury.
full_text: After more than a month, 49ers receiver Mike Evans is on track to return to action. Via Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, Evans is set for his return on Sunday night, when the 49ers face the Vikings in Mexico City. Evans has been dealing with an Achilles injury. He left the Week 6 Monday night game against the Commanders, and he has not played since. He did not practice on Wednesday, and he was limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. On Friday, coach Kyle Shanahan was asked about the boost Evans's return will provide to the team. “I think a big one," Shanahan said. "Having Mike out there, everyone knows how good Mike is. I think the guys have done a good job holding it down with him not out there, but Mike's our guy and a very unique player and been doing it at a high level for a very long time. Played really unbelievable for the games he played in this year and it'd be great to get him back." Evans joined the 49ers in free agency, after 12 seasons with the Buccaneers. In six games with the 49ers, Evans has 27 catches for 420 yards and three touchdowns.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jaguars saw something in Liam Coen that other teams didn't
summary: The Jaguars identified Coen as their No. 1 candidate and re-shaped their front office to get him, at a time when other teams weren't even interviewing him.
full_text: ' In a season and a half with the Jaguars, Liam Coen has established himself as one of the best coaches in the NFL. Last year, Coen took over a team that had gone 4-13 the year before and improved their record to 13-4 — the best record ever for a first-year coach taking over a team that had won four or fewer games the year before. This year Coen is showing that last year was no fluke, with the Jaguars at 7-2 with an NFL-best point differential of +125. Coen's great success should have other teams that hired new head coaches in 2025 asking themselves: What did we miss? Because the Jaguars were so high on Coen that he was their No. 1 target and they were willing to do whatever it took to get him, while no other team even bothered to give Coen an interview. During the 2025 NFL coaching search , we tracked dozens of reports of head coaching interviews and requests among the seven teams that had vacancies. The Jaguars were the only team that so much as asked Coen to interview. This week there's been some media scrutiny on the Jets, who hired Aaron Glenn without considering Coen as a candidate. Glenn is 5-22; Coen is 20-6. But it's unfair to single out the Jets for failing to interview Coen, because no team other than the Jaguars did, either. The 41-year-old Coen had a résumé that should have made him a good candidate. NFL teams are always on the lookout for coaches who can nurture a franchise quarterback and run an innovative offense. Coen played quarterback at UMass and coached quarterbacks in college before getting hired by Sean McVay to work on the Rams' staff, eventually became the Rams' offensive coordinator under McVay, and had been a successful playcaller as offensive coordinator for the Buccaneers, as well as at Kentucky. With that background, it's surprising that only the Jaguars wanted him. And the Jaguars really wanted him, to the point that they were willing to do whatever it took to hire him. Coen initially turned the Jaguars down and agreed to a contract extension to stay with the Buccaneers, but Jaguars owner Shad Khan wouldn't take no for an answer. When Coen said he was concerned about the direction of the Jaguars' front office, Khan fired General Manager Trent Baalke and agreed to reshape the front office in a way that Coen would approve of if Coen would take the job. Coen was persuaded to take the Jaguars job, and the Jaguars later hired James Gladstone, who had worked with Coen on the Rams, as GM. The result has been the Jaguars going from one of the worst teams in the NFL to one of the best. Coen's success in Jacksonville has justified the faith Khan had in him. And raises questions about the total lack of interest from the rest of the league.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Tom Brady, after selling Birmingham City stake, buys piece of Chelsea
summary: Tom Brady's exit from the English soccer business was only temporary.
full_text: Tom Brady's exit from the English soccer business was only temporary. After selling his stake in Birmingham City, Brady has reportedly purchased a slice of the Chelsea soccer club, albeit indirectly. Via ESPN, Brady will become a minority investor in Clearlake Capital, the entity that controls Chelsea. Separate reporting from the Times characterizes the situation as Brady being " in talks " to take a "small minority stake" within the portion of Clearlake Capital that owns Chelsea. Brady, per the Times, also would become a member of the board of advisors. Whether that means he'll eventually be criticizing the work ethic of the team's manager remains to be seen. The end result is that Brady hasn't streamlined his overall portfolio in an effort to achieve more " balance " in his life. Instead, he's swapping out his piece of a second-tier club for interest in a member of the Premier League.

title: Daiyan Henley being out with a knee injury changes nothing about the failed trade to Broncos
summary: The failed trade of Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley returned to the front burner on Friday, with the news that Henley will miss Sunday's game against the Jets due to a knee injury.
full_text: The failed trade of Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley returned to the front burner on Friday, with the news that Henley will miss Sunday's game against the Jets due to a knee injury. It was a knee condition that prompted the Broncos to pull the plug on the deal — after trying to renegotiate the terms after the trade deadline. From Mike Klis of 9News, who covers the Broncos: "Chargers ILB Daiyan Henley missed entire week of practices with knee injury and has been ruled out for game vs Jets. This validates concerns raised by Broncos medical team and GM George Paton. And proves Chargers were not on the up and up ." Does it really prove that the Chargers weren't "on the up and up"? The issue is that the Denver physical flagged a knee problem. In lieu of finding that the physical had been failed and that the trade won't happen, the Broncos were willing to give Henley a passing grade, if the compensation was changed. Henley has played every game this season. He played on Monday night against the Ravens. As far as anyone knows, he injured the knee during that game. As far as anyone knows, the currently injured knee isn't the same knee that created the concern during the Denver physical. It's all just noise at this point. The core problem is the ability of a team — after the trade deadline has passed — to renegotiate the terms of a trade. And the related issue is the ability of a team to give a conditional grade on the pass-fail question of a physical that is tied to the specific compensation. A player either passes the physical, or he fails it. The process shouldn't include an epilogue premised on the outcome of the physical being "maybe." Especially after the time for negotiating trades has ended.
author: Mike Florio

title: Philadelphia mayor wants the Eagles to play in a dome
summary: The Eagles will become an indoor team if the mayor of Philadelphia gets her way.
full_text: The Eagles will become an indoor team if the mayor of Philadelphia gets her way. “ I want a dome ,” Mayor Charelle L. Parker said on 93.3 WMMR, via the Philadelphia Inquirer . “Don’t you tell. This is a secret between us. I just saw a rendering of this beautiful dome that they’re talking about for the Bears.” Moving into a dome would change the character of late-season and playoff games in Philadelphia, which are often affected by snow, wind and cold. Plenty of fans won't like it. But politicians and NFL owners often prefer stadiums with roofs because they bring in lucrative events, indoor sports, concerts, conventions and trade shows. The Eagles told season ticket holders last year that they are looking at either renovations to Lincoln Financial Field or a new stadium . Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie has committed only to staying in "the region," not in the city of Philadelphia, but both Parker and Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro have said they want the Eagles to remain in the city. The Eagles' lease at Lincoln Financial Field runs through the 2032 season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bud Dupree requests release from Chargers, who haven't granted it
summary: As the season continues to unfold — and as the trade deadline fades into the rear-view mirror — unhappy players have only one option: To request a release.
full_text: As the season continues to unfold — and as the trade deadline fades into the rear-view mirror — unhappy players have only one option: To request a release. Via Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, Chargers linebacker Bud Dupree has done that . The Chargers, however, have not granted the request. Dupree, per Fowler, also requested his release before the season. It's unknown whether the Chargers tried to trade him. His playing time has systematically dropped this year. He had no defensive snaps in two straight games before he was a healthy scratch in the Week 10 Monday night game against the Ravens. That move came three days after Dupree had some pointed comments for the front office. "Don’t ask hard questions to us; ask hard questions to them,” Dupree said. “Ask the hard questions. Everybody pull they cameras out and g o upstairs and ask questions to them. Everybody. Walk upstairs and ask them ." Dupree is under contract, so there's nothing he can do to force his way out. Still, the situation underscores the one-way nature of these deals. The team can cut the player whenever it wants. The player can't get out unless the team is willing to let him go.
author: Mike Florio

title: Nicolas Cage on his John Madden misfire: "I'm not Frank Caliendo"
summary: This whole thing is antithetical to my identity.
full_text: '' This whole thing is antithetical to my identity. That's the one line that resonates most strongly in the new Madden movie. Because it's exactly what John Madden would say if he saw it. It's bad. It's very bad. Anyone who says it's good has no taste and/or an agenda that involves the strategic application of lips to asses. The biggest problem is Nicolas Cage as John Madden. Anyone who vividly remembers the unique charisma of John Madden knows instantly that nothing about Cage's portrayal reflects the true nature, spirit, and demeanor of one of the most important and impactful figures in the entire history of the sport of football. Cage, who seems to realize that his portrayal missed not only the bull's-eye but also the entire wall on which the dart board was mounted, has defended the outcome by peering down his nose at the sports world. “ He was not on my radar ," Cage said of Madden, via Kirsten Chuba of the Hollywood Reporter . "I was growing up watching black-and-white Orson Welles movies and Fellini movies and Bruce Lee. I wasn’t interested in team sports whatsoever." And it shows. "I’m someone that likes to stay out of his comfort zone and take a risk, I said yes, because that would be a transformation,” Cage explained regarding the decision to attempt to play the towering, iconic figure. “It would be something where I might learn a few things, taking on this character who is really nothing like me.” The audience has learned that Cage's interpretation is nothing like Madden. “That’s what acting’s about," Cage said. "I’m not an impressionist, I’m not Frank Caliendo. I lean more towards being a surrealist, meaning I like to get a concept of a personality and then dig deep and see what I can locate emotionally with my imagination and my psyche and filter it through the cadence and the appearance, within reason, of John Madden. I’m trying to give you an evocation, more or less, or an interpretation.” The problem was it wasn't even "within reason." It was without reason. And the entire film was beyond unreasonable. And I like Nicolas Cage. He was brilliant in Moonstruck . He won an Oscar for Leaving Las Vegas . And The Family Man remains a highly underrated holiday film. Still, to quote another holiday film, "They can't all be winners." Cage's role in Madden as John Madden is not. I only met John Madden once. I watched him on TV for decades. I've heard plenty of stories about him from people who worked with him at NBC. And I'm confident that he would be livid about this film. "That's not me," he'd say. "Not even close." Or, perhaps, "This whole thing is antithetical to my identity."

title: Carmelo Anthony calls out Ravens' Marlon Humphrey after controversial Baltimore 'criminals' comment
summary: Anthony spent his formative years growing up in Baltimore and wasn't going to let Humphrey's comments slide
full_text:
Among sports fans, Carmelo Anthony is perhaps most synonymous with New York -- both upstate from his incredible year at Syracuse and in New York City, where he starred for the Knicks . But Anthony was raised in Baltimore and is extremely proud of his roots.
So when Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey made headlines this week when he said that the thing the city of Baltimore was best at creating was "criminals," Anthony felt compelled to respond. Humphrey was admonished by the Ravens, which sent him home for the week and will hold him out on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers. He also received scathing responses from Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott and many other prominent Baltimore figures.
Anthony joined that group on Friday with an Instagram post that called on Humphrey to go beyond the apology he issued earlier in the week. Anthony wants Humphrey to join him, Scott, and others in the community to find ways to lead by example.
I've been sitting with this one for a couple of days, because Baltimore isn't a talking point to me. It's in my blood. I came up on Myrtle Avenue in West Baltimore. I saw what this city can take fro you. I lost friends to the streets, and I watched people I loved get swallowed by a system that was built to swallow them. I know the reputation. I've heard every joke and every headline my whole life.
So when one of our own stands on our name and says the best thing Baltimore makes is criminals, and then laughs that it'll get cut out, that doesn't get cut out for me. It doesn't get cut out for the kid in Baltimore who heard it. It doesn't get cut out for the mother working two jobs to keep her son off the corner. And it doesn't get cut out for the man who did his time, came home, and is fighting every day to be seen as more than his worst moment.
Marlon, I see the apology. I'll take it, man to man. But Baltimore has been apologized to its whole life. Apologies don't build anything. Presence does. I put my time, energy and resources in Baltimore because I want kids to have somebody who believe in them. That's the job when you wear this city on your chest. You don't get to rep Baltimore on Sundays and talk about it like an outsider on Wednesday.
So let me tell you what Baltimore makes. We make fighters. We make builders. We make people who were counted out from the day they were born and showed up anyway. We make teachers who buy supplies out of their own pockets, coaches who become fathers, artists the whole world copies, and returning citizens who turn their pain into purpose. We make Olympians, Hall of Famers, legends. We make ME. We make Tank Davis.
The Mayor opened a door. Walk through it. And when you do, call me. I'll meet you there. Let's sit with these young boys together and let them hear from two men who wear this city that they are not what anybody says they are.
Baltimore doesn't make criminals. Baltimore makes the ones who make it out. And the ones who come back. #B-MORE.
The overwhelming response to Humphrey's comments in Baltimore has been to highlight the incredible work being done by leaders to improve conditions, decrease violence, and provide mentorship and guidance to young people in the city.
Anthony echoed the mayor's invitation to join in that work in the community and offered to be there right alongside him.
author: Robby Kalland

title: How to watch 49ers vs. Vikings in Mexico City: TV, streaming, betting odds for 'Sunday Night Football' clash
summary: The NFC-leading 49ers face the Vikings in a Mexico City duel at Estadio Azteca
full_text:
The biggest game of Week 11 -- and arguably the biggest game of the season so far -- goes down on "Sunday Night Football," when the San Francisco 49ers face the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City.
The 49ers (8-1) lead the NFC, while the Vikings (7-2) are tied for the conference's second-best record. Not only that, but it's a classic matchup of unstoppable force meeting immovable object.
Brock Purdy and the 49ers offense are coming off a 46-point performance in a win over the Cowboys and have been cooking all season. San Francisco leads the NFL in yards per game and yards per play and is third in offensive points scored per game. Purdy is having arguably his best season, and he leads the league with 9.0 yards per attempt.
But Brian Flores' defense could provide the toughest test yet. The Vikings' defense is second in yards allowed per game and yards allowed per play. Blitzing at the league's highest rate by far, Minnesota leads the NFL in pressure rate and sack rate by a wide margin.
The duel between Flores and Kyle Shanahan is the clear headliner here, but it's far from the only one. Looking at the Vikings' offense against the 49ers' defense, Kirk Cousins makes his second start for Minnesota after returning to the team at the trade deadline. Cousins threw a pair of touchdown passes in his first game back, a 30-10 Week 10 romp over the Packers , and he has looked as good as ever since his 2023 Achilles tear ended his first stint in Minnesota.
The San Francisco defense, meanwhile, doesn't garner the same headlines, but it ranks fourth in yards per play. Cousins and Justin Jefferson trying to crack one of the league's stiffest defenses will be key to this monster showdown, too.
It's also worth noting this game is being played at significant altitude. Here's how the 49ers and the Vikings are trying to adapt.
Date: Sunday, Oct. 25 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location : Estadio Azteca (Mexico City) TV: NBC | Stream: fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: 49ers -3 via DraftKings Sportsbook
How does Brock Purdy fare against pressure? Purdy has been outstanding against pressure this year, leading the NFL in completion percentage (58%) and ranking third in yards per attempt (8.5) in those situations. He has also thrown just one interception when pressured. But Flores' pressures aren't like normal pressures. The Vikings blitz on 72% of opponent dropbacks, by far the highest rate in the league, and when they get pressure, opponents average just 2.2 yards per play, the second-lowest rate in the league. In two games against Flores' defense, Purdy has thrown just two interceptions (compared to three picks) and has been sacked on nearly 10% of his dropbacks. Purdy is better than his past self, but the Vikings' defense is, too.
Will Mike Evans play? The 49ers have been without Evans ever since he left near halftime in Week 6 against the Commanders . The star wide receiver has been dealing with Achilles issues all season, but he's officially questionable for Sunday night, and Shanahan said, "he's going in the right direction." https://x.com/RapSheet/status/2123864564974460973 E SPN reported that Evans has "a real chance to go." If Evans does indeed play, it'd be a massive boost for San Francisco. In Evans' last full game, he had seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Seahawks , and his ability to win contested catches would be huge for Purdy against such an aggressive defense.
What can Kirk Cousins produce in his second game? Cousins completely changed the Vikings' offense -- both in terms of structure and results -- in Week 10. The Vikings' 30 points were their most since Week 1. Cousins converted several third-and-longs and gave Jefferson his healthiest workload of the season: nine catches on 13 targets. The 49ers do an excellent job limiting explosive plays, but Jefferson is an explosive play waiting to happen, and now he has a quarterback who can feed him.
This is a true best-vs.-best matchup, but perhaps the least talked-about unit will play the biggest role. The 49ers' defense is truly elite, and linebacker Fred Warner is making a legitimate Defensive Player of the Year case at a position that rarely wins the award. Purdy will make enough plays, even if the Vikings limit the San Francisco attack overall, and the 49ers emerge with a close win.
Pick: 49ers 20, Vikings 17

title: NFL week 11 anytime TD best bets: There's value on Mark Andrews and a Tony Pollard revenge game
summary: Tony Pollard faces his former team, Justin Jefferson reunites with Kirk Cousins on an international stage and Josh Downs makes his Chiefs home debut
full_text:
This week in the NFL , Fernando Mendoza makes his second career start against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense coming off a bye, the Jacksonville Jaguars will get tested by J.J. McCarthy and the New York Giants , while the Minnesota Vikings take on the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City in what could be the "Sunday Night Football" matchup of the year.
Let's discuss some anytime touchdown bets. These have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Below, we will break down five anytime TD bets to consider. These will not be predictable choices like a Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson score that offer zero value, but they won't be wild long shots such as a team defense. Let's begin with a veteran tight end.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
Mark Andrews was Jacoby Brissett's go-to target in his first start for the Baltimore Ravens . The tight end caught all eight of his targets for 82 yards against the Los Angeles Chargers . Those eight targets marked a season-high for Andrews, as did his 82 yards -- which led the team. This Carolina Panthers defense the Ravens are up against on Sunday allows 26.2 points per game, which is tied for 25th in the NFL. Carolina actually allows 38.5 points per game at home. I can see Andrews finding pay dirt during a red-zone trip.
It was fun to see the Kansas City Chiefs passing attack take off against the Atlanta Falcons last week. Patrick Mahomes threw for 348 yards and a whopping five touchdowns. We can't credit trade-deadline addition Josh Downs alone for this resurgence, but the former Colt did catch four passes for 53 yards and a touchdown.
This week, the Chiefs host the 3-7 Arizona Cardinals -- who are 16.5-point underdogs! The Cardinals are tied in having allowed the most passing touchdowns this season with 22. I'll take Downs to find the end zone in his first home game as a Chief.
Again, I hate paying a -130 price straight up, but this could be a parlay leg. Parlay it with the Over in this game! The Tennessee Titans and Dallas Cowboys statistically have the two worst defenses in the NFL.
Tony Pollard has rushed for 279 yards with 112 receiving yards and scored six total touchdowns over the past three games. He's been great, and now faces off against his former team, who allows more rushing yards per game (154.1) than any other club. Spotrac mentioned that Pollard is one rushing touchdown away from a $200K bonus. The former Cowboy scores on Sunday.
How about Chargers running back Omarion Hampton last week? He rushed 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown in L.A.'s first win of the season in Baltimore. Good things happened when he got the ball, which is something I think offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel realized. This week, the Chargers host the flailing New York Jets , who allow 135.3 rushing yards per game. That ranks third-worst in the NFL.
Justin Jefferson is surely excited that Kirk Cousins is back. He caught nine balls on 13 targets for 74 yards in the Week 10 win over the Green Bay Packers . Those nine receptions marked a season-high, and the 13 targets were the most he's seen in a game in two years.
The 49ers will surely be a tough test for this new-look Vikings offense, but Jefferson remains Cousins' go-to weapon. I'll take him to score and break out the "Griddy" in Mexico.

title: Don't sleep on these three NFL Week 11 games, from Joe Burrow's historic run to a rookie QB encore
summary: Joe Burrow's historic MVP push, Tampa Bay's dominant rushing attack and Fernando Mendoza's second NFL start highlight three overlooked Week 11 games worth watching
full_text:
It's Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season and there's no lack of storylines. This is our final week before the very busy Thanksgiving slate, and it will be make-or-break for many teams.
The playoff picture is starting to take shape, and while we have a lot more football left to play this season, teams are running out of time to make that postseason push as we inch towards the end of the season.
There are some clear must-watch games on the slate, but there are also some underrated games that fans should tune into. Here's a look at three under-the-radar matchups that you should keep up with this weekend:
This game could've made it on my list solely because it was a chance to watch Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow continue his MVP-level season. Throw in the fact that it's also a primetime game and an international game, and we have must-see TV.
Burrow is one of five QBs in NFL history with over 30 touchdowns through nine games, and the other four in the category- Tom Brady in 2007, Aaron Rodgers in 2011, Peyton Manning in 2013 and Patrick Mahomes in 2018- all won the MVP the year they hit the mark.
The Bengals quarterback is also one of just two quarterbacks (Manning) with five consecutive games with at least four touchdowns. Over this time, Burrow has 20 touchdowns in the air, two touchdowns on the ground and just three picks, with a 78% completion percentage.
Watching Burrow this season is watching history and any chance to watch him is a chance to watch the potential MVP.
At this point in the season, a team sitting at 3-6 probably wouldn't be discussed as a possible divisional winner, but the state of the NFC South makes this a different conversation. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are not that far off from the 4-5 Carolina Panthers , who lead the division. The Bucs have won two of their last three and their last two losses were only for a combined 10 points.
Tampa Bay leads the league in rushing yards per game (163.9), and if Baker Mayfield , who is dealing with a foot/ankle injury, is sidelined, the run game can still thrive. The Detroit Lions defense has a big hole to fill after star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL last week and will be out for the rest of the season. Detroit's run defense is strong, allowing just 90.4 yards per game, fifth-fewest in the league, so watching the battle between a strong run defense and a strong run game should make things interesting.
We are still very early in the Fernando Mendoza era, with his first NFL start coming last week in front of a home Las Vegas Raiders crowd. In his starter debut, the 2026 No. 1 overall pick gave us all a flashback to the National Championship game with a rushing touchdown on a designed draw. His big introduction to Raiders Nation wasn't perfect, going 17-of-29 (58.6 completion percentage), for 143 yards, no interceptions and no touchdowns in the air, against a solid Seattle Seahawks defense.
With those first-start jitters behind him and against an easier defense, it will be interesting to see how Mendoza does. The Broncos' defense has allowed the sixth-most yards per game (355.0), but the ninth-fewest points per game (20.7). They will still present a challenge for the rookie, given the pressure of a divisional game and the road trip to Mile High, a difficult place to play.
The Raiders sit at 4-6, but aren't too far outside of that playoff bubble, sitting two spots out at No. 9. Meanwhile, the 7-2 Broncos would be the No. 5 seed if the season ended today, still fighting with the 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs in a narrow divisional race.
The Broncos are favored, but divisional games tend to bring surprises, and with the added excitement of a new quarterback at the helm in Vegas, this should be an entertaining game.

title: Tom Brady says it's 'obvious' who the NFL's best quarterback is right now: 'Numbers don't lie'
summary: There is one QB who's playing at a higher level than any other QB in the league right now, according to Brady
full_text:
If you want to know who the best quarterback in the NFL is right now, there's no better person to ask than Tom Brady. After spending 23 seasons in the NFL and winning seven Super Bowls, Brady knows better than anyone what it takes to play the quarterback position at a high level, and right now, he says there is one QB in the league who is playing at a higher level than anyone else.
During a video for Fox Sports that was posted to social media this week , Brady was asked directly if Joe Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL right now and he gave a simple answer.
"Numbers don't lie," Brady said. "It seems pretty obvious this week."
After watching Burrow and the Bengals beat up on some bad teams over the past few weeks, it seems that Brady finally jumped on board the Burrow hype train after watching the QB throw for 409 yards and four touchdowns in a 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in a battle for first place in the AFC North on Sunday night.
"Last week, I said Cincinnati needed a signature win, that's not the case anymore," Brady said. "They handled Pittsburgh by 20 on a huge stage, and it was basically over by halftime. Joe Burrow threw four touchdowns without a pick, and that's five straight wins, scoring 30 or more."
The Bengals offense has been on fire since Week 4, scoring at least 31 points in five straight games, which is a franchise record. If Burrow can total at least four touchdowns against the Washington Commanders on Monday night, he'll become the first quarterback in NFL history to hit the four-touchdown mark in six straight games. To put that in perspective, Brady never had a span in his career where he totaled four touchdowns in even five straight games.
During the Bengals' five-game winning streak, Burrow has thrown 20 touchdown passes, making him just the third QB ever to reach that mark in a five-game span, joining Brady (2007) and Peyton Manning, who did it twice (2004, 2013).
For the season, Burrow has been so good that he leads the NFL in multiple passing categories. If you're wondering just how dominant he's been, here's a short breakdown:
To give you an idea of how incredible his passing yardage number is, just consider this: No other QB is even averaging 285 yards per game. Also, he has five more TD passes than the next closest player, and his completion percentage is so high that he might actually break the NFL single-season record of 74.4%, which was set by Drew Brees in 2019.
Burrow is currently a heavy favorite to win his first MVP award, with odds of -125 (the next-closest player is Josh Allen at +370).
As Brady said, "Numbers don't lie," and that's why he thinks Burrow is the best QB in the NFL right now.

title: 49ers lose shot at breaking NFL record for most miles traveled due to Week 11 travel detour en route to Mexico
summary: The 49ers are taking a detour in Week 11 that's going to cost them the NFL record for most miles traveled
full_text:
With a trip to Australia in Week 1 and a trip to Mexico City in Week 11, the expectation before the season started was that the 49ers were going to break the NFL record for most miles traveled this season , but that's actually not going to happen due to a travel detour that the team is taking this week.
After beating the Cowboys in Week 10, the 49ers didn't fly home to California. Instead, they took a flight to Colorado, where they spent the week getting acclimated to the high altitude in Mexico City, which sits at an elevation of 7,350 feet.
The 49ers' decision to head to Colorado will reduce the total number of miles the team travels this year.
If the 49ers had flown home after their game against the Cowboys, they would have traveled a total of 2,876 miles round trip. After that, their round-trip flight to Mexico City would have covered 3,702 miles for a two-week total of 6,578 miles.
However, since the 49ers didn't fly home after playing the Cowboys, that will lead to a drastic change in their mileage total. Here's what their Week 10 to Week 11 travel will look like (the 49ers fly out of San Jose):
Total for all four: 5,257 miles
The decision to practice in Colorado this week will cut their total travel by 1,321 miles this year, trimming their season total from 38,105 miles to 36,784. At that number, they won't set the NFL's mileage record.
The Los Angeles Chargers set the record for most travel miles last season when they flew 37,086 miles , and that record will stand for at least another year thanks to the 49ers' decision to take a pit stop in Colorado before heading to Mexico City in Week 11.
That being said, the 49ers will be setting one NFL record when they take the field on Sunday: They'll become the first team in NFL history to play two international games in two different countries in non-consecutive weeks. The Vikings played in Ireland and England last season, but that came in back-to-back weeks. The 49ers' two international trips are coming 10 weeks apart.

title: Colts waive Daniel Jones: Indy not trading QB or Jonathan Taylor at deadline now a major second-guess
summary: Indy has put themselves in a very tough spot after sitting on the fence at the deadline.
full_text:
Mobb Deep said it best: "Ain't no such thing as halfway crooks."
The Indianapolis Colts tried to sit on the fence at the 2026 trade deadline, ship away some (not all) expendable pieces, and land a somewhat respectable, middle-of-the-road record that might save a few jobs in the process. That meant moving on from the likes of DeForest Buckner , Quenton Nelson , and Josh Downs , but holding on to Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones . Less than two weeks removed from that semi-fire sale, it's safe to say Indy botched it.
What's the old saying? If you're going to be a bear, be a grizzly. Well, if the Colts felt alright selling some pieces at the deadline, they should've stripped it down to the studs, knowing full well they are entering a rebuild anyway after firing GM Chris Ballard in mid-October.
The losses have only continued to pile up for the Colts, which includes a demoralizing defeat at the hands of the Houston Texans in Week 11. That game, which dropped them to 3-8, proved to be the straw that broke the camel's back for the Daniel Jones era, as the team has since waived the veteran quarterback.
Again, this is a player who teams were reportedly interested in leading up to the deadline. Instead of pursuing those opportunities to shed a sunk-cost under center, ESPN reports that Indy rebuffed trade interest from teams like the Minnesota Vikings and Baltimore Ravens .
As a reminder, the Vikings traded a 2027 third-round pick to acquire Kirk Cousins , while the Ravens shipped a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Cardinals in exchange for Jacoby Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick. It's unclear what the compensation for Jones would've been, but I can tell you this—it's more than what they have now after waiving him: nothing.
In the nine games before the deadline, Jones had the Colts at 2-7 while completing 60.3% of his passes, averaging just 191.3 passing yards per game, and posting a passer rating of 68.9. In total, Jones had tallied seven touchdowns and 13 turnovers.
It was abundantly clear in the lead-up to the deadline that the two-year, $88 million extension the Colts signed Jones this offseason to was a disaster. Miraculously, a lifeboat drifted by them in the form of multiple teams inquiring about taking that burden off their hands, but they decided to stay on the deserted island. Now they're paying the price , with Jones set to account for $35.2 million in dead cap space for 2027 (provided he clears waivers) while the team pays him $49.8 million for 11 games played this season.
On top of Jones, Taylor, arguably the most sought-after prize on the trade market this cycle, should've been firmly on the block. With the Colts now without a clear answer at quarterback, Taylor is the living embodiment of that meme where the Lamborghini is sitting in the driveway of the trailer park.
He was most valuable to Indy as a trade chip at the deadline, and that remains the case this offseason. The only difference is that any team acquiring him is getting a back that's a little older, has a little more mileage, and doesn't help them for this stretch run in 2026. That sets up a possibly diminished return this offseason if/when the Colts deal him compared to what they could've gotten at this deadline.
For a team that won't have its first-round pick in 2027 after trading for Sauce Gardner at last year's deadline, they were in a position to refill the cupboard. Neither Jones nor Taylor likely would've fetched a first-rounder, but they would've given Indy premium ammunition for a later deal that could vault them back up. That level of asset mismanagement around the deadline now has the potential to ripple beyond just this second half of the season.
Jones being waived is just one of the initial steps that the Colts will take as they embark on this rebuild and they tripped out of the gate. Whether it's firing Shane Steichen, trading Taylor, or eventually hiring a new GM (if they can find a taker), the organization needs to have a more definitive and realistic plan for its future so they're not looking back with major second guesses like they currently are following this deadline.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Cardinals turn to Josh Johnson — fourth starting QB in four weeks — with Carson Beck (back) sidelined
summary: Johnson will make his season debut vs. Chiefs, the eighth team he's taken regular-season snaps for.
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals will use their fourth starting quarterback in four weeks on Sunday, turning to journeyman veteran Josh Johnson against the Kansas City Chiefs . Carson Beck , the third-round rookie who started last week against the Los Angeles Rams , is dealing with back spasms and was ruled out Saturday .
"There is no next step to the playbook; this is going back to the starting table of contents, and that's OK," coach Mike LaFleur said . "For a three-and-a-half-hour window, it's my job to figure out, as you know, whatever we can to get the ball moving forward."
Joey Aguilar , signed off the Jaguars ' practice squad, will be the backup. Aguilar, an undrafted rookie, has yet to see regular-season snaps.
Arizona has endured a revolving door of quarterbacks this season. The season started with Jacoby Brissett as the starter, but he was benched midway through Week 8. Gardner Minshew took over and led the Cardinals to a win over the Cowboys , claiming the starting role in the process. Brissett was demoted to QB3 and, shortly thereafter, traded to the Baltimore Ravens .
In his first start, though, Minshew tore his UCL , an injury that required surgery.
That led to Beck, the No. 65 overall pick out of Miami, taking the reins . He played just one game before landing on the injury report with a back issue, though.
Johnson is on his 15th team (including practice squad and offseason stints) in 14 seasons. He joined Arizona after Minshew went down with the injury, and the Cardinals signed him off the Cincinnati Bengals practice squad. The 40-year-old was selected by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the fifth round of the 2008 NFL Draft and has bounced around the league ever since, including time in the UFL, AAF, and XFL. The Cardinals will be the eighth team he has played for in the regular season. He appeared in five games for the Washington Commanders last year, finishing 1-1 in the games he started.
Johnson will be the second-oldest quarterback to start a game this season, behind 43-year-old Aaron Rodgers .

Now, the pass catchers are backups to backups, while the QB room is down to two rookies and a guy who is being paid by his 17th NFL club. This weekend as the Arizona Cardinals are preparing to play the Kansas City Chiefs, one of the best teams in the AFC, the coaching staff just might be starting its fourth quarterback this season. Rookie Carson Beck may not start. RELATED: SHOULD THE CARDINALS MAKE A CLAIM FOR QB DANIEL JONES? Beck started his first NFL contest last week in the 34-6 beatdown from division foe Los Angeles Rams. He was scheduled to start again this weekend as center Hjalte Froholdt has been released from concussion protocol. Mike LaFleur: QB Carson Beck had his back spasms flare up. Will proceed as if Josh Johnson will start on Sunday. But won’t close door on Beck just yet. — Darren Urban (@Cardschatter) November 20, 2026 But Beck has had some flare-ups with back spasms. Although the team hasn’t ruled Beck out for the Chiefs game, journeyman Josh Johnson is being prepped to start instead. If Johnson does play, that will become four starting quarterbacks in four games. What a QB turnstile. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur stated that the team is taking Beck’s situation one minute at a time, which made it sound serious since he avoided the classic “one day at a time” standard answer. Beck did not participate in practice on Friday while the coaching staff is waiting to see how the young signalcaller responds to treatment. The rookie QB was previously sidelined with back spasms earlier in the season. LaFleur added: “We’re not gonna shut the door on him, but we’re gonna proceed as if Josh [Johnson] is gonna be starting on Sunday.” Beck was taken in Round 3 of this year’s NFL draft and basically was the emergency quarterback for the majority of the year. Then Jacoby Brissett was shipped off, and suddenly Beck was the backup to Gardner Minshew against the Seattle Seahawks. Minshew became injured in that game and then was placed on IR after surgery to repair his () in his throwing arm. Which meant, the next man up. Beck started against the Rams as the Cardinals offensive line did not provide much protection and sacked Beck five times, which could just as easily been double digit numbers. Beck finished going 11 for 18 for 108 yards and two picks, of which one was the receiver’s fault. Johnson is 40-years old. He was a fifth-round selection of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers way back in 2008. The Cardinals are his 17th NFL team. He has played for three clubs twice, plus was a roster member of an UFL team, an AAF franchise, and the XFL where he was the passer rating leader. He played in five games for Washington in 2025 with two starts. Beck was seven years old when Johnson was drafted by Tampa Bay. Johnson has always been the backup, or the backup to the backup. He has played in just 50 NFL games with a mere 11 starts. His total career passing yards is 2,669, what most starters eclipse in a single season. Johnson has a career 58.7% completion ratio with 94 rushing attempts for 481 yards, so he is mobile. I get not throwing him to wolves in this game. Fans would lose interest in watching him play the rest of the year, even with a flawed roster. But back spasms, excuses or not, doesn’t inspire fans support for organization or player. — AZJones (@BrettJonesing) November 21, 2026 Which means he has experience. If Beck can’t go, rookie Joey Aguilar will become the backup with WR/KR Devin Duvernay the emergency QB.

title: The Colts cut QB Daniel Jones. Should the Cardinals make a claim?
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are one of the league’s worst teams this year. Another bad team, the Indianapolis Colts just released their starting quarterback, Daniel Jones. Should the Cardinals make a waiver wire claim? Before Jones was released, he had trade value. The waiver wire is situated where the worst team has the first dibs, then […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts throws a pass against the Houston Texans during the first quarter of the game at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are one of the league’s worst teams this year. Another bad team, the Indianapolis Colts just released their starting quarterback, Daniel Jones. Should the Cardinals make a waiver wire claim? Before Jones was released, he had trade value. The waiver wire is situated where the worst team has the first dibs, then the second worst, and so on. RELATED: CARDINALS DRAFT PICKS HAVE FAILED TO MAKE AN IMPACT The current order is: 1 Tennessee Titans (1-8-0) 2 Los Angeles Chargers (1-8-0) 3 Miami Dolphins (1-8-0) 4 New York Jets (2-8-0) 5 Philadelphia Eagles (2-7-0) 6 Indianapolis Colts (3-8-0) 7 Arizona Cardinals (3-7-0) 8 Atlanta Falcons (3-7-0) This means that the Cardinals are seventh in line. The Titans drafted Cam Ward last year, the Chargers have Justin Herbert, Miami spent big bucks on Malik Willis in last year’s free agency period, and Geno Smith for the Jets is back into the fold. The big question might be for Arizona is if they grabbed Jones off waivers, would he become the default starter or just another stallion in the QB stable? Would he play, or sit until Carson Beck becomes injured, frustrated, or incapable of assuming the starting role? While with the Colts, Jones was under a two-year $88 million deal. Here is the QB status of each team: Titans: Ward is doing okay considering the offensive line is weak. The team has a capable backup in Mitch Trubisky. Chargers: LA got their first win with Herbert still under center. His backup, Trey Lance, is on IR which means QB3 D.J. Uiagalelei is now Herbert’s backup. Dolphins: Willis is on IR with Kyle McCord starting and Brady Cook his backup. Jets: Starter Geno Smith has just returned from IR. Rookie Cade Klubnik is his backup. Eagles: We are all aware that starter Jalen Hurts is on IR and gone for the year. In his place is Joe Milton who isn’t exactly tearing up the league. Tanner McKee and Cole Payton are backups. With the Colts picking at #6, they are out. The Titans look good along with the Jets. But the remainder could use Jones. So could Arizona. Jones was taken with the sixth overall selection in the 2019 NFL Draft by the New York Football Giants after a standout career at Duke. He was supposed to be the future after Eli Manning retired. In 2022, Jones made NFL history by becoming the first player ever with 300+ passing yards, 2+ touchdown passes, and 70+ rushing yards in a playoff game. The next year, Jones inked a four-year $160 million extension, but had a knee injury in Week 9. Late in 2024, he was benched for undrafted Tommy DeVito who set the New York area on fire as an Italian-American quarterback who was winning games and his downhome attitude. In late November, the Giants shocked everyone by releasing Jones. He spent one season with the Minnesota Vikings before hooking on with the Colts in 2025 who signed him to a one-year $14 million deal and competed with Anthony Richardson for the starting role. Jones tore his Achilles tendon late in the season and landed on IR. +2 for the Terminator 😤 📺: @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/TzcavjrlrF — Houston Texans (@HoustonTexans) November 20, 2026 This season, he was named the starter for Week 1. Jones started all 11 games for a listless offensive unit which has been selling off their key players. Their offensive line is absolutely porous. This year, Jones hasn’t had any time to throw and has paltry production such as 144 (twice) yards, 108 (twice), 143, and 166 in games. He has thrown seven touchdowns against 13 interceptions. For his eight-year career, Jones’ stats: 94 games with 93 starts, 1,903 completions on 2,976 attempts for 19,657 yards, converted 979 first downs, 96 TDs, 68 picks, a 63.9% completion ratio, sacked 257 times, an 84.1 QB rating, and a 35-57-1 starting win-loss record. He is a very good runner with 478 carries for 2,441 yards with another 21 scores. Gooooooould 💨 📺 Prime pic.twitter.com/YmZXB3NfsN — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 20, 2026 Thursday night, the Colts lost to the then-3-6-0 Houston Texans 26-3 in a totally lopsided contest. Indy had 38 rushing yards while Jones went 12 for 27 for 144 yards, sacked twice and had a single pick with zero TDs. The Colts’ offense is ranked #30 in the league. They have allowed the eighth most sacks (28) and thrown the most interceptions with 13. Despite losing one of the best offensive guards in the league by trading away LG Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks before the trade deadline, the Indianapolis offensive line is ranked #17. By claiming Jones, it could mean the Cardinals would have a capable quarterback for their remaining games this season who would compete with Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck in training camp next year. Then again, what would be the cost to bring him in? None of the four quarterbacks on the roster are costing the franchise hardly anything.

title: Brandon Dorlus, DeMarcco Hellams, Harold Perkins fined for plays in Falcons vs. Chiefs Week 10
summary: The Falcons racked up nine penalties in last week’s lackluster loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, but they were all procedural — there weren’t any flags for actions that typically lead to fines. But that didn’t stop the NFL from issuing four fines total to three different defensive players stemming from last Sunday’s action. Defensive […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images The Falcons racked up nine penalties in last week’s lackluster loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, but they were all procedural — there weren’t any flags for actions that typically lead to fines. But that didn’t stop the NFL from issuing four fines total to three different defensive players stemming from last Sunday’s action. Defensive lineman Brandon Dorlus was the lucky guy who got hit with two fines, each for $7,114. One was for unsportsmanlike conduct/taunting, and one was for a late hit on a quarterback. DeMarcco Hellams, who slid into the starting spot opened up by the Falcons’ decision to trade Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars before the NFL’s deadline, owes the NFL $6,509 for unnecessary roughness/a hit on a defenseless player, and linebacker Harold Perkins was also fined $5,203 for unnecessary roughness/use of the helmet. The NFL splits the fine money it collects from players between the NFL Foundation to support the health, safety and wellness of athletes at all levels of football and the Professional Athletes Foundation to support NFL Legends in need. title: Ravens’ 2026 season has come to a crashing halt
summary: It took just one play. As optimistically as it began, the 2026 Ravens season is all but finished. On the first day of November, on his first snap back from a high-ankle sprain, Lamar Jackson injured his right thumb when his throwing hand struck the wrist of Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau. Jackson knew something […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Trainers attend to Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens kneels after getting hurt on the first play of the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images It took just one play. As optimistically as it began, the 2026 Ravens season is all but finished. On the first day of November, on his first snap back from a high-ankle sprain, Lamar Jackson injured his right thumb when his throwing hand struck the wrist of Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau. Jackson knew something was wrong immediately, sprinting straight to the sideline and then to the locker room. The two-time MVP has since had surgery on his thumb with a late-season return technically in play – if it even matters. At this point, Jackson is the Baltimore Ravens, and his contract reflects that. Many want to bash the supporting cast, the coaches and the front office, but it just isn’t realistic for a team paying a star quarterback that much to also have stars at every other position. What did the Chiefs look like without Patrick Mahomes last year? What did the Bengals look like without Joe Burrow? What would the Bills look like without Josh Allen? On top of losing Jackson, the Ravens have suffered a rash of injuries elsewhere, primarily on the offensive line. A position group that typically thrives on continuity is operating with a new offensive coordinator, a new offensive line coach, and a rotating door of new starters. This year, the unit has had five different centers and four different right guards. Has the offensive line been good enough? No. But we never got to see the vision. Heck, we never even got to see Jackson and Zay Flowers play a full game together. The full extent of the Ravens’ woes came to a head five days after the Jacksonville Jaguars. With undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano making his first start, the Ravens were once again trounced at home, this time in a downpour. We all expected the offense to struggle, and predictably, it did. But once again, the defense let the dam break. Is that partly a product of the offense’s struggles? Probably. Still, it looked more like a group of unmotivated, aging players struggling to adjust to a new defensive system. Marlon Humphrey and Malaki Starks were both burned for big plays, and the middle of the field — an area that has plagued this defense for years — was wide open all night for Trevor Lawrence. And yet, Monday night’s loss to the Chargers might have been worse. Jacoby Brissett performed admirable in his Ravens debut, but an anemic running game and a defense that once again could not tackle gifted a winless team their first victory. Unfortunately, the near future doesn’t look much brighter, largely because of some questionable decisions by the front office. The Ravens’ so-called “star” veterans by salary have underperformed this year. Marlon Humphrey, Roquan Smith, Ronnie Stanley, Mark Andrews and John Simpson make up more than 25% of the Ravens’ salary cap. That’s not a winning formula. It’s easy to engage in revisionist history on contracts. Humphrey signed his extension in 2020 and Smith signed his in early 2023. Since then, both have followed the natural arc of an NFL second contract: some very good years, and now the back end of their careers. Humphrey was an All-Pro in 2024, and Smith was an All-Pro in 2022 and 2023. Their decline isn’t surprising. What’s surprising is that the Ravens have forgotten one of Ozzie Newsome’s favorite phrases: ‘better to move on from a player a year too early rather than a year too late.’ It might be two years late for Humphrey now. Smith’s decision point should be this offseason. His oversized contract is arguably worse. Fred Warner is probably the only middle linebacker in the NFL worth that kind of money. Humphrey has virtually seen himself out the door in the last week; if the Ravens are committed to change, Smith should be gone this offseason, too. Now let’s talk about Mark Andrews. In my opinion, re-signing him was the worst contract DeCosta has ever handed out. Andrews has been terrible. So bad that he’s actively hurting the team. From 2019 to 2025, the Ravens consistently had one of the best tight end rooms in the league. Now it’s one of the worst. Meanwhile, as many of us suspected he would, Isaiah Likely is looking like one of the best tight ends in football. For his entire tenure in Baltimore, we assumed he’d be Andrews’ successor. That said, I don’t think it’s fair to claim the Ravens have simply punted on the trenches. On defense, Trey Hendrickson, Nnamdi Madubuike and Travis Jones all got paid. On the offensive line, the Ravens re-signed Ronnie Stanley, traded picks for center Cam Jurgens, spent their 2026 first-round pick on a guard and drafted Roger Rosengarten in the second round. The problem is that those players aren’t playing up to their price. Stanley and Rosengarten are both playing like average tackles. On the interior, Jurgens has been fine, but he hasn’t looked like he is worth a second-round pick. John Simpson hasn’t been much better than what the Ravens had at guard last year, though he’s dealt with a groin injury for most of the season. The Ravens trust their development process to a fault. Sometimes it’s paid off, but there have been far too many instances where it hasn’t, especially on the offensive line. Emery Jones Jr., Andrew Vorhees and Daniel Faalele have been abject developmental failures. Some of it is just bad luck. Ronnie Stanley was one of the best tackles in the NFL before his gruesome ankle injury. Since then, he’s played just well enough to earn another contract. But that’s the issue: the Ravens have been fine with “just good enough.” Rather than proactively building a dominant offensive line, they’ve settled for adequate. Look at the elite teams in the NFL right now. The Bills, 49ers, Lions, Bears, Broncos and even the Steelers all have top offensive lines. Obviously, if it were that easy, every team would do it. But when you have a superstar quarterback, protecting him is paramount. In a way, the 2024 season did them in. Despite two below-average guards, the Ravens put together a record-setting offense, so naturally, DeCosta thought it prudent to run it back. Let’s face it: when Jackson is healthy, the Ravens have typically had great offenses regardless of who’s blocking for him. Even this year, the Ravens ranked second in EPA per play with Jackson and this current group.The downside is that when Jackson is injured or hobbled, the team falls apart because the line can’t impose its will on opponents. If the Ravens are serious about building a championship team, they need to pour as many resources as possible into the trenches. Teams don’t fear playing the Ravens anymore because they’ve become largely a finesse team, with undersized corners, offensive linemen, linebackers and receivers. As a result, they can’t salt away games like they used to. In the second half, when opponents know the run is coming, the Ravens get shut down. Their status as one of the league’s worst short-yardage teams reflects that.In the early stages of the Lamar Jackson era, the major question was whether the Ravens could play from behind. They were that good at putting opponents away. Now it’s the opposite. DeCosta also has a habit of overcorrecting for past problems. The Ravens struggled to draft and develop receivers, so he spent multiple first-round picks trying to find one instead of trading for an established star, the way the team did with Anquan Boldin. The Ravens went through a few years where they couldn’t keep cornerbacks healthy, so he overcorrected again, spending pick after pick on corners to make sure it wouldn’t happen again. The better approach: trade for stars at the positions you’ve historically failed to develop. DeCosta also has a habit of being too loyal to his players. In one of his first press conferences as…

title: 3 Keys to Victory for Ravens-Panthers in Week 11
summary: This is it. You can’t finish with a record of 11-6 until you first reach 5-6. Technically, the Ravens could make the playoffs with seven or eight losses — but this feels like a defining moment. With the Houston Texans on the rise, Tampa Bay’s roster built perfectly to beat the Ravens, and then four […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Mike Green #15 of the Baltimore Ravens celebrates during an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images This is it. You can’t finish with a record of 11-6 until you first reach 5-6. Technically, the Ravens could make the playoffs with seven or eight losses — but this feels like a defining moment. With the Houston Texans on the rise, Tampa Bay’s roster built perfectly to beat the Ravens, and then four division games in a row, this game against Carolina feels like the easiest one remaining on the schedule. If the Ravens lose, any little fleeting hope for a run will fizzle. It’s been a drama-filled week for the Ravens, and they’ll be missing Nnamdi Madubuike, so they need to figure out how to put their heads down and grind out this win to avoid dropping six in a row. Find the formation that works The Ravens have run multiple tight end sets at the seventh-highest rate this year, 43.6% of the time, according to Next Gen Stats. They are largely successful throwing out of these sets as well, averaging 8.1 yards per pass attempt, which is 12th-most in the league. The issue is they pass out of 12 and 13 personnel less than 40% of the time, according to SumerSports. This both inflates their pass success rate and shows they are running more than 60% of the time out of these formations, allowing defenses to key in on the run. Recently, Declan Doyle has had an issue with running out of heavy on first down too frequently, making it very obvious and setting the Ravens behind the chains. The Ravens need to start mixing it up more. That could mean throwing out of heavy on early downs more often to catch the Panthers by surprise. The biggest issue there is that the Panthers have allowed the third-fewest yards per attempt against multi-tight end sets (5.8). The real solution might just be to lean on Jacoby Brissetts arm, play more 11 personnel, and sling the ball around the field to Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and Ja’Kobi Lane. The Panthers have been down their top three cornerbacks for a while. Rookie Will Lee is expected to return in this one, but Jaycee Horn remains on IR and Mike Jackson, while practicing this week, hasn’t been activated yet. The Ravens might want to test whoever is covering their wide receivers. Spreading the offense out in 11 might help the run game as well if the Ravens can find success early through the air and back the Panthers off the line of scrimmage and out of the box. Finishes from Mike Green and Trey Hendrickson Hendrickson leads the Ravens in pressures despite missing two games and dealing with a figure injury since Week 1. He’s also getting double-teamed 42% of his pass rush snaps, according to ESPN. He also only has two sacks through his first eight games as a Raven, and that simply isn’t good enough or what the Ravens paid for. Conversely, the Ravens have seen Green get better throughout this season while going through some ups and downs, switching from one side of the defensive front to the other. He leads the Ravens in sacks with 5.5. The Panthers’ biggest overall weakness is their offensive line. Both of Carolina’s offensive tackles have been question marks this season. Their rookie right tackle, Monroe Freeling, has a 6-foot-7 frame with speed and athleticism, but the transition from left tackle in college to right in the NFL hasn’t been without questions. Rasheed Walker on the left side has struggled this season and given up a chunk of sacks as well. Without Madubuike, the Ravens need their two top edge rushers to get pressures and, more importantly, finish. Middle of the field defense It’s no surprise to anyone who watches Ravens games that their defense has given up a lot over the middle of the field. They’ve also been the worst defense on intermediate passes, giving up a league-worst 0.77 EPA per play on passes between 10 and 19 yards. Furthermore, the Ravens have been targeted on in-breaking routes on 36.7% of opponents’ passes, giving up seven touchdowns on them, 10th most in the league according to Next-Gen Stats. Meanwhile, the Panthers have four different 6-foot-4 wide receivers, and Bryce Young has thrown in-breakers on 38.8% of his routes, averaging 9.0 yards per attempt on these routes. That’s a lot of size and a lot of attempts for Roquan Smith to cover over the middle. Jesse Minter’s defense is designed to leave the middle of the field open; it’s the hardest area of the field to consistently throw in, with the most bodies, hands, arms, and heads to navigate. The idea is to funnel passes there, force as many tough throws as possible, and then have 11 hats on the ball to tackle quickly when passes do get caught there. It hasn’t worked so far. The Ravens players haven’t executed it consistently all season, and Minter has yet to deviate from it. Something has to change, and this would be a great game to make changes for it.

title: AFC North Week 10 Recap: Browns pull off another comeback
summary: Three teams in the AFC North appear poised for a playoff push down the final stretch of the season. Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) The Bengals took the division lead with a 38-18 dismantling of the Steelers on Sunday Night Football. No quarterback has played better than Joe Burrow over the past month. Against Pittsburgh, he completed […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Deshaun Watson #4 and Quinshon Judkins #10 of the Cleveland Browns celebrate after a 5-yard touchdown run by Judkins during the quarter against the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field on November 15, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Three teams in the AFC North appear poised for a playoff push down the final stretch of the season. Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) The Bengals took the division lead with a 38-18 dismantling of the Steelers on Sunday Night Football. No quarterback has played better than Joe Burrow over the past month. Against Pittsburgh, he completed 35 of 44 pass attempts for 406 yards and four touchdowns. Burrow is now the betting favorite to win MVP with a league-high 27 passing touchdowns through 10 weeks. His top target, Ja’Marr Chase, has been red-hot as well in recent weeks, culminating in his best game of the season against the Steelers with 231 receiving yards on 11 catches. Chase Brown led the team in rushing with 44 yards on 10 carries while adding 39 yards and a pair of touchdowns on eight receptions. Dohnte Meyers and Drew Sample accounted for Burrow’s other two touchdowns. Cincinnati’s free agent additions continue to show up on defense as both Boye Mafe and Jonathan Allen had sacks against Pittsburgh, bringing the pair’s combined sack total to 10.5 on the season. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) The Steelers fell to 6-3 and second place in the division with their 38-18 loss to the Bengals. Pittsburgh found themselves in a 31-3 hole to start the fourth quarter. It was only then that Aaron Rodgers and the offense found some rhythm with consecutive touchdown drives. Rodgers finished the game with 15 completions on 29 attempts for 143 yards and a pair of touchdown passes — one to DK Metcalf, who led the team with 54 receiving yards on two catches, and the other to Pat Freiermuth. Jaylen Warren struggled to get going on the ground, rushing seven times for just 15 yards. Instead, it was fourth-year running back Lew Nichols who led the team with 43 rushing yards on six carries. The Steelers’ defense had no answers for Burrow and Cincinnati’s passing attack. Patrick Queen had the defense’s lone sack of the night while Payton Wilson racked up 19 total tackles. Cleveland Browns (6-4) After starting the game down 17-0, the Browns rallied to defeat the Houston Texans, 27-24, to improve to 6-4. Deshaun Watson returned to the field after missing Week 9, completing 25 of 40 pass attempts for 312 yards and an interception while adding a team-high 49 yards and one touchdown on eight carries. This was Watson’s sixth fourth-quarter comeback this season. Harold Fannin Jr. continues to look like a rising star at the tight end position as he led the team with 91 receiving yards on seven catches. As usual, Carson Schwesinger led Cleveland’s defense with 13 total tackles. Isaiah McGuire had the only sack on C.J. Stroud while Tyson Campbell came away with an interception in the second quarter. Baltimore Ravens (4-6) The Ravens suffered their fifth straight loss in Week 10, falling 23-20 to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers. Veteran journeyman Jacoby Brissett made his debut at quarterback for Baltimore after just 10 days with the team. Brissett threw the ball 49 times, completing 33 passes for 340 yards and an interception. Mark Andrews seemed to have an immediate connection with his fourth quarterback of the season, leading the team with 82 receiving yards on eight catches — both season highs. While the passing attack found life for the first time in weeks, the run game was the complete opposite. Derrick Henry was repeatedly hit behind the line of scrimmage, finishing the game with just 10 yards on 10 carries, though he did find the end zone twice. The Ravens’ defense continues to be a disappointment under Jesse Minter. Omarion Hampton had his best game of the season, crossing 100 rushing yards for the first time in a game this year. This was also the first game that Justin Herbert did not throw an interception all season. Mike Green was a bright spot for the unit at least, with two sacks on Herbert and several strong plays against the run.

title: Buffalo Bills elevate Tre’Davious White, Shaq Thompson from practice squad
summary: Grappling with injuries on defense, the Buffalo Bills have elevated linebacker Shaq Thompson and cornerback Tre’Davious White from their practice squad ahead of Sunday’s matchup with the Miami Dolphins. Thompson, 32, played in 12 regular-season games for Buffalo last season, starting 6. He totaled 56 tackles, 1 sack, 6 tackles for loss, 2 pass breakups, […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 17: Tre'Davious White #27 of the Buffalo Bills looks on from the field during an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Grappling with injuries on defense, the Buffalo Bills have elevated linebacker Shaq Thompson and cornerback Tre’Davious White from their practice squad ahead of Sunday’s matchup with the Miami Dolphins. The Bills have elevated ILB Shaq Thompson and CB Tre'Davious White from the practice squad for tomorrow’s game. — Sal Capaccio 🏈 (@SalSports) November 21, 2026 Thompson, 32, played in 12 regular-season games for Buffalo last season, starting 6. He totaled 56 tackles, 1 sack, 6 tackles for loss, 2 pass breakups, and 1 fumble recovery. In Buffalo’s two playoff games, Thompson was excellent, notching 13 total tackles, a team-high 10 solo tackles, 2 tackles for loss, and an interception. The veteran is a former first-round pick of the Carolina Panthers, having been the No. 25 overall selection in the 2015 NFL Draft. Thompson will have a role this week in place of Dorian Williams, who is out with a calf injury that he suffered late in last week’s win over the New York Jets. Whether Thompson plays a significant role on defense or not is yet to be determined, but at worst, he provides strong depth for the Bills. Rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr is the other likely option to start next to Terrel Bernard. White, 31, also spent last season with the Bills. He played a significant part in the team’s defense, starting 16 games in the regular season across from Christian Benford. It’s thanks to Benford’s injured groin that White finds himself elevated this week, as he’ll either start across from rookie Davison Igbinosun or serve as depth behind the second-year man that he started over last season, Maxwell Hairston. During the 2025 season, White totaled 40 tackles, 10 pass breakups, and an interception. In the postseason, White started both games, totaling six tackles and three pass breakups. White originally entered the NFL in 2017 as Buffalo’s first-round draft choice that year, and after spending the 2024 season with the Baltimore Ravens and Los Angeles Rams, he returned home and played well last season. White allowed just 51% of the pass thrown when he was the closest man in coverage to be completed, holding opposing quarterbacks to a 71.1 quarterback rating when targeting him. The Bills and Dolphins are a 1 p.m. EDT start on Sunday. Each team’s official inactive lists will be released 90 minutes prior to kickoff.
