title: Buffalo Bills vs. Miami Dolphins injury news: Ed Oliver questionable for Week 11
summary: The injuries continue piling up for the Buffalo Bills ahead of their Week 11 home game against the Miami Dolphins. A surprise report originating from the team on Saturday afternoon revealed that Bills starting defensive tackle Ed Oliver is dealing with an oblique injury. Oliver is now listed as questionable for Sunday’s home game, though […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Ed Oliver #91 of the Buffalo Bills reacts as he takes the field against the Baltimore Ravens prior to an NFL football game at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The injuries continue piling up for the Buffalo Bills ahead of their Week 11 home game against the Miami Dolphins. A surprise report originating from the team on Saturday afternoon revealed that Bills starting defensive tackle Ed Oliver is dealing with an oblique injury. Oliver is now listed as questionable for Sunday’s home game, though the news is not all doom and gloom. Matt Parrino provided some context to Oliver’s injury , tweeting that “(p)er a league source, Ed Oliver notified Bills training staff this morning that he felt pain in his oblique. The staff checked it out and there’s optimism that he’ll play against the Dolphins.” Per NFL rules, Oliver’s ailment must be accounted for on the injury report even at this late stage, which is why he’s being listed as questionable. In the past, Oliver’s situation would have likely had him tabbed as “probable” for game day. The NFL has since done away with that injury designation, which has seen the questionable term pick up the slack in filing injuries throughout the league. Should Oliver be unable to go (or limited in some fashion) it would be a huge blow to Buffalo’s defense, which already has to account for injuries to starters in cornerback Christian Benford and inside linebacker Dorian Williams. Both Bills defenders have been ruled out ahead of Week 11 .

title: 5 Miami Dolphins to watch at the Buffalo Bills
summary: The Buffalo Bills host the Miami Dolphins on Sunday in a game of two franchises headed in completely opposite directions. The 8-1 Bills sit atop the AFC, leading the conference by one game over the Jacksonville Jaguars and Kansas City Chiefs (the Denver Broncos are also 7-2, but they are currently the No. 5 seed […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills host the Miami Dolphins on Sunday in a game of two franchises headed in completely opposite directions. The 8-1 Bills sit atop the AFC, leading the conference by one game over the Jacksonville Jaguars and Kansas City Chiefs (the Denver Broncos are also 7-2, but they are currently the No. 5 seed in the playoff picture). Miami, on the other hand, is 1-8 and tied for the AFC’s worst record with the Los Angeles Chargers and Tennessee Titans. On paper, this a game that Buffalo should win running away. However, games are played on the field, not on paper, and Miami has kept plenty of games close this season. Half of Miami’s losses have come in one-possession games, and they’ve held great offenses like the Chiefs and the Detroit Lions under their season scoring average. If the Bills want to avoid the pitfalls of a textbook “trap game,” they’ll need to lock in and focus on stopping Miami’s key players. Here are five Dolphins to watch in Sunday’s tilt with the Bills. _____________________________________________________________________________ RB Ollie Gordon After De’Von Achane went down with a knee injury earlier this season, it was easy to assume that Miami’s run game would suffer mightily. Thanks to Gordon, though, Miami has been able to run fairly well throughout the course of the year. With former Syracuse Orange quarterback Kyle McCord set to make his second career start this week, Miami will want to try to establish the run and maintain possession of the ball to keep their young quarterback out of obvious passing situations. Shutting Gordon down and keeping Miami in continuous second-and-long or third-and-long scenarios will go a long way towards driving the Bills to victory this week. Buffalo has been good against the run, as they are No. 8 in yards allowed on the ground. Gordon averages 4.2 yards per rush. If the Bills can prevent him from breaking big runs, they’ll be in great shape. WR Malik Washington Buffalo’s secondary is beaten up, and while the Dolphins don’t boast a great passing attack, they do have some sneaky-good weapons who can beat you if you aren’t careful. Chief among those weapons is Washington, who leads Miami in targets (51), receptions (36), and receiving yards (400). At 5’8” and 192 lbs., he operates out of the slot more often than not, so it will be up to whomever Buffalo plays inside to contain him. Given their injuries in the secondary, that responsibility could fall to Dee Alford, Jordan Hancock, Damar Hamlin, or a combination of multiple defenders, including linebackers. Washington is particularly good after the catch, as 123 of his 400 receiving yards have come as “YAC” gains. If he catches a short pass, that’s fine; what the Bills can’t do is let him slip tackles and pick up big gains after he makes that grab. DE Chop Robinson The 2024 first-round pick is on pace for a career year, and good for him. It took Robinson some time to put it together as a pro, but he has five sacks already on the season, which is one shy of the career-high six sacks he notched as a rookie. He also has 13 quarterback hits, which is just one shy of his career-high total from that same 2024 rookie season. Both Spencer Brown and Dion Dawkins are likely to play this week, so Buffalo should finally be back at full strength along the offensive line after playing some different combinations due to injury over the last three weeks. Making sure that Robinson stays out of the offensive backfield needs to be a major focus of the game plan. LB Jacob Rodriguez While the Rookie of the Year hype that came with Rodriguez in the season’s early going has faded a bit, what hasn’t faded is the quality of Rodriguez’s play. The rookie out of Texas Tech has looked every bit the part of a long-term starter at middle linebacker for a Miami defense that has played better than the team’s 1-8 record would suggest. Rodriguez was a fan favorite for many Bills-connected folks during the draft process last spring, and his play so far has justified that hype. He has 80 tackles, four tackles for loss, one sack, one interception, and one forced fumble so far this season. Head coach and offensive playcaller Joe Brady needs to try to give the rookie some different looks by using motion to throw off his keys. That should help Buffalo to make him hesitate just enough to wall up some blocking around him. Buffalo is the league’s second-best rushing offense, but the Dolphins allow just 3.9 yards per rush thanks in large part to Rodriguez’s talent. Neutralizing him in the middle could make for a long day for Miami. S Michael Taaffe Taaffe is someone I really liked for Buffalo in April’s draft. He’s a hyper-athletic safety who reminded me a little bit of Cole Bishop. Like Bishop, he’s made some plays here in the early portion of his career, but he’s also been burned for some big gains. Taaffe leads the Dolphins with three interceptions, but he’s also allowed three touchdowns and a passer rating against of 100.7 this season, as opposing quarterbacks have completed 64% of their passes for a whopping 329 yards when he’s the closest man in coverage. If Buffalo can run the ball effectively, that will lead Taaffe to creep closer to the line of scrimmage to help out in run support. When that happens, the play-action pass will be on, and Buffalo could find some big plays through the air. As long as Josh Allen isn’t forcing the ball, he might be able to exploit a young player in Taaffe at the back end of Miami’s defense. If he’s not careful, though, Taaffe is more than capable of turning what looks like a big offensive play into a turnover.

title: Buffalo Bills game-day food: Frita-Cubana Meatballs
summary: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a […]
full_text: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a themed recipe based on the Bills and their opponent. I’ve done recipes for Miami Dolphins games lots of times and this has never come up. Is it authentic Miami? I dunno. It was good though. Frita-Cubana Meatballs How many Dolphins games have we done now? Let’s see; 2018 until now… add a playoff game, carry the one… it’s been a few. Somehow I never stumbled on frita as a food item until now. For those of you also new to the term and food, it’s a hamburger variant that mixes burger and chorizo into the patty and tops it with French fries, I wanted to make it a little more shareable and went with a meatball variation. It’ll definitely make enough to share, but maybe you won’t want to. Frita-Cubano Meatballs Makes: Enough for 4-6 people Active time: 30 min Total time: About 2 hours Ingredients 2 large eggs 1/2 red onion, minced 1/2 cup hot sauce 3 Tbsp melted butter 1 tsp salt 2 tsp black pepper 1/4 tsp cinnamon 1 lb hamburger (80/20 for the fat) 1 lb chorizo, preferably ground but you can use links (I had to, see below) 1 1/2 cups crushed potato chips Vegetable oil for cooking Essentials: Mixing bowl, high-wall fry pan, spatulas for carefully rolling and extracting meatballs, paper towels, food processor recommended Crack eggs into mixing bowl. Stir in onions, melted butter, hot sauce, salt, pepper, and cinnamon. Fold in burger and chorizo (if using links, see below). Thoroughly mix in crushed potato chips; chill in refrigerator. Add approximately one half-inch of vegetable oil to high-wall fry pan; preheat on MED/HIGH (about 6 or 7 on my stove top). Squeeze together meatballs, forming each into roughly 1-inch diameter rounds. IMPORTANT: Squeeze tightly as these tend to be a bit more fragile than traditional meatballs. Carefully place meatballs in oil, in batches; roll every few minutes to brown evenly. Continue until all sides have a crispy exterior; about 10-15 min (see picture for final color). Carefully remove from pan when fully cooked; place on a tray or large plate covered in paper towels to catch and drain excess oil. Repeat steps 7 through 8 until done. Garnish with cheese, additional hot sauce, etc. before serving. Wingin’ It tips A reminder to buy Ninja products from the link below so I can get some beer money or something maybe. If you’re looking for a good food processor that made mincing the onions trivial, mine did the trick in seconds. The same with the chorizo. On that note in particular: I ended up having to buy links, which meant removing the casing and making it mixable into the burger. I find it easiest to snip the very end of the sausage to remove the casing. And again, the processor made chopping trivial. I could have likely done the chips in here too, but didn’t think of it until after the onions and chorizo — which meant the sides had moisture on them. I also suspect the fact that I bought links contributed to some of the difficulty being cohesive. I used very firm pressure to make the meatballs, and gentle flipping until all sides were cooked thoroughly made them stable. Not enough to put on toothpicks, but enough to pick up easily. Give me money. Money me. Money now. Me a money needing a lot now ! Skarekrow likes certain products. Skarekrow likes money. Skarekrow recommends the following products and hopes you buy them from these links, which might result in Skarekrow getting money. Melinda’s Hot Sauces! Ninja Kitchen Appliances!

title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch vs. the Miami Dolphins
summary: The Buffalo Bills are looking to extend their current winning streak to six games this week as they take on the Miami Dolphins, who are looking to avoid extending their own three-game losing streak. In 17 matchups with No. 17 at the helm against Miami, the Bills are 14-3. While the Dolphins did win the […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills are looking to extend their current winning streak to six games this week as they take on the Miami Dolphins, who are looking to avoid extending their own three-game losing streak. In 17 matchups with No. 17 at the helm against Miami, the Bills are 14-3. While the Dolphins did win the last time these two teams met, scoring a decisive 30-13 victory over Buffalo last November, much has changed since then. For starters, neither team’s head coach from that game is with the club, as former Buffalo head coach Sean McDermott is unemployed, and former Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel is the offensive coordinator for the 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers. Miami has torn the team down to the studs, as quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, running back De’Von Achane, and wideouts Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill are either no longer with the club or injured. Buffalo, meanwhile, has started the Joe Brady era by winning eight of their new head coach’s first nine games. How can the Bills avoid dropping what should be a winnable game against a rebuilding divisional foe? It would help if their top players performed well, but with some injuries to navigate, the Bills will have some new faces stepping up this week. Here are five Bills to watch against Miami on Sunday. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Josh Allen Allen has long dominated the Dolphins, posting video-game numbers against Miami for the whole of his career. Allen has completed 66.6% of his passes for 4,608 passing yards, 45 passing touchdowns, and 11 interceptions. On the ground, he’s run for 723 yards and five scores on 101 carries against Miami. Remember, this is across 17 games. Allen traditionally does great things against the Dolphins, and I’d expect that he’ll continue that trend this Sunday. He might not run for the kinds of yards that he did in years’ past against Miami, especially with a game coming up on Thursday night, but he will definitely be a central figure in the action. Look for the Bills to give Allen some quick-hitters early to establish a rhythm before hitting some big throws on play-action as the game progresses. TE Dawson Knox Dalton Kincaid is doubtful to play thanks to thumb and ankle injuries, and while it’s entirely possible that he suits up, he’ll likely be limited even if he does play. That means that Knox may have a chance to step up against a Miami defense that has not defended opposing tight ends well this season. George Kittle, Travis Kelce, Mason Taylor, T.J. Hockenson, Mike Gesicki, and others have either had big games or scored plenty of points—in real and fantasy football—against Miami. Knox isn’t elite, but he is a reliable target for Josh Allen as his longest-tenured pass-catcher. If Kincaid is able to go, I expect he’ll break off a big play or two, but if he can’t, expect Knox to have his best day of the season. OLB Greg Rousseau Groot is the kind of guy who can just wreck anything the Dolphins have going for them on offense. Against second-year man Kyle McCord, who will be making his second start, Rousseau presents a problem for multiple reasons. First, his length gives him the ability to block passing lanes that would otherwise be open. Second, he is shifty enough and strong enough on the edge to make McCord uncomfortable regardless of the situation. Third, the Dolphins are very weak at tackle, and having someone like Rousseau out there with Ed Oliver, Deone Walker, Bradley Chubb, T.J. Sanders, and T.J. Parker doesn’t bode well for a struggling offensive line. Austin Jackson, Miami’s starter at right tackle, is ranked No. 71 out of 72 qualifying tackles at Pro Football Focus . He’s No. 69 in pass block grade and No. 65 in run block grade. Rousseau should be excited to see Jackson across from him this week. LB Kaleb Elarms-Orr The rookie is likely to start this week with veteran Dorian Williams out due to a calf injury he suffered in last week’s win over the New York Jets. That’s a big loss for Buffalo, as Williams has been very good of late. However, the team is high on Elarms-Orr, and he has flashed some big-hitting ability early in his career. He’s appeared on just 21% of Buffalo’s defensive snaps this season, totaling 18 tackles, but he alreayd has two fumble recoveries to his name, as well. He’s struggled a bit in pass coverage, so look for Miami to try to manipulate him through motion and play-action early. Will the Bills call veteran Shaq Thompson up from the practice squad to supplement the linebacker group this week? And, if they do, will Thompson eat into Alarms-Orr’s playing time? We’ll find out on Sunday, but look for No. 52 to make some big hits this week. CB Maxwell Hairston The second-year man has looked totally lost this season, as a rookie year that flashed some potential has given way to a second season where he has lost not only a shot at a starting gig, but really any shot at playing many meaningful snaps. Rookie Davison Igbinosun has far outplayed Hairston this season, but with Christian Benford out this week, Hairston has a chance to build back some trust with the coaching staff. Miami’s passing game isn’t exactly elite—it’s not even league-average, as the Dolphins rank No. 31 in attempts, No. 29 in passing yards, and No. 29 in passing touchdowns—so this is a good time for Hairston to make a play or two. I think the ship has sailed, at least for now, where we look at Hairston as someone who should be playing when all of Buffalo’s corners are healthy; however, it would be nice for him to have a week where he looks like someone who could play in a big spot if needed. That’s a low bar to clear, but one he’s consistently knocked over throughout this season. Veteran Tre’Davious White may see time as a practice squad elevation, too. If Hairston can’t see snaps and play effectively this week, then it might be time for a bigger conversation about the former Kentucky product.

title: Bills news: Previewing the Dolphins
summary: The Buffalo Bills (8-1) host the Miami Dolphins (1-8) on Sunday afternoon in a battle of teams sitting at opposite ends of the AFC East. What can fans expect in Week 11, when the Bills and Dolphins meet up for the 125th time? Today’s edition of Buffalo Rumblinks leads off by sharing the key matchups […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills (8-1) host the Miami Dolphins (1-8) on Sunday afternoon in a battle of teams sitting at opposite ends of the AFC East. What can fans expect in Week 11, when the Bills and Dolphins meet up for the 125th time? Today’s edition of Buffalo Rumblinks leads off by sharing the key matchups to watch and positional analysis as Josh Allen and the Bills look to beat the Dolphins for the 15th time in their last 18 meetings. Check out the assessments below and then let us know your thoughts on the game in the comments section. Bills vs. Dolphins storylines to watch Linked below: Breaking down the key story lines to watch, including how, for the fourth straight week, Buffalo’s defense will be tasked with facing a backup quarterback: former Syracuse University standout Kyle McCord, who will be making his second start. We examine what a McCord-offense could look like against an improved Bills defense that has excelled over the last three weeks, regardless of who was in at quarterback. Buffalo knocked out both Baltimore Ravens starting quarterback Lamar Jackson and New York Jets starting QB Geno Smith in wins in Weeks 8 and 10, while confounding Minnesota Vikings backup QB Carson Wentz in a Week 9 win on Monday Night Football. We also dissect the changes Jim Leonhard has made for a Bills defense that has not allowed a touchdown over the last 33 possessions; hear what Joe Brady, Josh Allen and others think about the clash with the Dolphins; find out which rookies have stepped up their productivity to help fuel the defensive turnaround; identify the Bills players with the most to prove vs. Miami; explain why a few of Buffalo’s young defensive players could be primed to contribute in place of some injured starters; and more! summary: The Carolina Panthers have been on an odd run of injuries, poor discipline, horrible officiating, and good opponents for too long now. Injury luck, if only for the moment, seems to be a tide turning in the Panthers’ favor; discipline may yet prove to be the deciding factor in head coach Dave Canales’ tenure; and […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - NOVEMBER 20: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens shakes hands with Baker Mayfield #6 of the Carolina Panthers after an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 20, 2022 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers have been on an odd run of injuries, poor discipline, horrible officiating, and good opponents for too long now. Injury luck, if only for the moment, seems to be a tide turning in the Panthers’ favor; discipline may yet prove to be the deciding factor in head coach Dave Canales’ tenure; and the quality of their opponent this week is certainly up for debate. Whether we’re talking Lamar Jackson or Marlon Humphrey, the Baltimore Ravens are perhaps the first team missing as much talent as the Panthers—if not more—that Carolina has seen on their schedule this season. Enter Jacoby Brissett. The spry, 33-year old, ten year veteran was acquired by the Ravens via trade on November 6th after Jackson and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley were both lost for the season after only five pass attempts against the Buffalo Bills in Week 8. Brissett started his first game just last Monday, November 16th, for the Ravens and attempted 49 passes in a three-point loss to the Los Angeles Chargers. We don’t know what we’re going to see from Brissett tomorrow. He’s with a new team, has a history of ups and downs as a starter, and is coming off of a short week of preparation. Brissett and the Ravens are a true wildcard. Maybe Will Lee III and Mike Jackson returning will be enough to iron out any concerns over what Brissett and Ravens team in disarray will bring to the field. Then again, we’re pinning a lot of hope there on a rookie corner returning from injury who has shown both promise and a penchant for his own discipline related penalties. That’s not to mention the broader penalty issues or quarterback Bryce Young’s returning lack of consistency. Maybe that’s why, at -2.5, the Panthers are favored over the Ravens in what is tied as the second narrowest spread on FanDuel this week. There are as many reasons to be optimistic about the Panthers in this and future weeks as there are reasons to keep them firmly in the “I’ll believe it when I see it” category. summary: All it took is one skin-of-their-teeth win over the New Orleans Saints to end a three-game losing skid, seize first place in the NFC South, and restore some faith from fans for the 4-5 Carolina Panthers. It helps, of course, that they are facing, at home, a 4-6 Baltimore Ravens team who is on their […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Jacoby Brissett #11 of the Baltimore Ravens warms up prior to the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images All it took is one skin-of-their-teeth win over the New Orleans Saints to end a three-game losing skid, seize first place in the NFC South, and restore some faith from fans for the 4-5 Carolina Panthers. It helps, of course, that they are facing, at home, a 4-6 Baltimore Ravens team who is on their own five-game losing streak and is 1-5 in their last six games since Lamar Jackson was injured the first time for the season. This week they are giving newly acquired Jacoby Brissett his second start at quarterback for the Ravens and we’re all going to see what happens after that. Confidence rising 26% after a win in which the team arguably played a less complete game than they did in their loss to the Denver Broncos the week before has me wondering if this survey is just a lagging indicator of wins. They are the division leader with the worst record, with the NFC East leading New York Giants coming in as a close second at 5-3-1. Third place is a four way tie of 7-2 teams, including the Detroit Lions who currently sit atop a three-way 7-2 tie in the NFC North. There is no wonder we are seeing a lot of contemplation about changes to the playoff format when the Panthers are on track for a home playoff game (or whoever ‘wins’ the NFC South) and the NFC North is likely to have one or more teams with winning records miss the playoffs entirely. As for this week, most fans are unsurprisingly expecting a win. The Ravens have suffered injuries both natural and self-inflicted—looking at you, Marlon Humphrey—and are struggling to find a quarterback solution to keep their own playoff hopes on life support. The path to a wildcard berth is more open in the AFC, but extremely unlikely all the same. Have the Ravens given up as a team? Are they simply hopeless without Jackson? Are the Carolina Panthers capable of resurrecting any team’s lost pride and dignity with a surprisingly competitive game? A disciplined Panthers squad that is getting healthier are catching the ailing Ravens at the perfect time. Whether or not that is what we see on Sunday is anybody’s guess. title: Bears have a chance to prove a key prediction wrong in Week 11 vs. Saints
summary: With newly acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons in the fold, the Chicago Bears’ defensive outlook and philosophy have undergone a major shift for the better. That’s not just from an individual perspective, though Simmons has been great in that regard, posting three tackles for loss, two sacks, and two passes defended in his two weeks […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 15: Travis Etienne Jr. #3 of the New Orleans Saints warms up before a game against the Carolina Panthers at Caesars Superdome on November 15, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With newly acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons in the fold, the Chicago Bears’ defensive outlook and philosophy have undergone a major shift for the better. That’s not just from an individual perspective, though Simmons has been great in that regard, posting three tackles for loss, two sacks, and two passes defended in his two weeks with the Bears. The unit as a whole has benefited from the increased double teams the All-Pro tackle has faced, allowing just 4.5 yards per play when he’s been on the field and ranking in the top 10 in EPA/play and success rate allowed since Simmons got here. But there’s one aspect in which, while improved, the Bears have remained somewhat middling at: defending the run. That’s why NFL.com ‘s Brooke Cersosimo forecasts New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne might be a problem for Chicago on Sunday. “Etienne returned to action last week after missing five games with a hamstring injury and looked rusty — to say the least — rushing for 14 yards on eight carries. He turns things around in dramatic fashion against the Bears on Sunday with his first 100-yard rushing performance and touchdown of the season,” Cersosimo wrote for her bold prediction for this week in NFL action. That’s definitely a choice. When healthy, Etienne is one of the better dual-threat backs in the league. But nothing about his performance in his first season with the Saints suggests he’s either of those things (142 rushing yards on 38 carries). In fact, no one in New Orleans running backs room has done much worth writing home about: through nine games, quarterback Tyler Shough leads the team with 187 rushing yards. That’s ugly. The Saints have a true running-by-committee squad, ravaged by a combination of injuries and ineffectiveness. So it’s unlikely any of them gets enough action on their own to approach 100 yards rushing unless one of them gets hot. From what we’ve seen, there’s nothing to suggest that’ll happen. Plus, if the Bears come out hot on offense and put Shough and the Saints in catch-up mode, you can forget about Etienne as a rushing threat. That, no doubt, is part of what the Bears hope to do. But it’s also important to note just how big a deal this Simmons acquisition has been for Chicago. Because yes, the Bears defense has been pretty uninspiring against the run for the past couple of years, and a player with Etienne’s skill set could definitely have given them trouble in a game like this before Simmons arrived. These days, though, the Bears have the look of a squad bent on changing that reputation (as long as Simmons stays healthy and on the field himself). The presence of an elite defensive tackle has everyone playing better, especially speedy linebacker Devin Bush. Again, there’s nothing wrong with a bold prediction or two. But let’s stash an Etienne 100-yard game in the “highly unlikely” category.

title: Chicago Bears vs. New Orleans Saints: Week 11 Players to Watch
summary: Though the Chicago Bears have won 4 of the last 5 games, including three straight prime-time matchups, the BYE week couldn’t have come at a better time as they embrace the much-needed opportunity to rest their wounded and prepare for the final stretch of the 2026 season. That starts in earnest this Sunday as Caleb […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 13: Carl Granderson #96 and Chase Young #99 of the New Orleans Saints stand on the sidelines during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on September 13, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Though the Chicago Bears have won 4 of the last 5 games, including three straight prime-time matchups, the BYE week couldn’t have come at a better time as they embrace the much-needed opportunity to rest their wounded and prepare for the final stretch of the 2026 season. That starts in earnest this Sunday as Caleb Williams and Co. host the New Orleans Saints. A team that has struggled mightily this season despite being one game behind in the race to win the putrid NFC South. Make no mistake, this is as winnable a game as the Bears will see the rest of the season, but a conference matchup in such a tight race atop the NFC is also a must-win at this point in the season, and it also happens to be against Bears’ defensive coordinator’s former team, so there will absolutely be some added emotions this week. Either way, here are a couple Saints players to keep an eye on. Starting on offense. Offense: Jordyn Tyson, #0 – WR The number 8 overall prospect selected in the 2026 NFL and the 2nd WR taken, the former Arizona State Sun Devil has been inactive for most of the season dealing with some nagging soft-tissue injuries. While Tyson was only targeted 5 times in his first action as a pro two weeks ago against Cleveland, he led the team with 13 targets (more than doubled the next most player) last week against Carolina and converted 11 of those into receptions for 80 yards. Tyson is an explosive play-maker who might not be quite as physical after the catch but reminds me of Luther Burden III with his burst in and out of cuts and how he can make defenders miss in the open field. Tyson is the type of receiver who can give our corners fits, so I will be eager to see how Dennis Allen plans to slow him down while not losing track of the big-play weapons like Chris Olave, Barion Brown and fellow rookie Bryce Lance. With a depleted offensive line, I expect much more quick passes from QB Tyler Shough, so Tyson figures to once again receive the bulk of the targets. If Chicago can limit his YAC, they should force New Orleans to turn the ball over and score enough points on offense to put this one away. That is, if they can slow down the Saints pass rush. Defense: Carl Granderson, #96 – DE With two players in the top 5 of the current NFL sack leaders, the Saints boast as potent of a pass-rush threat as any team in the league. Carl Granderson holds the slight edge with 8.5 sacks to Chase Young’s 8.0, but both players will be key in containing Caleb Williams and forcing errant throws like we saw in Chicago’s last action against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Not only does Granderson lead the team in sacks, but he also leads the team in tackles for a loss with 10.5, and that is despite missing a game this season already. While I have the utmost confidence in Chicago’s OL and how Ben Johnson schemes up protection, fending off these pass rushers will be a primary focal point this week. As our own Mongo Peanut pointed out , Bears Left Tackle Theo Benedet will have his work cut out for him this week. If Chicago can limit their production and prevent them from making any game-wrecking plays, the Bears should march up and down the field and put up points in droves. If not, New Orleans has a chance at an upset in Week 11. What about you? Which New Orleans players figure to be most important for a Saints victory, outside of QB Tyler Shough?!

title: Caleb Williams has moved on from that 4 pick anomaly
summary: The Chicago Bears are 7-2 and coming off a much-needed bye week, which allowed them to regroup and refresh after a first half of the season in which they led the league in time of possession. They’ll also get back one of their key offensive players, running back Kyle Monangai, who hasn’t played since Week […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears celebrates a touchdown during a game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears are 7-2 and coming off a much-needed bye week, which allowed them to regroup and refresh after a first half of the season in which they led the league in time of possession. They’ll also get back one of their key offensive players, running back Kyle Monangai, who hasn’t played since Week 4. Also, wideout Luther Burden III, who exited their last game with a concussion, has cleared protocol during the bye and will be good to go this Sunday. Chicago’s bye really came at a perfect time for the team, although it also came after Caleb Williams threw four interceptions against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Caleb’s competitiveness and drive are well chronicled, so he was asked earlier this week if that performance has lingered with him at all during the bye. After breaking down the four picks as one “bad decision,” two of them “funky,” and one where the ball “popped up in the air,” he explained what stuck with him during the week. “The biggest thing is, the frustration comes from the feeling of, for me, personally, I always don’t want to let my teammates down,” Williams said from Halas Hall. “That’s always big for me. And in that situation, in those situations, I feel like I did. And so, that’s the frustrating part that lingers.” You can tell Williams is itching to get back out there and put that game behind him, but did you realize that even with those 4 interceptions, he’s still the least-intercepted quarterback in league history? Okay, technically Williams doesn’t have enough attempts to qualify for the all-time leaderboard, but his 1.36 interception percentage is lower than Aaron Rodgers’ 1.42%. Williams needs 175 more passing attempts to reach 1,500, and if he stays under Rodgers’ interception percentage mark, he’ll be the new and official number-one least-intercepted QB, per Pro Football Reference . Then again, Rodgers is still active, so he’ll have a say in the number, but regardless, Caleb is in rare air with how safe he is with the football. “I’ll move on from it,” he said about his 4 pick game anomaly. “I’ve moved on from it,” he clarified. “You know, it’s more of a how can I get better? What can I be better at? Just finding ways to be more consistent. And in those other situations where, you know, I’m not making a dumb decision like the first one. I’m trying to either get it out of bounds or, you know, anything like that — just juice it out of bounds.” The Bears host the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, and FanDuel Sportsbook has Chicago at -11.5. The Bears’ moneyline is -720, and the game’s over/under is 48.5.

title: Question of the Day: How many wins will it take to win the NFC North?
summary: The Chicago Bears sit at 7-2, but unfortunately, the Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings also sit at 7-2, making it a 3-way tie for first. The Bears currently are losing the tiebreakers to both Detroit and Minnesota, so the Bears technically sit in 3rd place in the division, with the 6-4 Packers in last. The […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 14: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears and Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions shake hands following the game at Ford Field on September 14, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears sit at 7-2, but unfortunately, the Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings also sit at 7-2, making it a 3-way tie for first. The Bears currently are losing the tiebreakers to both Detroit and Minnesota, so the Bears technically sit in 3rd place in the division, with the 6-4 Packers in last. The North is a gauntlet and a half and with 6 divisional games left to be played (4 featuring the Bears), it’s going to be the divisional games that are truly going to decide who is going to win the crown and have home field advantage in the playoffs through at least the first two rounds of the playoffs. Question of the Day: How many wins will it take to win the North? I think for the Bears, it’s going to come down to which teams they beat down the stretch. With 8 games to go, however unlikely, if the Bears win their 4 games out of the division and go 1-3 in the games in the division, that’s going to put them at 12 wins, but they will probably not have the tiebreaker against any of the teams in the division if that happens, which means that won’t be enough. But if the Bears go 2-2 outside of the division and 3-1 in the divisional games, that’s also a 12-5 record, but they would be in much better shape in the tiebreaker situation. Answer. With the 0-2 divisional record, even if the Bears went 3-1 in the division and finished with 12 wins, they probably wouldn’t have the tiebreaker against everyone. If the 1 loss comes to the Packers or Vikings, that team will have the tiebreaker. If Minnesota wins 1 more divisional game, they’ll most likely have the tiebreaker against the Bears. It gets tricky for Chicago and tiebreakers within the division. Unless the Bears go 4-0 in divisional games down the stretch. However, if they do that, with New Orleans and Miami on the schedule, the Bears would be looking at, most likely, at least 6 more wins, giving them 13. 13 is the number. With 3 teams at 7-2, and with how good all four teams are, I just think it’s more likely than not that one of them reaches the 13-win total. I find it hard to believe that two of them will, given they all have divisional games remaining against each other. I think one of these teams finds a way to 13, and that’s the number that wins the North. I think if the Bears or any of the other teams reach 12 wins, that will guarantee them a wild-card playoff spot. If any of them only get to 11 wins, I think that leaves them vulnerable to missing the playoffs. An 11-6 team missing the playoffs would be wild, but if the last-place team in the North finishes 11-6, and the Seahawks or Rams can get to 11-6, that means one of them is going to be sitting home in January with 11 wins but missing the playoffs. What do you say, Bears fans? Do you think they need to win 13 games to win the division, or do you think a smaller number can get it done? Or do they need to reach an even bigger total?

title: Bears Week 11 Flashbacks: Ditka’s Revenge, Butler’s Boot, Jets Shutout
summary: Climb aboard the Gridiron Time Machine as we revisit three memorable Week 11 performances from Chicago Bears history! 1.) 1985, Bears @ Cowboys: Ditka gets the last laugh November 17, 1985 | Bears win 44-0 The 1985 Chicago Bears entered Week 11 undefeated at 10-0, but their trip to Dallas carried a little extra significance […]
full_text: Chicago Bears linebacker Brian Urlacher (54) runs upfield, chased by New York Jets Brad Smith and Brandon Moore, following an interception on the goal line in the second quarter. The Bears defeated the Jets, 10-0, at Giants Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, Sunday, November 19, 2006. (Photo by Jim Prisching/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) Climb aboard the Gridiron Time Machine as we revisit three memorable Week 11 performances from Chicago Bears history! 1.) 1985, Bears @ Cowboys: Ditka gets the last laugh November 17, 1985 | Bears win 44-0 The 1985 Chicago Bears entered Week 11 undefeated at 10-0, but their trip to Dallas carried a little extra significance for head coach Mike Ditka. Waiting on the opposite sideline was Tom Landry, the legendary Cowboys coach who had brought Ditka onto his coaching staff after his playing career ended. By the time the afternoon was over, Landry probably wished his former assistant had stayed home. The Bears wasted little time making their presence felt. Richard Dent intercepted a deflected Danny White pass and returned it one yard for a touchdown to open the scoring. Mike Richardson joined the fun in the second quarter, returning another interception 36 yards for a score. Chicago led 24-0 at halftime, and things weren’t about to get any better for Dallas. November 17, 1985 #Bears #Cowboys The student vs the teacher. Chicago dominates Dallas, Dent TD. 44-0 #DaBears pic.twitter.com/UYpuQHWiOC — Old Time Football 🏈 (@Ol_TimeFootball) October 30, 2022 The Bears’ defense intercepted four passes, recovered a fumble and sacked Cowboys quarterbacks six times. Dallas managed just 171 total yards, including a miserable 52 on the ground, while converting only three of its 13 third-down opportunities. Walter Payton handled business on the offensive side, rushing for 132 yards on 22 carries. Chicago finished with 216 rushing yards and 378 total yards of offense, while Kevin Butler connected on all three of his field goal attempts. The Bears scored another 20 points in the second half, including fourth-quarter touchdown runs from Calvin Thomas and Dennis Gentry, turning an already embarrassing afternoon into a historic beatdown. Chicago walked out of Texas Stadium with a 44-0 victory, improving to 11-0 and clinching the NFC Central championship. Four interceptions, two defensive touchdowns and a 44-point shutout against America’s Team. Not a bad way to remind your former boss how far you’ve come. 2.) 1990, Bears @ Broncos: Butler gets a second chance November 18, 1990 | Bears win 16-13 (OT) The Bears entered Week 11 of the 1990 season at 8-1, riding a five-game winning streak and looking like one of the best teams in the NFC. A trip to Mile High Stadium against John Elway and the Denver Broncos would prove to be anything but easy. Chicago’s offense struggled to find the end zone for much of the afternoon, settling for a pair of Kevin Butler field goals before Brad Muster finally broke through with a 10-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter. The score gave Chicago a 13-6 advantage heading into the final period. Unfortunately, Elway wasn’t finished. The Broncos quarterback scrambled nine yards for a touchdown early in the fourth quarter, tying the game at 13 and setting up a tense finish. Chicago had an opportunity to win in regulation, but Butler’s 41-yard field goal attempt struck the left upright. Not exactly the ending the Bears had in mind. Fortunately, overtime gave Butler an opportunity to make up for the miss. After the Bears got the ball back with favorable field position, Butler stepped onto the field and drilled a 44-yard field goal to secure a 16-13 victory. While Butler supplied the game-winning points, Chicago’s ground game did much of the heavy lifting. Neal Anderson rushed for 110 yards on 28 carries, helping the Bears pile up 202 rushing yards and control the football for more than 40 minutes. The defense also made life difficult for Elway, recording six sacks and forcing two turnovers while holding Denver to just 108 rushing yards. Chicago escaped Mile High Stadium with its sixth consecutive victory, improving to 9-1 on the season. A missed game-winner, an overtime opportunity and a kicker who made sure he didn’t miss twice. Sometimes all you need is a second chance. 3.) 2006, Bears @ Jets: The defense does it again November 19, 2006 | Bears win 10-0 The 2006 Chicago Bears were already 8-1 when they traveled to the Meadowlands for a Week 11 matchup with the New York Jets. They were also beginning to establish a familiar formula for winning football games. Play outstanding defense, run the football and hope Rex Grossman doesn’t make things too interesting. Against the Jets, that formula worked just fine. Neither offense managed to score in the first half, with Chicago struggling to move the football through the air and New York finding little success against Lovie Smith’s defense. Grossman completed just 11-of-22 passes for 119 yards on the afternoon, while the Bears converted only four of their 14 third-down opportunities. Fortunately, Thomas Jones was there to keep the offense moving. Jones rushed for 121 yards on 23 carries, helping Chicago accumulate 173 yards on the ground. The Bears finished with 284 total yards of offense, but points remained difficult to come by. Robbie Gould finally broke the scoreless tie with a 20-yard field goal in the third quarter, giving Chicago a 3-0 lead. Then, early in the fourth quarter, Grossman connected with Mark Bradley for a 57-yard touchdown that provided some much-needed breathing room. That was more than enough for the Bears’ defense. Chicago intercepted Jets quarterback Chad Pennington twice, with Brian Urlacher and Nathan Vasher each recording a takeaway. Pennington finished with just 162 passing yards, and New York managed only 264 total yards despite running nine more offensive plays than Chicago. The Jets also converted just six of their 17 third-down attempts as the Bears secured their second shutout of the season. Chicago walked away with a 10-0 victory, improving to 9-1 and continuing its march toward Super Bowl XLI. Ten points, 119 passing yards and another victory. Who needs an explosive offense when the other team can’t score? Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs .

title: At 7-2, Have the Bears Met or Exceeded Your Preseason Expectations?
summary: The Chicago Bears have completed what Ben Johnson would refer to as “2 quarters” of the 2026 NFL season. Despite early adversity, they’ve managed to come away with only two losses so far – a mark that would be more impressive if they weren’t still sitting in 3rd place in their division. Still, the halfway […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 4: Head Coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears walks out to the field prior to the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears have completed what Ben Johnson would refer to as “2 quarters” of the 2026 NFL season. Despite early adversity, they’ve managed to come away with only two losses so far – a mark that would be more impressive if they weren’t still sitting in 3rd place in their division. Still, the halfway point of the season presents us with a great opportunity to look back at the record predictions of a few of our WCG writers and evaluate just how close we each were to predicting this level of performance from the Bears. It also gives us a chance to look at our predictions for the remaining games and how confident we may now be feeling in those predictions. First, here’s the Bears’ remaining schedule: Week 11 – Nov. 22 vs. New Orleans Saints, noon on FOX Week 12 – Thanksgiving Day at Detroit Lions, noon on CBS Week 13 – Dec. 6 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars, noon on FOX Week 14 – Dec. 13 at Miami Dolphins, noon on CBS Week 15 – Dec. 19, Saturday at Buffalo Bills, 7:20 p.m. on CBS Week 16 – Christmas Day, Friday, Dec. 25 – vs. Green Bay Packers, noon on Netflix Week 17 – Jan. 3 vs. Detroit Lions, 3:25 p.m. on FOX Week 18 – Jan. 10 at Minnesota Vikings, TBD And here’s our look back… Donald Gooch: I had the Bears at 12-5 on the season, so if you project out their record over the next eight games based on the first nine, the expected record is between 11-6 and 12-5, so the Bears are on pace for what I expected before the season. I expect the Bears to meet, and perhaps exceed, my preseason prediction. Jacob Infante: My expectation was that the Bears would finish the year with a similar 11-6 record to what they had in 2025. Now, my expectations are higher, especially seeing their offensive improvement and after the addition of Jeffery Simmons to the defense. Their divisional schedule will be difficult to deal with, but my expectation is now that they’ll end the season with a 12-5 record. TJ Starman: My original prediction was for the Bears to end up 11-6. I was pretty accurate with my expectations for the first half of the season, though I did ultimately trade a predicted win in week 2 vs the Vikings for actual wins against both the Eagles and Seahawks. That said, I still expect 3 more losses in the next 8 games, which would put my adjusted prediction at 12-5. Josh Sunderbruch: I had the Bears at 10-6-1 and just barely making the playoffs in May, and I had guessed 6-3 at the bye, so they’ve beaten my expectations by one win so far. I can see them going 4-4 down the stretch, for 11-6, but I’d love for it to be 5-3 (for 12-5). Either way, I see them making the playoffs but losing out on hosting a home wildcard game due to a poor record against divisional foes.
author: Josh Sunderbruch

title: Saints at Bears Q&A: Dennis Allen Revenge Game Part 2
summary: The Bears are back from their bye week and ready to welcome the New Orleans Saints to Soldier Field. The Bears are sitting at 7-2 and in prime position to make the playoffs. The Saints sit at 3-6, but fortunately for them, they are only a game and a half out of first in the […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen of the Chicago Bears looks on during the fourth quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bears are back from their bye week and ready to welcome the New Orleans Saints to Soldier Field. The Bears are sitting at 7-2 and in prime position to make the playoffs. The Saints sit at 3-6, but fortunately for them, they are only a game and a half out of first in the weak NFC South. To help get you set for this matchup, we sat down with Nic Jennings of our sister site, Canal Street Chronicles (SB Nation’s New Orleans Saints site), to get you set for their opponent. 1. The Saints are sitting at 3-6, but from my outsider view, I feel like this team is close to clicking, potentially even the back half of this season and start winning some football games. What’s the vibe around the Saints for the fan base? The vibe around the fanbase isn’t great right now. I don’t think fans have given up on the players, but rather they’ve given up on Kellen Moore, Mickey Loomis, and Gayle Benson. The Saints are somehow only one game out of first place in the division, so there’s still hope that they can turn things around and make a push. But it is frustrating to watch a roster with this much talent continue to fail to put everything together. At this point, I think changes need to be made within the regime, and until that happens, I expect the vibes around the fanbase to remain largely the same, win or lose. 2. I’ll be honest, when Kellen Moore was hired, I didn’t think much of him as a head coaching candidate, but I’ve come around on him a little. What did Saints fans think of the hire last year, ar and where are they at with him midway through 2026? The initial reaction to Moore’s hiring was that the Saints finally had another offensive-minded head coach in the building who could bring a refreshing change to the way things had been done. However, that optimism has long since faded. Moore is running out of excuses, and quite frankly, I don’t think there is any way he can win the fanbase back at this point. Through his first 26 games, the Saints have trailed in every single one of those games, while failing to score in the first quarter 18 times. Two consistent issues have plagued Moore’s teams across both seasons: slow starts that force the Saints to claw their way back into games and an offense that continues to look dysfunctional, with a putrid run game forcing Tyler Shough to carry the team on his back. At this point, the frustration has gone beyond results, and fans are rightfully questioning whether Moore is the guy to lead this team moving forward. 3. I’ve never been a fan of how Mickey Loomis has handled the cap and the rebuild/reload (whatever you want to call it) of this roster. Are Saints fans still behind Loomis or do they want to see a change? Yes, the fanbase still wants a change in the front office, but it’s not necessarily because of the financial side of things. The Saints are expected to finally be out of “cap hell” next season and back to operating with more financial flexibility. However, Mickey Loomis’ draft-day decisions and head coaching hires since Sean Payton’s departure have taken their toll on the fanbase. For a team that has been in a rebuilding phase, it’s difficult to get out of that cycle without consistently drafting impactful players, and that’s been one of the biggest issues. The tricky part is that Loomis is the NFL’s longest-tenured general manager at 25 years and has won a Super Bowl with the franchise. Given his history and relationship with the organization, I don’t see Gayle Benson moving on from him unless he decides to step down himself. That’s what makes the situation so complicated. 4. Tyler Shough certainly looks like he’s taking strides this year, but he’s also 27 years old. Do you think Shough is a legit NFL QB that can lead this Saints offense for the next 5 to 7 years? Absolutely. Shough is the real deal, and his teammates rally behind him. He’s been one of the few consistent bright spots for the Saints this season, along with Chris Olave, Chase Young, and Carl Granderson. Shough showed a lot of promise in his limited starts as a rookie, then attacked the offseason and blew expectations out of the water. He’s carried that same momentum into this season. His ball placement, ability to stretch the field with his arm, poise in the pocket, and ability to extend plays with his legs give the Saints a dimension offensively that they haven’t really had. And most importantly, he has that clutch gene. He’s shown he can make plays when the Saints need them most. I do think there are still things he can improve on, and he’s had a bit of a rough stretch over the last two weeks. Like I previously mentioned, the offense has developed a habit of starting slowly, and while I’d put more of that on Kellen Moore, Shough still plays a role in getting the offense into a rhythm. Though,gh to Shough’s credit, the Saints have a nonexistent rushing attack, which hasn’t eased the pressure on Shough and the passing game one bit. But overall, I’ve seen more than enough to believe he can be the long-term answer in New Orleans. As for his age, to put things into perspective, Drew Brees joined the Saints at 27 years old, and it felt like he was in New Orleans for a lifetime. Even as a 26-year-old rookie, Shough was visibly more prepared than his fellow rookies. I view his age as a benefit rather than a drawback and believe he has a long career ahead of him. 5. What is one player on the Saints offense and one player on the Saints defense that may not be a headliner that you think can make an impact on Sunday? Do you have a prediction for the game? On offense, I’ll go with Devaughn Vele. After the Saints invested a fourth-round pick in him last year to pry him away from Denver, Vele has come in and become the contested-catch slot receiver the Saints have been searching for since Michael Thomas. He’s quickly become one of Tyler Shough’s favorite targets and has established himself as the go-to guy in third-and-long situations. With Jordyn Tyson back in the mix alongside Chris Olave, Vele’s production has dwindled a bit over the past two games. That said, I believe his opportunities will come, and he’s proven he can take advantage of them. For a six-foot-five receiver to move the way he does and possess that type of body control is truly remarkable. On defense, keep an eye on second-year defensive back, Jonas Sanker. He consistently finds his way to the football and has been impressive in his first year starting in the slot. He returned a fumble for a touchdown against the Vikings and had another return for a touchdown in Week 1 against the Lions that was called back after Jared Goff apparently “intended” to throw the football forward. With Justin Reid now out of the picture in New Orleans, perhaps we see Sanker move back to his natural position at safety, where he spent his rookie season.

full_text: Not much more than Cleveland Browns fans could ask for in 2026 than to be heading into Thanksgiving with the team at 6-4 , in a playoff spot , and among the second tier of AFC contenders . Getting to enjoy the bye week while looking forward to Week 12’s Sunday Night Football game adds to the peace and joy in the middle of November. We’ve used the bye week to catch up on some things while also looking ahead. GM Andrew Berry will likely continue to look for changes that he believes could help the team, which could include players returning from injured reserve. As of now, Cleveland has six players on the IR list, but only three could return: OL Teven Jenkins – A back injury limited him in training camp and then into the season before being placed on IR. Jenkins could return FB Michael Burton – Placed on injured reserve last week, Burton’s calf injury is not considered major, and he might be able to return this season, if needed RB Raheim Sanders – A hip injury earlier in the year knocked the Browns backup back out, but a return is possible and even expected DE Alex Wright – Out for the year due to a ruptured Achilles DT Kalia Davis – Cleveland thought they would get Davis back, opened his practice window, then found an injury in practice that ended his possibility of playing for the team this season. CB Damarri Mathis – A roster hopeful, Mathis injured his knee in training camp and is out for the year D o you think Jenkins, Burton or Sanders will be helpful to the Browns at some point this season? title: With Christmas a month away, buying a current Browns player’s jersey is a fun, tough decision
summary: For all of us who have been Cleveland Browns fans for decades (four-plus here), the honest truth is that it takes more time and energy to defend our fandom than it has often been worth on the field. That is why Browns fans have long been the greatest fanbase in the world. We’ve loved hearing […]
full_text: For all of us who have been Cleveland Browns fans for decades ( four-plus here ), the honest truth is that it takes more time and energy to defend our fandom than it has often been worth on the field . That is why Browns fans have long been the greatest fanbase in the world. We’ve loved hearing all of the stories about your fandom and what this team means to you . Now, we are excited for Sunday Night Football for the nation to learn all about what is great about Cleveland, the fans, and (finally) the team: And, now, choosing a Browns jersey is actually a tough decision, but finally a fun one. Cleveland’s roster has a number of very good young players who, from all accounts, are good people as well. Unlike in the past, when a Browns jersey would almost certainly be Joe Thomas, Joe Haden, Nick Chubb , or one of a select few historical players, fans preparing for Christmas lists and/or shopping have to be a little more particular about which player’s number they’d like to have or buy for a Cleveland fan: CB Denzel Ward – The veteran on the list, Ward is having an All-Pro season WR KC Concepcion – The rookie who battles his stutter publicly is an inspiration off the field and is playing well on it. LB Carson Schwesinger – “Captain America” was a star as a rookie and continues to play at a high level, with a high motor and all the effort any Browns fan could want from a defender. WR Denzel Boston – A big, fun-loving receiver who makes highlight plays and seems to enjoy life, often seen with a smile on his face. TE Harold Fannin Jr. – Coming out of a smaller Ohio school to become a star in Cleveland? Yeah, that is the story of a great jersey purchase. Add that to his fight-for-every-yard mentality on the field, including a few “Angry Runs” and you have the makings of a Browns fan favorite. DT Mason Graham – The question of who would replace Myles Garrett on the defensive line has started to come from the interior with Graham. The second-year pro has exploded on the field, despite an injury limiting him for a bit, and plays with passion and determination. (He’ll get a slight knock from me and many other Buckeyes for his choice of colleges, but that can always be forgiven) OT Spencer Fano – A player I would describe as equal parts serious, goofy, and hard-working, pronounced: “Fawn-O” (like a “little baby deer,” as my friend Cami Justice explained to me), Cleveland fans love players on the offensive line, so he had to be on this list. An interesting website called Jersey Advisor has taken on the task of actively helping fans choose a jersey based on a number of criteria: …a tool that scores active NFL players on how “safe” a jersey investment they are, weighing performance, tenure, durability, sportsmanship, and popularity. Constantly updating the scores, Jersey Advisor currently has Schwesinger as the safest pick among Browns fans. After the linebacker, linemen take the next three spots, with many Cleveland fans likely to disagree with one of the choices: DE Jared Verse , Graham, and Fano. The rest of the list order may not be exactly what Browns fans would expect, but the names make sense, especially for an algorithm trying to encapsulate what every roster has going on. Check out Jersey Advisor and see their thoughts on your favorite Browns players. Which jersey would you want for Christmas or would you want to buy for a Browns fan in your life? title: Browns roster: 2 backups who could help take the offense to another level
summary: Fans of the Cleveland Browns are enjoying a peaceful bye week before preparing for Week 12’s Sunday Night Football matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders. There are still a ton of questions surrounding the Browns, including whether they are actually a good team or just happened to win games. Cleveland HC Todd Monken must use […]
full_text: Fans of the Cleveland Browns are enjoying a peaceful bye week before preparing for Week 12’s Sunday Night Football matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders . There are still a ton of questions surrounding the Browns, including whether they are actually a good team or just happened to win games . Cleveland HC Todd Monken must use the bye week to get the team’s running game going and figure out how to help in the early part of the game . Beyond that, the offense has to find more stabilit y, much of which could come through the rushing attack and a schedule with defenses that can be attacked . While many will point to the offensive line, QB Deshaun Watson , and RB Quinshon Judkins as places where the Browns offense needs to improve, two backups could help take the offense to another level: RB Dylan Sampson and WR Isaiah Bond . Now, neither player is likely to take over significantly more snaps for the rest of the season, although Bond needs a few more if he’s going to make any impact at all, but both have a chance to help Monken’s offense be more explosive in different ways. Sampson is not just a change-of-pace back, but one who can make big plays in ways that Judkins just can’t. Misdirection runs, screen plays, dump-off passes, and the occasional late leak-out play could all give Watson and company big gains and keep the offense on the field. Sampson’s ability to make plays all over the field and from a variety of positions makes him a versatile threat that must be accounted for. Bond, on the other hand, has really one gift to give the Browns offense: straight-line speed. Unfortunately, mistimed jumps and drops have led Monken to limit the speedster’s snaps in favor of veterans Malachi Corley and Tylan Wallace . It also doesn’t help Bond’s chances that the top three receivers, KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston , and Jerry Jeudy , have deep route speed and ability, but Bond speed is unique. If Monken can trust the second-year receiver and he makes just a couple of big plays in the first few games coming out of the bye week, Bond can not only become impactful in the stat sheet but also as a decoy. Having Bond run deep post, 9-route, and corner routes can take the top off of a defense, pull the safety away, and create more spacing underneath for all of the above-mentioned players, along with TE Harold Fannin Jr. , to make plays after the catch. Cleveland’s offense will not be decided by the performances of Sampson and Bond, but both backups have a chance to take the unit’s performance to another level, assuming that the line, QB play, and starting weapons are doing as well as or better than they have so far this season. Barring injury, neither is likely to be a fantasy star or steal significant snaps from any starters, but their impact with explosive plays could move things from good to great. Do you think either Sampson or Bond will be able to make a huge impact for the Browns roster the second half of the season? full_text: The Cleveland Browns are entering the bye week with a 6-4 record , already exceeding many expectations for this season. There have been many highs this season, like watching all the young talent succeed and a number of fourth-quarter game-winning drives. Despite all the highs, there are still several areas where the team could improve. One of the biggest downfalls for the Browns this season was the play from the offensive line. It has been inconsistent, and they have struggled to protect the quarterback and relieve pressure in several situations. There have been a lot of sacks, not all at the fault of the offensive line, but there also have been a lot of penalties from that group. The run blocking has been a more consistent concern as well. They need to clean up their play in the remaining weeks to give the offense the best chance to succeed. Cleveland should also look to improve its starts to games to avoid having to rely on fourth-quarter comebacks. Even though they’ve had success with these fourth-quarter comebacks, they cannot rely on that continuing. It will be important for the team to come out strong in the remaining games and score early to avoid having to fight their way back for a win. title: Cowboys passing attack should shine, pass rush could struggle
summary: The Dallas Cowboys desperately need a win, and Sunday’s matchup against the Tennessee Titans offers a chance to get something positive going after all the Christian Parker drama. Tennessee is 1-8 and has one of the league’s worst defenses, particularly in the secondary. Dallas should have plenty of opportunities to move the ball through the […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys desperately need a win, and Sunday’s matchup against the Tennessee Titans offers a chance to get something positive going after all the Christian Parker drama. Tennessee is 1-8 and has one of the league’s worst defenses, particularly in the secondary. Dallas should have plenty of opportunities to move the ball through the air, especially with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens coming off productive performances. There are still reasons to be cautious. The Cowboys’ defense has been a disaster this year, and Tennessee quarterback Cam Ward has improved over the past few weeks. With Dallas also changing its defensive play-calling, this matchup could tell us a lot about the team’s direction. Here are two players to buy and one area to sell ahead of Sunday’s game. Buy: WR CeeDee Lamb CeeDee Lamb has been on a tear this year, and this week’s matchup against Tennessee should give him another opportunity to put up big numbers, so it’s no surprise he’s on this list again. Lamb is coming off a seven-catch, 72-yard, one-touchdown performance against San Francisco. That came after his 10-catch, 195-yard outing against Indianapolis. Through 10 games, Lamb has 77 receptions for 976 yards and eight touchdowns. He’s averaging 97.6 receiving yards per game and has become the most consistent weapon in Dak Prescott’s passing attack. This matchup is appealing. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per game, the most in the NFL. The Titans have struggled to contain opposing receivers, with Cleveland’s KC Concepcion, Cincinnati’s Tee Higgins and Jacksonville’s Parker Washington all putting up big performances against them in recent weeks. Lamb should have plenty of opportunities to take advantage of that secondary. Whether he’s working out of the slot or lining up outside, the Cowboys need to make sure he’s involved early and often. With eight touchdowns already on the season, there’s little reason to believe his production is slowing down. What a grab from CeeDee 🔥 SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TDOobHrr9r — NFL (@NFL) November 16, 2026 Sell: The Cowboys’ pass rush I’m not buying the Cowboys’ pass rush this week, even after the unit recorded five sacks against San Francisco. That might sound strange, but Tennessee has allowed just 14 sacks this season. The concern is what Cam Ward has been doing with his legs and how the Titans have adjusted their offense to better suit him. Ward has been much more comfortable over the past few weeks. He’s completed 54 of 79 passes for 535 yards, four touchdowns and one interception across his last two games, posting a 98.9 passer rating. He’s also been more involved as a runner, and Tennessee has increasingly used tempo and designed quarterback runs to create opportunities for him. The Titans’ offensive approach has changed considerably. They’ve incorporated more no-huddle looks and opportunities for Ward to use his mobility. Against Jacksonville, Tennessee used no-huddle on 49% of its offensive plays, the highest rate by any team this season. That’s a concern for Dallas. The Cowboys have struggled to contain quarterbacks who can escape the pocket, and their pass rush has too often lost its discipline when trying to generate pressure. If the defensive front gets too aggressive and opens running lanes, Ward has the mobility to make them pay. There is also a new wrinkle on the Dallas sideline. Mike Pettine will take over defensive play-calling after the Cowboys removed those responsibilities from Christian Parker. Maybe the change helps, but it’s difficult to expect an immediate turnaround from a defense that has struggled with execution and consistency all season. Cam Ward leads all QBs in rushing yards over last 2 games with 80 yards Him using his legs completely unlock a new dimension of the offense. I know he’s a pocket passer at heart, but it’s clear that Daboll is working with him on this and it’s working pic.twitter.com/B7Z7QbANLi — Titans Era (@titanserashow) November 16, 2026 Buy: WR George Pickens If Lamb is the Cowboys’ most consistent weapon, George Pickens might be their most dangerous big-play threat. After missing time with a hamstring injury, Pickens returned against San Francisco and delivered the best performance of his Dallas career. Pickens hauled in 11 receptions for 145 yards and three touchdowns on 18 targets. He set career highs in catches and receiving touchdowns, giving Prescott another reliable option in a passing game that has been productive throughout the season. Through nine games, Pickens has 50 receptions for 678 yards and five touchdowns. He’s averaging 13.6 yards per catch and has shown the ability to stretch the field and win contested catches. Tennessee’s secondary has struggled to contain receivers all season, and its recent performances suggest opposing offenses can find plenty of downfield opportunities. The Titans are allowing the most passing yards per game in the league, and they’ve surrendered several big performances to opposing receivers over the past month. With Lamb commanding attention from the secondary, Pickens should have opportunities to exploit one-on-one matchups. The Cowboys have two legitimate receiving threats capable of taking over a game, and this is the type of matchup where both could produce. title: Cowboys vs Titans: Writer predictions for Week 11
summary: Dallas gets one of its best opportunities of the season to steady things after the 46-40 loss to San Francisco. Tennessee is 1-8 and ranks near the bottom of the league on both sides of the ball. Dallas should be the better team here, but after giving up 584 yards last week, the defense still […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images | Getty Images Dallas gets one of its best opportunities of the season to steady things after the 46-40 loss to San Francisco. Tennessee is 1-8 and ranks near the bottom of the league on both sides of the ball. Dallas should be the better team here, but after giving up 584 yards last week, the defense still has something to prove. When Tennessee has the ball Tennessee should lean heavily on Tony Pollard. The former Cowboy has 628 rushing yards and six touchdowns, and Dallas has just been gashed for 214 yards on the ground by San Francisco. If the Titans can get Pollard moving early, it takes pressure off Cam Ward and gives Tennessee a chance to control the tempo. Dallas has to make Ward win this game through the air. Tennessee ranks near the bottom of the league in scoring and total offense, while Ward has been inconsistent despite showing flashes. The Cowboys need to contain Pollard, keep Ward in the pocket and force long third downs. With Tennessee also dealing with injuries at receiver, Dallas should have the advantage if it avoids the missed tackles and busted assignments that hurt so badly last week. When Dallas has the ball This is where Dallas should take control. Tennessee owns the league’s worst pass defense, while Dak Prescott is playing some of his best football and just threw five touchdowns against San Francisco. With CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens both capable of taking over a game, Dallas should attack downfield rather than becoming too conservative. Javonte Williams still needs enough work to keep Tennessee honest, but this matchup belongs in Prescott’s hands. The Titans can create turnovers, so Dallas cannot get careless, but if the offensive line protects well there should be favourable matchups across the field all afternoon. The Cowboys should have too much firepower for Tennessee. If Dallas tackles better, limits Pollard and avoids gifting the Titans short fields, this is a game it should control. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (5-5) Often a shakeup mid-season sees at least a temporary improvement in performance. I think that will be the case here. Cowboys 34 Titans 23 Brandon Loree (7-3) The Cowboys made a big shakeup this week by taking play-calling duties away from Christian Parker. I feel like the defense is going to try to win this game for their defensive coordinator, and it sets them up well with the Tennessee Titans coming to town. The Titans should be a get-right game for the Cowboys on all fronts, for a team that’s in desperate need of a win. Dallas should have their best performance of the season on defense and should have a strong performance on offense, leading to a 34-17 win before Thanksgiving. Dyllan Rivers (6-4) The Cowboys have struggled against every team this season, good and bad. Considering the game day changes Dallas has made with the defensive play-calling duties, there is a chance Dallas finally takes care of things against a bad team early in a game instead of in the waning moments. But I won’t trust it until I see it. My gut feeling tells me Dallas wins by a touchdown or less. Let’s go with 31-27 Cowboys Matt Holleran (5-5) The Cowboys are no doubt a mess, but this absolutely has to be a get-right matchup for them. With all the issues both on and off the field I don’t have much confidence they’ll do it, but I’m going to pick Dallas to get a win. Give me the Cowboys, 33-23. Mike Poland (4-6) To lose this one would bring shame to the game for Dallas. Sure, things are rough right now for the Cowboys after last week, and to lose this one would be a massive shock to all of Cowboys Nation. Confidence is best described as positive, but skidish. Cowboys win 31-17.
