title: NY Giants’ pass defense has been much better than expected
summary: There were, if not outright concerns, certainly questions about how good the New York Giants defense could be in 2026. Between edge defenders Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, and Kayvon Thibodeaux, as well as off-ball linebackers Tremaine Edmunds, Arvell Reese, and Micah McFadden, the Giants’ linebacking corps was expected to be one of the best in […]
full_text: New York Giants defensive back Jevon Holland and Deonte Banks celebrate after an interception. | Getty Images There were, if not outright concerns, certainly questions about how good the New York Giants defense could be in 2026. Between edge defenders Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, and Kayvon Thibodeaux, as well as off-ball linebackers Tremaine Edmunds, Arvell Reese, and Micah McFadden, the Giants’ linebacking corps was expected to be one of the best in the NFL. And the hope was that their defensive line would at least be serviceable after the addition of veteran defensive tackles D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris. The bigger questions were about the Giants’ secondary, particularly after Cor’Dale Flott left in free agency. 2025 free agents Paulson Adebo and Jevon Holland hadn’t panned out in their first years as Giants, while 2023 first round pick Deonte Banks had regressed badly under DC Shane Bowen and was considered a bust. The Giants signed former Cleveland Browns and Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback Greg Newsome II, as well as former Baltimore Ravens safety Ar’Darius Washington, in the 2026 free agency period and drafted Tennessee cornerback Colton Hood in the second round of the draft. However, those moves weren’t viewed as much more than Band-Aids for a Giants’ secondary, and national commentors suggested that the Giants’ scondary could be putrid in the first year of John Harbaugh’s rebuild. Fast-forward nine games, and the Giants’ secondary has been much, much , better than anticipated under Dennard Wilson, Donald D’Alesio, and Addison Lynch. The Giants are currently fielding the NFL’s fourth-best defense in total yardage allowed (2,751 total yards). They’re third-best in passing yardage allowed per game (184.1 yards per game), second in yards per completion allowed (9.8 yards per completion), and 2nd in yards per attempt allowed (6.2 yards per attempt). The Giants are accomplishing this feat with smothering coverage from their starting corners. Both Deonte Banks and Greg Newsome II have been incredibly sticky in man coverage, allowing little separation for receivers. CB Separation Prevented & On Ball Grade pic.twitter.com/Ur1AAOquwB — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) November 20, 2026 Banks is allowing just 2.1 yards of separation as the nearest defender, per NFL NextGenStats, while Newsome is allowing all of 2.6 yards of separation. Banks and Newsome are both forcing tight window throws on over 40 percent of the plays in which they’re the closest defender — which is exactly what the “step coverage” Dennard Wilson’s defense calls for. ( note: “step coverage” calls for the defensive back to be within a step of the offensive player ) And while slot corner Dru Phillips is allowing more separation (3.6 yards on average), he’s allowing -5.9 EPA in coverage and a Catch Rate Over Expected of -13.0 percent. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson praised the Giants’ safeties when he spoke to the media on Thursday, saying, “I think Ar’Darius played his best game the last outing against Washington. Obviously, he tackled extremely well. You saw him, in the fourth quarter in a critical situation, come up with an interception. He’s been doing everything that I know he could do, from being around him in Baltimore when he was there. He is a smaller guy that plays with a big stick. He is going to attack the line of scrimmage. He tackles well. He can cover. So he’s doing a good job. I think all the safeties are doing a good job in their role. It’s kind of safety by committee. All of them deserve the opportunity to play. So that’s why we’ve been playing them.” And Wilson wasn’t just puffing up his players. Each of the Giants’ safeties have played very well in coverage as well. Safety Separation Prevented & On Ball Grade pic.twitter.com/zWzZKQYicC — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) November 20, 2026 Jevon Holland has been among the best safeties in the NFL this year, allowing a -27.8 percent catch rate over expected which is 3rd best among all DBs in the NFL and -13.4 EPA allowed. Jason Pinnock has proven to be remarkably sticky in coverage The Giants’ airtight coverage is allowing them to lead the NFL in the rate of Cover-0, that is man coverage across the board, at 10.8%. That jumps to 11.8% in obvious passing situations, and the Giants are sixth in EPA allowed in those situations. Expected pass situations (EP >=70% based on down, distance, score, time left, etc) pic.twitter.com/pbLv2o08KD — Football Insights 📊 (@fball_insights) November 17, 2026 Interestingly, the Giants’ pressure rate has been remarkably low when only rushing four defenders, even with their sticky coverage. That’s led to frustrations from fans when it comes to sack totals (or the lack thereof), particularly with regard to Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux. Both of the Giants’ starting EDGEs have elite get-offs, but have all of 2.0 sacks between them. NextGenStats has shown us that part of the problem is that the Giants’ opponents specifically game plan for their hyper-athletic pass rushers. The Giants’ opponents feature the second-fastest Time To Throw of any defense in the NFL, as well as a Top-3 deviation from their usual Time To Throw. How does each defense influence Time to Throw? Opposing offenses get the ball out in an average of 2.74s against the Jaguars defense (4th fastest), but that’s 0.17s quicker than they typically do against all other defenses (largest reduction in NFL). pic.twitter.com/8L8Bm4r7ls — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) November 19, 2026 The Giants’ sticky Cover-0 packages work with Wilson’s aggressive blitz patterns (as he refers to them) to provide an answer. The Giants are now second only to the Minnesota Vikings — and the madman that is Brian Flores — in the average number of pass rushers sent at 4.90. Average number of pass rushers by pre-snap alignment Dennard Wilson sneaking into Brian Flores territory pic.twitter.com/9xrjqHLDwz — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) November 19, 2026 The Giants are currently sitting at 5-3-1 on the season, and they can thank their defense for closing out four of those wins, as well as forcing the tie against the Washington Commanders. All told, the Giants’ secondary has been one of the most surprising units in the entire NFL, and it’s powering a defense that is finally playing up to its potential. I suspect they’d be getting much more attention on the national level it weren’t for the low sack numbers and what Flores is doing in Minnesota. Now, the Giants will need them to keep it up, or perhaps even find another level if they can.
author: Chris Pflum

title: New York Giants mailbag: Play calling, Malik Nabers, Dominic Zvada, more
summary: Ben Fitzsimmons asks: I know Matt Nagy is the OC and is the one calling plays. I don’t fully understand how Greg Roman fits into it. We’ve seen the Giants run it between the tackles at least 400 million times on first down this year. We’ve seen that terrible play from the infamous JJ Package […]
full_text: Ben Fitzsimmons asks: I know Matt Nagy is the OC and is the one calling plays. I don’t fully understand how Greg Roman fits into it. We’ve seen the Giants run it between the tackles at least 400 million times on first down this year. We’ve seen that terrible play from the infamous JJ Package show up a few times (still hasn’t worked once btw). We’ve seen the Giants attempt and fail miserably to run the clock out at the end of games multiple times this year. We’ve seen a lack of creativity in the run game as they mostly just run behind Ricard and hope it works (it usually doesn’t). What I’m curious about is how much of that is Greg Roman and how much is Matt Nagy. Is Roman designing the run plays and Matt Nagy is just calling them? Is Roman just providing advice and vibes while Nagy draws up the plays? Does Roman have any impact on how run plays are called each game (I would assume not, but I’ve been wrong many times before)? Ed says: Ben, Greg Roman’s title is ‘Senior Offensive Assistant’. Nagy runs the offense and makes all play-calling decisions. He makes final determination, with John Harbaugh’s input, on the game plan. Roman is acknowledged as one of the best run-game designers in the game today. To my knowledge, Roman is responsible for designing much of the Giants’ run game. Harbaugh has explained that much of the vertical passing game comes from Nagy’s background. As I’ve said, Roman’s specialty is the run game. Nagy’s job, as he has explained it, is to take the menu of options he has in front of him and decide what to use and when to use it. Roman, who has been an offensive coordinator multiple times, sits in the booth with Nagy on game days. Of course there will be some sharing of information and ideas. The decisions, though, are Nagy’s to make. We see the warts. Sometimes, you make the wrong call. Sometimes, you make the right one and players don’t execute it. The Giants are 14th in the league in score at 22.6 points per game. That’s pretty good, considering that they are on their third quarterback and have struggled mightily to block in the run game. Bob Donnelly asks: Following the Commanders’ game you have questioned some of the offensive play calls, especially not running the ball in a few key situations. The OC makes the play call yet much of the blame/criticism seems to be directed towards the HC and his lack of confidence in his team’s ability to run the ball in those situations. In your view how much play calling influence does our head coach exert in critical situations? Ed says: Bob, the reality is that the head coach gets credit when things go right, and everything that goes wrong also lands at his feet. Harbaugh does not call the plays. He can set the direction, though. Does he want the ball run? Thrown? What personnel does he want in the game. Tom Donlan asks: Malik Nabers can make spectacular catches and carry the passing game with a high volume of targets and catches. We’ve also seen drops and a costly fumble against Washington, as well as what some view as immature or disruptive behavior with poor body language on the field. What do you think he needs to do to become a more consistent No. 1 receiver, and do you know how the Giants view the way he voices his frustrations publicly? Ed says: Tom, Malik Nabers has a drop rate this season of 3.5%, per Pro Football Reference. That isn’t exactly terrible. He has fumbled three times in 185 career touches, one basically every 62 touches. Again, that isn’t awful. Drops happen occasionally. No one who has the ball a lot goes through a career without fumbling at times. I’m not getting into the body language debate. As far as becoming a more consistent No. 1 receiver, how about getting some consistent reps with the quarterback. Nabers barely had any time with Jaxson Dart last year. Nabers’ reps were limited all summer as he came back from his knee injury, then Dart went down for the season in Week 2. Now, Nabers and J.J. McCarthy have worked together for a month. My educated guess is the Giants would like him to choose his words more carefully. But, he was encouraged to speak his mind freely as a rookie, and he is still a 23-year-old kid learning to grow up with a much different coach than the one who drafted him. One other thing I will say is that I still believe Nabers has to learn to do a better job fighting to protect his quarteerback. I’m thinking about that interception at the end of the Washington game. The receiver simply has to put up a fight there to make sure the ball gets knocked down and not intercepted. Joel Story asks: I read an article saying that after the Giants/Eagles game on Nov. 8th, Kayvon Thibodeaux was fined $11,941 for taunting, Jeremiah Trotter was fined $6,428 for tripping, Zack Baun was fined $6,750 for illegal use of the helmet, and Andrew Mukuba was fined $9,041 for a hit on a defenseless player. Are these amounts correct? If so, do you know why the NFL/NFLPA have chosen to fine players more for taunting than for the other three actions which could potentially end other players’ seasons or even their careers? Ed says: Joel, yes those amounts are correct. The fine schedule, which you can see it for yourself , is collectively bargained. Taj Siddiqi asks: JH is being criticized for keeping Dominic Zvada and let Jason Sanders walk. Sanders is performing like a pro while Zvada is struggling. Some people think one of the causes for his firing at Baltimore was his decision to stay with the kicker, whose name I can’t recall. Is JH over confident regarding his ability to evaluate kickers? Is the guy at the Baltimore still there or is he even in the league? Ed says: Taj, John Harbaugh has been around long enough to fully understand the ups and downs, and the risks, of choosing to ride with a rookie placekicker. Harbaugh had a rookie placekicker in Baltimore last season. Tyler Loop was very good for the Ravens in 2025. He made 30 of 34 field goals (88.2%). Harbaugh got fired because the Ravens missed the playoffs and the organization felt like his tenure had run its course after 18 years. It just so happens that Loop missed a 44-yard field goal on the final play of that game that would have gotten Baltimore into the playoffs. It was his only miss of the year between 40 and 49 yards. How does anyone criticize a coach for riding with a kicker who went 30 of 34? Loop is still with the Ravens, but he is injured and on IR. Overconfident in his ability to evaluate kickers? Well, he and the Ravens drafted Jordan Stout in the fourth round in 2022. Stout is probably the best punter in the league. Sam Koch punted in Baltimore for 16 years, 14 of those for Harbaugh. Justin Tucker was the best field goal kicker in the NFL for more than a decade, and was bombing 60+ yard kicks long before there were a bunch of other kickers in the league capable of doing it. I would say Harbaugh knows good kickers when he sees them. If Harbaugh ends up being wrong about Zvada, that will be the first kicker or punter he has been wrong about in his time as a head coach. As for Jason Sanders, I saw a number of those practices in the spring. A day or two before he got cut I watched him try to kick a 50-ish yard field goal on a windy day, and I watched the ball basically die and go straight down a couple yards short. I didn’t think he could handle the MetLife Stadium conditions, either. Francis Castros asks: Can you provide the rehabilitation status of the following players and are they required to rehab at the Quest Diagnostics Training Center? – Tyrone Tracy Jr. — RB (Hamstring) – Tremaine Edmunds — LB / MLB (Chest / Shoulder) – Braxton Berrios — WR (Foot – surgery) – Chauncey Golston — DE / Edge (Neck) – Jaxson Dart — QB (Knee – Meniscus) – Brian Burns — LB (Knee – ACL) – Roy Robertson-Harris — DE (Achilles) – Calvin Austin III — WR (Knee) – Rico Payton — CB (Undisclosed) – Jarrick Bernard-Converse — CB (Knee) – Gunner Olszewski — WR (Achilles) – Thaddeus Dixon — CB (Achilles) Ed says: Francis, I…

title: NY Giants news: Clean injury report, ‘baby DJ Reader,’ more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants look to bounce back as they host the Jacksonville Jaguars tomorrow. Giants’ schedule ramps up in difficulty with Sunday’s game against Jaguars | The Athletic The upcoming stretch of games will reveal whether the Giants are for real or […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants look to bounce back as they host the Jacksonville Jaguars tomorrow. Giants’ schedule ramps up in difficulty with Sunday’s game against Jaguars | The Athletic The upcoming stretch of games will reveal whether the Giants are for real or just the beneficiaries of the easiest schedule in the league in the first 10 weeks of the season. The Giants’ first nine opponents have a combined .345 winning percentage. Their final eight opponents have a combined .566 winning percentage, which is the fourth highest in the league. The Jaguars defense will represent the toughest challenge for McCarthy. His first three starts were against the Houston Texans (18th in points allowed per game), the Philadelphia Eagles (19th) and the Washington Commanders (20th). The Jaguars are allowing 16 points per game, second best in the NFL. The Jaguars have been particularly stout against the run, allowing the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game. They rank in the top 10 in yards per carry allowed, rush defense expected points added and success rate on run plays. title: Three Things I’m Looking at in the Jets vs Chargers Game
summary: The New York Jets are headed to the City of Angels for a football game where stadium seats cost less than a cheeseburger in that stadium. A rare Sunday where I get to wait until 4pm to be utterly disappointed instead of the classic 1:00 devastation. I figured the Jets hadn’t been to SoFi too […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 06: (NEW YORK DAILIES OUT) Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers in action against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on November 06, 2023 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Chargers defeated the Jets 27-6. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets are headed to the City of Angels for a football game where stadium seats cost less than a cheeseburger in that stadium. A rare Sunday where I get to wait until 4pm to be utterly disappointed instead of the classic 1:00 devastation. I figured the Jets hadn’t been to SoFi too often, but I was shocked to learn that they haven’t been there since two trips in 2020. The first trip should sound fairly familiar: a Week 11 contest between two terrible teams that had only two combined wins. The Jets employed an old journeyman QB with no tangible long-term future with the team, and the Chargers had Justin Herbert. Had the Chargers not won this past Monday, this would’ve been the exact description of both Jets vs. Chargers games at SoFi Stadium. The second trip was much more memorable: the 0-13 Jets faced a talented 9-4 Rams team and shocked the world by finally winning their first game of the season. We all remember this as the game that shifted the Jets’ odds of having the first overall pick when every poor fanbase was looking to ‘Tank For Trevor’. The Jets won the following week and finished 2-14, securing the second overall pick and failing to properly tank. For those of you who value tanking so much, the Jets have an opportunity to repeat history by winning a game in SoFi Stadium and dropping further down the draft board. But don’t fret: if history repeats the first trip to SoFi, it would mean the Chargers winning a shootout against the Jets, and you get what you want. For what it’s worth, I hate the toxicity of tank culture. For 16 years, the Jets have been losing time and time again, getting high draft picks, and the team isn’t any better. How about we root for wins? Especially this year, with the Colts having released Daniel Jones and the Jets having two additional first-round picks, why do you care so much whether the Jets’ specific pick is 6th or 11th? The flexibility to move anywhere on the board will be there regardless. We keep saying late wins don’t matter, we keep saying let’s get the highest pick, isn’t that the definition of insanity?! We’re literally yearning for the same thing every year and expecting a different result. Clearly, the high draft picks alone aren’t enough to save this team. Especially when they miss (Zach Wilson, Mekhi Becton, Olu Fashanu?). Anyway, let’s get back to this game. Regardless of which outcome you’re rooting for, let’s discuss what’s worth looking at: Grounded Can someone tell the New York Jets that the FAA has resumed flights? They must still think they’re grounded. In each of the last two games, the Jets have scored exactly zero touchdowns and four field goals for a total of 12 points in each game. With all the firepower at their disposable, this is a pretty inexcusable and mind-numbing stat. We talked last week about specifically scoring in the red zone, but now they can’t even throw a TD bomb from outside the red zone. Their last touchdown was a 21-yard run by Braelon Allen in the 3rd quarter against the Raiders. Someone on social media said it’s Breece Hall’s fault they haven’t scored a touchdown in the two games they’ve played since his return. Seeing how Braelon only scored two touchdowns in his five-game break out, I can’t co-sign that claim, but perhaps decreasing his workload to just eight carries per game is hurting the offense overall. Allen’s still averaging a healthy 4.5 yards per carry with Breece back. Hall is averaging 3.9 yards per carry and has had 26 carries to Braelon’s 16. It’s definitely interesting to consider what the rushing totals would be if it were Braelon who had 26 carries and Breece who had 16. While the Chiefs defense has been good, they had allowed a TD in six of the seven games they played before the Jets, despite facing bottom-feeders like the Dolphins, Raiders, and Colts during that time. The Bills had allowed seven of eight, with the exception being Joe Fagnano’s first (and perhaps only) NFL start ever. Sure those are two good teams, but neither defensive unit is giving the ‘85 Bears a run for their money. How about this hypothesis: Geno Smith isn’t doing enough to get this offense going. We mentioned last week how three Jets receivers sit atop the league-wide ranks for average separation score. Geno is not getting people open, that’s a combination of the receivers themselves and Frank Reich. Geno’s job is to hit people when they’re open, or at least not completely covered and he’s failing to do that. A quick look at Geno’s numbers from game-to-game tell the story. He’s been afraid to throw interceptions, so instead he makes a safer throw or holds onto the ball too long and takes a bad sack. After a three-week stretch where he aired out the ball more freely but threw an interception in each game, it seems apparent that his fear has returned. He stopped throwing picks, but had a huge uptick in sacks (again). In these past two weeks of safe Geno, he is throwing 58.5% completion, 0 touchdowns, 0 interceptions, 6 sacks in 10 quarters, and a paltry 5.9 yards per attempt. To compare that to the previous 8 games, he was throwing 69% completion, 12 touchdowns, 3 interceptions, 23 sacks in 32 quarters and 8 yards per attempt. The issue is that now he’s not hitting those “safe throws” either – and the offense as a whole is suffering. You could see pretty clearly the stark difference of Cade’s time in the game. He moved the ball down the field, was absolutely fearless, and while he was much less accurate than Geno he was still able to make plays due to his willingness to trust his playmakers to make plays – which they did . Geno is the more accurate option, he obviously is better at pre-snap recognition at this point in their careers, but he needs to find Cade’s level of fearlessness if the offense is going to take flight again. Hampton Inn This week is the latest in a weekly tradition of telling you guys to buckle up for a thrashing by the opposing team’s running back. It was looking like the Jets would finally get a break from facing a star running back, as Omarion Hampton was struggling(!) the first 8 weeks of the season. In his first seven games, he was only averaging 44 rushing yards per game on 3.5 yards per carry and three touchdowns in that span. Terrible numbers. In the last two games, however, he must’ve remembered he was a first round pick last year because now he’s averaging 81.5 yards per game on 4.7 yards per carry and one touchdown in that span. He has been explosive and a huge part of the reason why a team that was only averaging 14.1 points per game with 0 wins is now averaging 22.5 over it’s last two and split 1-1. What can the Jets do to stop him? Smart money would say ‘nothing’, and bet the over on Hampton’s yards. FanDuel currently has his rushing yards at 62.5, are they kidding? The Jets are on a streak of allowing 80+ rushing yards to the opposing RB1, and almost had bonafide scrub Corey Kiner reach 62.5 (he had 57) in just 11 carries in garbage time in Foxborough. I won’t go back and keep talking about Kyle Monangai’s performance, let’s keep it to the last five games: Opposing Rushing Leader Attempts/Yards Total Touchdowns Score at Halftime Corey Kiner 11/57 0 Jets 3, Pats 17 Ollie Gordon II 25/103 1 Jets 7, Dolphins 21 Mike Washington Jr. 25/83 0 Jets 23, Raiders 14 Kenneth Walker III 18/102 3 Jets 12, Chiefs 14 James Cook 18/157 1 Jets 6, Bills 10 Why include that last column? To make it clear that for this ineptitude, game script is irrelevant. The Jets could be down multiple scores, up multiple scores; it could be a one-score game. The only constant is the opposing leading rusher dominating our hopeless group. Our hopeless group is now…

title: Previewing the Jets’ opposition: Los Angeles Chargers
summary: The last time the Jets beat the Chargers, they were still representing San Diego and Plaxico Burress scored three touchdowns. Since that time, New York have lost five straight times to them, including a 27-6 drubbing in their most recent meeting in 2023. Let’s break down the Chargers’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks Justin […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 06: (NEW YORK DAILIES OUT) Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers in action against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on November 06, 2023 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Chargers defeated the Jets 27-6. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images The last time the Jets beat the Chargers, they were still representing San Diego and Plaxico Burress scored three touchdowns. Since that time, New York have lost five straight times to them, including a 27-6 drubbing in their most recent meeting in 2023. Let’s break down the Chargers’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks Justin Herbert was a pro bowler last season, but he’s having a rough year in 2026, with career-worst numbers in almost every category. In his first six seasons, he averaged 27 touchdown passes and 11 interceptions per year. However, over halfway through the 2026 season, he has thrown for just six touchdown passes and already has 11 interceptions. He didn’t have a very productive game as a passer against the Ravens on Monday night, but at least he managed not to throw an interception for the first time all year as the Chargers finally won their first game to improve to 1-8. He also rushed for a season-high 51 yards and a touchdown. DJ Uiagalelei is the backup but he’s completed just two NFL passes in his career. Offensive Line Incredibly, five of the Chargers’ eight active offensive linemen are rookies, although this is hardly by design. They have five offensive linemen on injured reserve, including well known names like Rashawn Slater, Tyler Biadasz, Trevor Penning and Trey Pipkins. Pipkins was activated for practice last week, though, so his return is possible on Sunday. His official game status is questionable. Unsurprisingly, this has led to the Chargers struggling to protect Herbert, who has been sacked 33 times. Only Deshaun Watson has been sacked more often that that this season. The only two players to start every game so far have been second round rookie Jake Slaughter at center and veteran right guard Cole Strange. At the moment, Joe Alt is at left tackle, with sixth round rookie Logan Taylor at left guard. Slater and Penning had started off the year on the left side, but Alt moved across from right tackle and Taylor stepped in when each of them got hurt. Since Alt’s move, fourth round rookie Travis Burke has been starting at right tackle. Alt has a team-high seven penalties and Strange, who has also given up a team-high three sacks, has six. The three players currently on the bench are veteran guard Kayode Awosika, sixth round tackle Alex Harkey and the undrafted center Jacob Spomer. Awosika and Harkey have started two games each this season. Running Backs Los Angeles’ top running back, Omarion Hampton, last season’s number one pick, is still averaging less than four yards per carry behind the banged-up line, although the Chargers rank 10th in the NFL for rushing offense. He’s coming off his first 100-yard rushing performance of the season in the win over the Ravens. Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal both get work as backups to Hampton but they combined for just four yards on five carries in the Ravens win. They have caught 30 passes and scored three touchdowns between them, though. Scott Matlock is also on the roster as a fullback with Alec Ingold on injured reserve. Pass catchers The leading receiver so far this year for the Chargers is last year’s second round pick Tre Harris who has 26 catches for 348 yards but no touchdowns. You would have expected Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnson to produce more alongside Harris but they’ve only started eight games between them and combined for just 31 catches. However, they’ve flashed big play potential with Johnson averaging 19 yards per catch and McConkey averaging 17. On Monday, McConkey – who is questionable for Sunday – was inactive and Harris was the only Charger with more than 16 receiving yards. At tight end, Oronde Gadsen II has caught 20 passes and Charlie Kolar has caught 15, but David Njoku has been a non-factor. Njoku could play more this week, though, because Kolar has been dealing with a concussion and is listed as questionable. The backups at wide receiver are Theo Wease Jr., KeAndre Lambert-Smith, Derius Davis and fourth round rookie Brenen Thompson. They’ve combined for 12 catches, half of which were by Lambert-Smith. Thompson is listed as doubtful for Sunday. Defensive Line The Chargers operate with a 3-4 system that employs Jamaree Caldwell, Dalvin Tomlinson and Teair Tart as starters. They are poor against the pass, but middle of the pack against the run, and held the Ravens to 16 yards on 15 carries on Monday night. Fifth round rookie Nick Barrett and Justin Eboigbe are the backups inside. All five have played at least 140 snaps with Tomlinson having contributed 2.5 sacks. Linebackers The Chargers drafted Akheem Mesidor in the first round but he’s currently coming off the bench behind veteran Khalil Mack and 2025 pro bowler Tuli Tuipolotu. While none of the three has more than three sacks, they’ve combined for 8.5. Mack leads the team with six tackles for loss, while Tuipolotu leads them with 16 quarterback hits. At inside linebacker, Daiyan Henley plays a full-time role and wears the headset. He leads the team with 62 tackles but has been bothered by a knee issue all year, which even nixed a potential trade to Denver. The knee issue has ruled him out for Sunday. The other starter has been former Jet Del’Shawn Phillips, although Henley was sometimes the only off-ball linebacker on the field. Backups Troy Dye and Marlowe Wax don’t get to play much but Wax should have a bigger role with Henley out. Bud Dupree and Caleb Murphy are the backups on the outside but neither has played much. Defensive Backs Aside from all their injuries on the offensive line, the Chargers have also been deeply impacted by pro bowl safety Derwin James being on injured reserve. Tony Jefferson and Elijah Molden are the current starters at safety, although RJ Mickens and fourth round rookie Genesis Smith have also played over 200 snaps each. Kendall Williamson is also on the roster but hasn’t played on defense and has been listed as out anyway. Tarheeb Still and Donte Jackson are the starting cornerbacks with Still reverting to the slot in nickel packages and Cam Hart entering the game on the outside. Hart has two interceptions and a team-high eight pass breakups. Still practiced all week but showed up on the injury report on Friday and is listed as questionable. Backups Rodney Shelley, Isas Waxter and Deane Leonard have all played less than 100 snaps at cornerback. Shelley is another undrafted rookie but he’s been ruled out, while Waxter is also listed as questionable. Special Teams The Chargers’ kicking game is pretty solid with kicker Cameron Dicker having only missed two kicks all season. He also has the third-lowest opponents’ kickoff return average in the NFL. While punter JK Scott’s raw numbers are not eye-popping, Pro Football Focus currently ranks him first in the league based on their grades. Davis, Mitchell and Vidal have all seen work on kickoff returns, with nobody managing a 35-yard return so far this year. The Jets should be wary of Davis, though, as he had an 87-yard punt return for a touchdown against them in 2023. He’s averaging 10 yards per return on punts with Thompson and McConkey listed as his backups. Jets fans may recall what a good special teams contributor Phillips was, and he’s continued in that vein by leading the Chargers in special teams tackles again despite moving into the starting unit. He led the entire NFL last year. Wax, Murphy and Dye are also productive, while the primary gunners have been Lambert-Smith and the backup cornerbacks.

summary: The eleventh weekend of the 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 11 games. EAGLES GAME The 2-7 Eagles have a 0.7% chance of making the playoffs, according to FTN Fantasy. They’re +4000 to qualify for the postseason on FanDuel, which means you can […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - DECEMBER 29: Teair Tart #93 of the Tennessee Titans sacks Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys during the fourth quarter of the game at Nissan Stadium on December 29, 2022 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The eleventh weekend of the 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 11 games. EAGLES GAME The 2-7 Eagles have a 0.7% chance of making the playoffs, according to FTN Fantasy . They’re +4000 to qualify for the postseason on FanDuel, which means you can bet $10 to win $400 if that happens. In other words, it’s time to be interested in the Eagles maximizing their positioning in the 2027 NFL Draft. Current draft order of non-playoff teams via Tankathon : I can understand fans not wanting the Birds to lose while the game is ongoing, or at all. But the reality is that the 2026 campaign is lost and the Eagles stand to benefit beyond this season by losing and getting the highest draft pick as possible. With a loss to the Steelers, the Eagles can potentially move as high as No. 2 overall. NFL DRAFT CONSIDERATIONS INDIANAPOLIS COLTS defeated by HOUSTON TEXANS: The Colts lost on Thursday night, which wasn’t ideal. They’re a threat to move ahead of Philly in the draft order, especially since their weak strength of schedule will likely give them a tiebreaker over the Eagles if they finish with the same record. The silver lining to a Texans win is that it keeps Houston mathematically alive to win the AFC South. The Eagles would prefer to see the Texans win their division instead of the Jags, since Philly owns Jacksonville first-round pick. JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS at NEW YORK GIANTS: Thanks to the Jordan Davis trade, the Eagles own the Jaguars’ first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Therefore, the Eagles want the Jags to lose as much as possible. The “bonus” to a Giants win is that it helps to prevent any false hope of the Eagles winning their division. Root for the Giants. TENNESSEE TITANS at DALLAS COWBOYS: Two reasons to root for the Titans here: 1) always great to see the Cowboys lose and 2) the Eagles need the Titans to win to have a chance to move ahead of them in the draft order. BALTIMORE RAVENS at CAROLINA PANTHERS: Thanks to the Cam Jurgens trade, the Eagles own Baltimore’s fifth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Therefore, the Eagles want the Ravens to lose as much as possible. Root for the Panthers. MIAMI DOLPHINS at BUFFALO BILLS: The Eagles need the Dolphins to win to have a chance to move ahead of them in the draft order. Root for the Dolphins. NEW ORLEANS SAINTS at CHICAGO BEARS: The Saints are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Saints. TAMPA BAY BUCCANEERS at DETROIT LIONS: The Bucs are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Buccaneers. ARIZONA CARDINALS at KANSAS CITY CHIEFS: The Cards are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Cardinals. NEW YORK JETS at LOS ANGELES CHARGERS: The good news for the Eagles is that one of these two teams currently ahead of them in the draft order will win (barring a tie). Looking at the remaining schedules for these teams (which both rank near the middle of the pack in terms of difficulty), I think the Chargers are actually more likely to win more games after this week. So, it could be good to see the Jets capitalize on a more rare opportunity for them to win. Root for the Jets. LAS VEGAS RAIDERS at DENVER BRONCOS: The Raiders are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Raiders. MINNESOTA VIKINGS at SAN FRANCISCO 49ERS: The Whiners are the less likable team, in my view. But there’s a case to be made the Eagles should want the Packers to win the NFC North (and, ultimately, the Super Bowl) since the Cowboys own Green Bay’s first-round pick. Root for the 49ers. CINCINNATI BENGALS at WASHINGTON COMMANDERS: The Commanders are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Commanders. title: Eagles roster news includes Dontayvion Wicks and Zack Baun to injured reserve
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced five roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 11 home game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Here’s an overview: Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game. A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited number […]
full_text: London, United Kingdom - October 11: Dontayvion Wicks of Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the NFL match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced five roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 11 home game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Here’s an overview: WR Dontayvion Wicks and LB Zack Baun were placed on injured reserve. RB Will Shipley was activated from injured reserve to the roster. DT Gabe Hall and LB Anfernee Orji were temporarily elevated to the roster. Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game . A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited number of times in the postseason. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. DONTAYVION WICKS Wicks hasn’t played since suffering an ankle injury in Week 6. It was looking like he might return to the field this weekend after being limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday. But then he was limited again on Friday and the Eagles added a foot injury description in addition to his ankle injury on their injury report. By going on IR now, Wicks (and Baun) are ineligible to play in the Eagles’ next four games: Week 11 vs. Pittsburgh Steelers Week 12 at Dallas Cowboys Week 13 at Arizona Cardinals Week 14 vs. Indianapolis Colts The Eagles are getting DeVonta Smith back at receiver on Sunday, which is a positive development for the offense. But it would’ve been ideal to get both Smitty and Wicks back on the field together to help out Joe Milton. Instead, the Eagles will move forward with Smith, Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Elijah Moore, and Britain Covey as their receivers for now. ZACK BAUN Baun had a strong game in Week 9 before unexpectedly appearing on the injury report coming out of the bye. Baun did not practice this week due to a back issue. Now he’ll miss at least the next four games … and maybe more if the Eagles decide to shut him down in a lost season. The Eagles will move forward with Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. as their starting linebackers. Campbell’s had more downs than ups in his second season while Trot Jr. has eaten into his playing time. Now we’ll get an extended look at both young players. WILL SHIPLEY The Eagles opened Shipley’s 21-day practice window to return from IR earlier this week. He was limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday before missing Friday’s session due to illness. It seems like Shipley is not yet 100%, so, his role against the Steelers might be fairly limited. But the Eagles needed some more running back depth behind Saquon Barkley since Jaydon Blue is the only other backfield option on the roster. GABE HALL In the aftermath of the Jordan Davis trade, the Eagles decided to temporarily elevate Hall to have more defensive tackle depth. This game will mark Hall’s first regular season snaps since Week 6 of the 2025 season. ANFERNEE ORJI With Baun going on IR and Smael Mondon ruled doubtful to play against Pittsburgh, the Eagles were in need of linebacker depth. And so they temporarily elevated Orji to be the top (and only) backup behind Jihaad Campbell and Trot Jr. A little interesting to see the Eagles went with Orji over the recently re-signed Chance Campbell, who was previously elevated earlier this season. STEELERS NEWS The Steelers downgraded pass rusher Nick Herbig from questionable to out, as expected. He didn’t practice this week. Pittsburgh also notably activated starting receiver Roman Wilson from injured reserve but kept Michael Pittman Jr. on IR.

title: Should the Eagles want Shane Steichen back?
summary: The Eagles have been so bad this season that they’ve forced me to change what I write about. I really enjoy studying opposing teams for the weekly previews, but I’m already more interested in what the Eagles might look like next year. So, over the remaining weeks of the season, I’m going to examine potential […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 24: Head coach Shane Steichen of the Indianapolis Colts looks on against the Philadelphia Eagles in the first half of the preseason game at Lincoln Financial Field on August 24, 2023 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles have been so bad this season that they’ve forced me to change what I write about. I really enjoy studying opposing teams for the weekly previews, but I’m already more interested in what the Eagles might look like next year. So, over the remaining weeks of the season, I’m going to examine potential coaching candidates and some offenses and defenses that interest me. Obviously, this depends on the Eagles making changes, and in this particular case, the Colts letting Shane Steichen go. Neither is guaranteed. However, I thought it would be interesting to look beyond the record and examine whether Steichen is still someone Eagles fans should want back. All statistics are courtesy of Fantasy Points Data Suite and cover Weeks 1–9 of the 2026 season unless otherwise stated. If you want to see a detailed video review of Steichen’s offense, please check it out here . UPDATE: I had just finished writing this when the Colts released Daniel Jones. I guess they agree with me that the quarterback was the problem! Pass Game My overriding feeling watching the Colts was that this looks like an offense Jalen Hurts would enjoy playing in. There are plenty of flood concepts, dagger variations, and opportunities outside the numbers. Steichen still likes to give his quarterback a defined picture and create space through route combinations. The Colts use 2×2 formations on 50.1% of their plays, the third-highest rate in the league, and you regularly see different concepts on either side of the formation. Eagles fans will recognize that immediately. Sometimes that familiarity is reassuring, and sometimes it brings back a few frustrating memories of the past couple of years. I think Steichen’s 2×2 concepts are a lot better than what the Eagles currently run, though. The flood concepts were particularly noticeable because Steichen gets to them in several different ways. Sometimes the running back initially shows protection before releasing into the flat. Sometimes a tight end chips before getting into his route, changing the timing of the combination. Elsewhere, a switch release changes how the defense has to distribute the receivers. These are small details, but they matter because the defense doesn’t get exactly the same picture every time. Steichen can attack the same area of the field while changing the release, the personnel involved, or the route that occupies the underneath defender. Even in a disastrous season, you can still see examples of him understanding how to overload zone coverage and manufacture an available throw. And we know how good Hurts is at throwing this intermediate deep out. So… I'm already in next season mode and have been studying the Colts offense under Shane Steichen. Here's a quick thread. 1) I get the concerns about how bad the Colts are, but I still think you can see elements of Steichen being a good coach. He has changed, but he still… pic.twitter.com/7QiKRF187x — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) November 20, 2026 One of my favorite combinations is a smash variation with a short route underneath and a deep corner route behind it. The Colts repeatedly attack Cover 3 with this, putting the underneath defender in conflict while finding space outside the deep coverage. Sometimes the short route is more of a hitch, sometimes the release changes, and sometimes the Colts adjust the combination based on the coverage. I kept watching these plays and thinking that Hurts could make these throws. You aren’t asking him to live on tight-window throws over the middle. There are opportunities to work outside the numbers, throw vertically, and get the ball to a receiver whose separation the concept created. That was an important part of my evaluation. I’m obviously selecting successful examples here, but these aren’t all plays where an elite receiver destroys someone one-on-one. The Colts don’t have much receiving talent available, yet there are still plays every week where someone is wide open because the design works. After watching the Eagles this season, that stood out! I’m not claiming every call is brilliant, but I saw enough to push back against the idea that Steichen has suddenly forgotten how to coach an offense. Even with limited personnel, he can still create opportunities that don’t require the quarterback or receiver to do something extraordinary. I watched every single offensive play with a positive EPA above 1, and I can’t recall seeing one play where the quarterback made something out of nothing. Everything good was about the scheme and not about talent. 2) I think a lot of the throws he asks his quarterback to make will suit Jalen Hurts. There are a lot of outside and vertical throws that Hurts can make. He loves this smash concept where the deep corner is frequently open vs. single-high coverage. Even if the Colts aren't… pic.twitter.com/BKiW2vlbV6 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) November 20, 2026 The screen game is another area where I still like his work. The Colts do more than catch the snap and immediately throw the ball outside, hoping the receiver beats a defender. They use misdirection, movement from the offensive line, and a clear effort to turn defensive aggression against itself. This example shows a clever answer to a linebacker blitzing through the B-gap. Elsewhere, I saw a bubble screen in one direction before bringing the ball back the other way, giving the defense something to react to before the actual screen develops. It doesn’t work every time, but there is thought behind how they get the ball to someone in space. Their screens have averaged 8.13 yards per play compared with 5.16 for the rest of the league, which supports what I saw. That is only 31 plays, but the screen game has been a relative strength within an otherwise awful passing offense. This is an area the Eagles could do with improving. 3) A clever way of countering the modern trend of blitzing a LB through the B-gap… fake the block and run a screen behind him! Steichen still has success with screens even in this disastrous offense. pic.twitter.com/doqdnDl79M — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) November 20, 2026 The RPO game is recognizable, too. There are quick slants and throws to the flat that Eagles fans have seen before, but I especially like how Steichen incorporates pulling linemen into some of these plays. If a linebacker sees a center or guard pull, he has a strong reason to react downhill, especially when the offense has already established that movement in the running game. Steichen can then throw into the space that reaction creates. That is why I think the variety in the running game matters beyond the runs themselves. There are good examples of Steichen giving Jones an accessible answer and putting a defender in conflict from this year. 4) They have also had success with some RPOs, which we have seen the Eagles run in the past. They work well here because they pull the center, which they do often in the run game. One benefit of pulling linemen in the run game is that it can make your RPO/play-action game much… pic.twitter.com/P1AHfYtMoN — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) November 20, 2026 The obvious response to all of this is to ask why the offense has been so bad. That is fair, and my biggest takeaway is that the receiving talent and quarterback play have made this extremely difficult. Alec Pierce’s absence has removed a significant vertical threat; Michael Pittman Jr. is gone, and Josh Downs has now departed as well. Some of the players in the clips I studied aren’t even there anymore. Steichen’s offense still needs receivers who can threaten the defense outside. The Colts have completed just 4 of their 28 targets traveling at least 20 yards downfield. They still send…

title: Eagles News: Makai Lemon or Max Iheanachor?
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Do you feel like the Eagles should’ve picked Max Iheanachor in their trade up to No. 20? Or do you stand by the team’s decision to go with Makai Lemon? Lemon was clearly the higher-rated pick in terms of the consensus […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 11: Max Iheanachor #71 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Do you feel like the Eagles should’ve picked Max Iheanachor in their trade up to No. 20? Or do you stand by the team’s decision to go with Makai Lemon? Lemon was clearly the higher-rated pick in terms of the consensus draft board, which the Eagles have leaned into in recent years. Lemon has been OK for the Eagles thus far, though it’s not easy to get a great evaluation of him in this current lackluster situation. That being said, Iheanachor plays a very valuable position and his upside is intriguing. He was my pick for the Eagles in my final mock draft . Which player would you rather have on the Birds right now? I think the Steelers found themselves a GEM at RT in Max Iheanachor… 22yrs old. Wow. Calm, square sets and patient/fast/firm hands… and a balanced mover. What a combo. VERY impressive debut – always a good thing when an OL is quiet on a broadcast hah @BrandonThornNFL pic.twitter.com/B8FOZf5JIM — Ben Fennell (@BenFennell_NFL) September 28, 2026 Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … An alternate reality where Max Iheanachor is on the Eagles, and everything else to know about Eagles-Steelers – Inquirer With the Eagles at 2-7 and preparing to face the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, it’s a perfect time to hop into the Cold Tub Time Machine — I just made that up, I think — and head back to April 23. What if Makai Lemon didn’t slide down the draft board? What if the Eagles didn’t move ahead of the Steelers — who literally were calling Lemon — to select him? What would the Eagles have done with their pick? It’s an interesting thought experiment, given what the Steelers did after realizing they couldn’t draft Lemon. They took offensive tackle Max Iheanachor, who visited the Eagles and plays a position they needed, one that came more into focus four weeks into the season when Lane Johnson retired. But here are some numbers to chew on as Markel Bell, the team’s third-round pick, prepares to make another start at right tackle. Iheanachor’s pressure rate allowed is 7.83%, while Bell’s is 7.14%, according to Pro Football Focus. Even Monroe Freeling, who was mocked to the Eagles by some and was drafted 19th by Carolina, is having a rough start to his NFL career with a pressure rate of 8.47%. Only Blake Miller (6.23%), picked 17th, is having a better season in pass protection than Bell among the tackles picked in the area of where the Eagles did. Caleb Lomu, who is a backup in New England, went seven picks after Iheanachor at No. 28, and then no tackle was selected until the Eagles drafted Bell 40 picks later. Bell’s first season hasn’t been perfect, and the circumstances haven’t been ideal, but he’s playing just as well as his peers drafted two rounds earlier. How would we all be viewing Iheanachor if he was the first-round pick? How would the Eagles? Would they still be entering the offseason wondering if they had the right tackle of the future in the building? Game Preview – PIT at PHI – Iggles Blitz One interesting subplot in this game will be the RTs. Max Iheanachor and Markel Bell are both rookies and now starting. Had the Eagles not traded up, there is a good chance they would have taken Iheanachor. Instead the Eagles moved up for Makai Lemon and took Bell in the third round. Bell and Iheanachor are having similar rookie seasons. Who will play better on Sunday? Bell has to go up against TJ Watt so that could make for a long day. Pittsburgh wants to move closer to a playoff berth. The Eagles just want to win a game. Eagles players and coaches say they haven’t given up on the season. They need to prove that with a good showing on Sunday. Eagles-Steelers questions: Reflecting on the Makai Lemon pick, previewing 2027 NFL Draft – The Athletic Berman: The context, of course, is that the Steelers were on the phone with Lemon when the Eagles traded up to acquire the wide receiver one spot ahead of them. Pittsburgh settled for Iheanachor. The Eagles would be better with a promising option at offensive tackle than at slot receiver, although it depends on their evaluation of Iheanachor and whether he would have been a markedly better long-term option than Markel Bell in the third round. Before the draft, I thought the Eagles should address the offensive line in the first round if the board allowed. They hadn’t addressed the position in the first two rounds since 2022. I also thought they could get in position for Kadyn Proctor and/or Monroe Freeling, but it did not happen. Iheanachor was in a different tier than those tackles. I’d still lean toward building through the line of scrimmage, and a combination of Iheanachor and perhaps Williams or Chris Bell in Round 3 would be better than Lemon and Markel Bell. Given how Lemon has been used, I wonder if that’s a role better addressed in a middle round, but it’s too soon to determine that. So I’d say yes on the positions, TBD on the players. What will make the 2026 Eagles season a successful one following the bye week? – BGN The 2026 Philadelphia Eagles season won’t be resulting in a Super Bowl championship. The playoff streak is also likely ending at five seasons. This season is a lost cause in terms of expectations from the summer. That doesn’t mean the 2026 season can’t be deemed a success. Bear with me here. Since the Eagles are 2-7 and aren’t expected to make the playoffs this year, there are some factors remaining in this season that can carry over into 2027. The wins and losses aren’t as important (well maybe the losses), but some aspects from 2026 can play into how the 2027 Eagles shape out. So what can make the remainder of this Eagles season a success? There are a few things to hope for in this lost season. Lew The Coop: How Will Jalen Carter Handle The Return Of Ex-Eagle Lew Nichols? – PHLY Sports Lew Nichols, still in the NFL years after he was initially named a Bo Wulf Camp Crush, comes to the LINC this weekend armed with vengeance in his heart against Howie Roseman, Nick Sirianni, Jake Elliott and the 2-7 Eagles. What does Deniz Selman make of this being the conceit of a show in November? Will Brandon Lee Gowton simp for Darius Cooper? Tune in to find out! Bowen: Nick Sirianni stumbles upon a truth about the Eagles’ offense under Sean Mannion – PHLY Eagles “I think one thing I always value about him is, anybody can come and give a play and say, ‘Hey, I want to do this, or I want to do that.’ I think he just has a really good monotonous approach to figuring out everything that could potentially happen in that situation, what the downfalls are, what the upside is and whether we move forward with some of those things. I think that just speaks to the (attention to) detail that he has.” I kept reading this quote over and over. “Monotonous approach”? I mean, it kinda fits. Sheil Kapadia noted after the Eagles lost to the Giants that the Birds have gone three and out on 43 percent of their offensive possessions, the highest rate for any team in the last three seasons, also highest percentage for any Eagles team in the 21st century. Pretty monotonous. But given that Sirianni did not fire Mannion or take away play-calling during the bye week, as had been widely anticipated, I don’t think Nick was insulting Mannion. After thinking it over, I’m pretty sure Sirianni meant meticulous approach, which is a little different. But the malapropism sums up so much. For me, anyway. Steelers EDGE Nick Herbig OUT vs. Eagles – Behind The Steel Curtain The Pittsburgh Steelers have downgraded edge rusher Nick Herbig to out for Sunday’s Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles, per Adam Schefter. Herbig has been dealing with a rib injury and didn’t practice at…

title: Eagles-Steelers Final Injury Report: DeVonta Smith will play, Dontayvion Wicks OUT
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final injury report of the week on Friday in advance of their Week 11 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Eagles ruled two players OUT: Zack Baun and Dontayvion Wicks. Baun, a rare bright spot for the Birds this season, did not practice this week due to a […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: DeVonta Smith #6, Makai Lemon #9, and Dontayvion Wicks #13 of the Philadelphia Eagles look on against the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final injury report of the week on Friday in advance of their Week 11 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Eagles ruled two players OUT: Zack Baun and Dontayvion Wicks. Baun, a rare bright spot for the Birds this season, did not practice this week due to a back injury. His absence means that Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. will start at off-ball linebacker. Wicks was limited in practice all week. He is also newly listed with a foot injury in addition to his ankle injury. The Eagles are getting DeVonta Smith back, which is nice, but it would’ve been ideal for both him and Wicks to be available for Joe Milton. The Eagles ruled one player DOUBTFUL: Smael Mondon. Mondon missed practice on Thursday and Friday after fully participating on Wednesday. Mondon would’ve been the top backup linebacker behind Campbell and Trot Jr. if healthy. Instead, the Eagles will likely look to temporarily elevate Chance Campbell and/or Anfernee Orji from the practice squad to have more depth at this position. The Eagles ruled one player QUESTIONABLE: Will Shipley. Shipley was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before missing Friday’s practice due to illness. The Eagles have until 4:00 PM Eastern on Saturday to activate him from injured reserve in time to play on Sunday. If he can’t suit up, the Eagles are left with Saquon Barkley and Jaydon Blue as the only two running backs on the roster. Elijah Mitchell is out of practice squad elevations … so the Eagles will need to sign him to the roster if they want him available to play. Which they shouldn’t, unless they’re truly trying to tank. Players notably listed without a game status: DeVonta Smith, Nolan Smith , Saquon Barkley, Jihaad Campbell, Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Andrew Mukuba, Tanner McKee , Michael Carter, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones . Smitty will play for the first time since Week 6. Nice to see the Eagles’ top receiver is back in action. Nolan Smith was upgraded to full on Friday after being limited due to illness on Wednesday and Thursday. Greenard was full go on Wednesday and Thursday before missing Friday’s practice due to rest. Carter and Jones were both limited on Wednesday and Thursday before being upgraded to full on Friday. Covey was limited in practice all week but will play and seemingly resume his role as the Eagles’ punt returner. Barkley, Campbell, Hunt, Mukuba, and McKee were full participants in practice all week. PHILADELPHIA EAGLES INJURY REPORT ( FRI DAY) OUT LB Zack Baun (back) WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) DOUBTFUL LB Smael Mondon (ankle) QUESTIONABLE RB Will Shipley (foot) … RESERVE/INJURED RB Tank Bigsby QB Jalen Hurts S Andre’ Sam RB Will Shipley (practice window open) WR Johnny Wilson The Eagles opened Shipley’s 21-day practice window to return from IR on November 16. Bigsby is currently eligible to return to the roster. Hurts, Sam, and Wilson are out for the season. RESERVE/NON-FOOTBALL INJURY S Tucker Large PITTSBURGH STEELERS INJURY REPORT (FRIDAY) The Steelers ruled six players QUESTIONABLE: starting receivers Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson, starting linebacker Patrick Queen, rotational edge rusher Nick Herbig, backup safety DeShon Elliott, and depth offensive lineman Gennings Dunker. Pittsburgh has until Saturday at 4:00 PM Eastern to activate Pittman Jr. and Wilson from IR in order for them to play on Sunday. Wilson fully participated in practice this week while Pittman Jr. was limited on Wednesday before going full go on Thursday and Friday. Their expected returns should help a struggling Aaron Rodgers. Queen will probably play. He’s never missed a game and he was full go on Friday after being limited the previous two days. Herbig probably won’t play since he did not practice this week. title: Antonio Brown critical of Steelers WR DK Metcalf amidst struggles
summary: It’s no secret at this point that DK Metcalf has been a massive disappointment ever since he was traded to the Pittsburgh Steelers. His second season in Pittsburgh has been just as disastrous as the first, as he is second in the NFL in drops with 6, while leading all receivers in penalties. Metcalf leads […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s no secret at this point that DK Metcalf has been a massive disappointment ever since he was traded to the Pittsburgh Steelers. His second season in Pittsburgh has been just as disastrous as the first, as he is second in the NFL in drops with 6, while leading all receivers in penalties. Metcalf leads the Steelers in yards with 432, but has hauled in just 35 of his 71 targets through nine games this season. The receiver admitted to the media that this was the first time he’s dealt with these kinds of struggles in his career, but a former Steeler had advice for Metcalf. Appearing on “The Matchup” podcast with former Steelers teammate Emmanuel Sanders and Chris Harris Jr., former Steelers standout wide receiver Antonio Brown told Metcalf he simply needs to come back to the ball more. “I see DK Metcalf trying to box a guy out,” Brown said. “Yo bro, you gotta go back to the ball. Take your nose to the ball. I feel like guys gotta be more confident taking their nose to the ball. You gotta take your nose to the ball first, and your eyes gotta catch it. It’s eyes, nose, hands. Most of these guys, they just use hands, no eyes. You gotta have the concentration. You gotta be focused to be a good pass catcher.” "I see D.K. Metcalf trying to box a guy out. Yo bro, you gotta go back to ball. Take your nose to the ball." @AB84 on WR drops in @NFL With @ChrisHarrisJr & @ESanders_10 on 'The Matchup' https://t.co/wK4t72rMEb pic.twitter.com/48O6vrYwlr — The Matchup (@matchup_pod) November 19, 2026 This sounds like shockingly decent advice coming from Brown, who has gained a reputation for being an internet troll at best over the course of the last few seasons. The concentration quote makes a lot of sense given the sheer number of drops Metcalf has had this season. Simply put, something has to give with Metcalf. Perhaps with the return of Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson to the Steelers’ offense, things will look smoother for Metcalf and the offense as a whole. Expect Aaron Rodgers to continue to rely on Metcalf down the stretch as the Steelers sit firmly in the playoff picture. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers-Eagles preview: What to expect from Philadelphia’s offense, defense Week 11
summary: The Steelers will travel to Philadelphia — a city where they haven’t won since 1965 — on Sunday in a game that many fans have had circled as an Eagles victory since before the season. However, the 2026 Eagles aren’t the same team that made the playoffs every year from 2021-25. They enter Week 11 […]
full_text: Photo by Todd Olszewski/Getty Images | Getty Images The Steelers will travel to Philadelphia — a city where they haven’t won since 1965 — on Sunday in a game that many fans have had circled as an Eagles victory since before the season. However, the 2026 Eagles aren’t the same team that made the playoffs every year from 2021-25. They enter Week 11 with a dismal 2-7 record, with all those losses coming in a row against the Bears, Rams, Jaguars, Panthers, Cowboys, Commanders and Giants. Philadelphia hasn’t been in the win column since a Sept. 20 victory over the Titans. Is this Eagles team finally bad enough for the Steelers to break such a lengthy losing streak in The City of Brotherly Love? Or will Philadelphia, fresh off a Week 10 bye, be able to hold off the Steelers at home for yet another season? We’ll find out in Week 11. What to expect from the Eagles’ offense Rushing YPG: 88.6 (28th) Passing YPG: 171.7 (27th) PPG: 16.4 (31st) RB: It’s been a rough year for the Eagles offense, now on its third quarterback of the season ahead of Week 11’s matchup versus the Steelers. The numbers above speak for themselves: Philadelphia has struggled on both the ground and in the air in 2026, dealing with injuries, the sudden retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson, and poor execution from players on the field. The Eagles have only scored over 20 points four times this season, and have yet to break 30 once. Before a Week 10 bye, the Eagles faced the New York Giants in Week 9, falling 19-11 in an ugly game that’s been all too familiar for the Philly faithful. But one thing did change, with the Eagles trying to spark their Jalen Hurts-less offense by replacing backup Tanner McKee with Joe “Bazooka” Milton at quarterback. He’s expected to start again against Pittsburgh on Sunday. The results were not great against the Giants, with Milton finishing with 169 passing yards and 18/34 completion in Week 9. He didn’t throw a single touchdown or interception, and was sacked a whopping seven times. However, the guy with the “Bazooka” nickname does indeed have a powerful arm, with Milton logging an 11.8% deep throw percentage along with eight air yards per attempt (both team highs for the Eagles this season). He’s also a much better runner than McKee, leading the Eagles with 64 yards on the ground and a 7.1 average against New York. Frankly, Milton plays like a still-developing quarterback. He holds onto the ball too long and doesn’t seem to go through his reads at NFL speed. However, his arm talent does allow him to rifle balls into open zones when he sees them, and there’s always a little bit of worry when playing a passer with his physical abilities — even if everything only clicks a few times a game, he can still make defenses pay. It’s worth noting that Pittsburgh hasn’t played many highly-mobile quarterbacks this year, and has had some issues with deep coverage this season. With Joe Milton getting a chance to start it's a good time for us to all remember THE PASS pic.twitter.com/WNYd7j9DRd — Bill Barnwell (@billbarnwell) November 4, 2026 With Milton under center, the Eagles have mixed up their playbook from McKee a bit with a few more rollouts and designed quarterback runs. What hasn’t changed, however, is that Philadelphia remains an 11-personnel heavy team that likes short throws outside the numbers to move the ball in the passing game. Making matters worse is that despite the short passing game, Philadelphia ranks dead-last in the league in yards after catch in 2026, with just 738 on the year. First-round receiver Makai Lemon is a name to watch as a twitchy underneath target, and Milton will get to throw to the now-healthy Devonta Smith for the first time this season after the latter missed the Giants game with injury. That’s a big boost to what was a decimated Philly receiving core in Week 9. However, Dontayvion Wicks will still be out for the Eagles against Pittsburgh. Eagles WR1 DeVonta Smith pic.twitter.com/fraYBtPOtG — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) June 1, 2026 Capping the Eagles’ offensive ceiling has been a rough year from the line, which lost All-World right tackle Lane Johnson to retirement in October and has struggled with some regression. Jordan Mailata remains a very good left tackle and Philadelphia now has Landon Dickerson back from injured reserve, but the Eagles still rank seventh-highest in sack rate allowed (9%), third-highest in pressure rate allowed (41.9%), and second-highest in runs stuffed percentage (23.5%) despite facing the seventh-most light boxes in the league. Having inexperienced signal-callers since Hurts landed on injured reserve certainly hasn’t helped the Eagles in pass protection. Philadelphia struggled mightily with interior pressure against the Giants, and gave up a number of unblocked rushers on stunts and twists. One name to watch is rookie right tackle Markel Bell, a massive human being who has struggled some in pass protection this year, but is a promising run blocker. Look at the big Markell bell on this play pic.twitter.com/1GM9qoYBTf — 𝗘𝗮𝗴𝗹𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗼𝗺 (@EaglesScoutRoom) October 6, 2026 Still, on the ground, the Eagles’ inside zone-heavy attack is tied for 28th in the NFL in yards per rush (3.7), with just 28 non-Milton yards on the ground against New York. However, star running back Saquon Barkley, who played through injury against the Giants, should be rested up after the Eagles’ bye and looking a bit more explosive. In two of Barkley’s first three games this season, he averaged 5.5 yards per carry — when healthy, the 29-year-old is still a legitimate offensive weapon. After a nightmare game against the Bengals last week, the Pittsburgh defense matches up much better against Philadelphia. The key will be stifling the Eagles’ run game and pressuring Milton, which the Steelers’ front seven is certainly capable of, especially with Derrick Harmon back in play on the interior. Milton averaged 3.12 seconds to throw last week — that should give TJ Watt more time to get home against a rookie right tackle. Still, with Devonta Smith back in the lineup for the Eagles, along with solid ancillary weapons in Lemon and tight end Dallas Goedert available, a Pittsburgh secondary that got torched last week will still need to bring a better performance to the table. That said, there should be a lot more optimism heading into this week than the last for the Steelers’ defense. What to expect from the Eagles’ defense Rushing YPG: 126.1 (25th) Passing YPG: 227.3 (18th) PPG: 24.6 (19th) RP : Much like the Eagles’ offense this year, the defensive side of the ball still possesses a lot of talent, but has performed well below expectations. A unit that was the driving force behind a Super Bowl victory just two seasons ago, the Eagles seemed poised to field a young and imposing defense that would keep them contenders for the rest of the 2020s. Instead, they were sellers at the deadline, shipping away defensive tackle Jordan Davis, whom they’d signed to a three-year, $78 million extension this March. I spoke with Brandon Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation this week , to try to get a sense of why the defense has underperformed, and he said it’s been one of the more baffling developments this season. He cited a lingering injury to superstar defensive tackle Jalen Carter and a general lack of pass rush as the biggest factor. Whether or not Carter is living up to the extension he signed this past summer (four years, $152 million) is seemingly a hot topic among Eagles fans and media, but a Steelers offensive line that just lost Mason McCormick should still be plenty concerned about his presence. Even in a “down” year, Carter’s five sacks are only two off the NFL lead for defensive tackles. Jalen Carter made his presence felt all game against Jacksonville. 5 TKL, 3 TFL, 2 SACK, 2 FF, 1 PD vs Jaguars Even in the loss, Carter was one of Philly’s biggest difference makers on defense. pic.twitter.com/NkV1yK8k0C — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) October 11,…

title: Pat Freiermuth says Steelers still believe in DK Metcalf
summary: DK Metcalf hasn’t quite lived up to expectations during his time in Pittsburgh, but that hasn’t shaken the confidence of his teammates. Pat Freiermuth opened up to the media today about the embattled wideout’s time in the Steel City. “Obviously he’s had some struggles but if you look at his effort on the run game […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images DK Metcalf hasn’t quite lived up to expectations during his time in Pittsburgh, but that hasn’t shaken the confidence of his teammates. Pat Freiermuth opened up to the media today about the embattled wideout’s time in the Steel City. “Obviously he’s had some struggles but if you look at his effort on the run game or downfield blocking, he doesn’t let his situation impact his ability to get other guys open,” said Freiermuth on Thursday afternoon. “I think that’s something that you can appreciate as a teammate and as a guy you can tell a lot about his character. You know, we’re with him until the end. He’s going to get this figured out. We’ve got a lot of trust in DK and a lot of belief in him. We paid him for a reason, and the Steelers have backed him for a reason.” #Steelers believe in DK Metcalf. Pat Freiermuth explains pic.twitter.com/r65haJHhGC — 93.7 The Fan (@937theFan) November 19, 2026 Metcalf’s struggles have been a combination of costly drops, difficulty creating separation against physical coverage and inconsistency in the Steelers’ passing game. Opposing defenses have increasingly focused on limiting his opportunities, while Pittsburgh has leaned heavily on its running game. The Steelers acquired Metcalf to be their No. 1 receiving threat, and his physical tools and big-play ability remain undeniable. He previously established himself as one of the NFL’s more productive receivers in Seattle, recording 6,324 receiving yards and 48 touchdowns from 2019-2024. While the production hasn’t consistently followed him to Pittsburgh, Freiermuth’s confidence suggests the locker room still believes Metcalf can turn things around. The challenge now is translating his talent into more consistent results on the field. Let us know what you think in the comments .
