title: Draft buzz: Interest in Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker could spur draft trade
summary: If the Titans or Chargers wind up with the No. 1 selection and stick with their franchise quarterbacks, interest in Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker could lead to a team seeking to trade up for the top overall pick.
full_text:
Drew Mestemaker 's meteoric rise through the 2026 season has seen the Oklahoma State  quarterback climb to No. 2 on ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr.'s Big Board , which might be an undersell on his eventual draft position.

 On Thursday's episode of "The Adam Schefter Podcast," Schefter examined the current 2027 NFL draft order that includes two teams that already have some confidence in their starting quarterbacks at the top.

 "There is going to be an auction, I believe, for the No. 1 pick for the right to draft Drew Mestemaker," the ESPN NFL Insider said. " Dolphins , Jets , Cardinals , Browns , whoever. Someone's going to want to trade up with the Titans or the Chargers ."

 

 Entering Week 11, the Titans (1-8) and Chargers (1-8) would have the top two picks in April's draft. With Tennessee and Los Angeles expected to stick with former top-six picks in  Cam Ward and Justin Herbert , respectively, the auction scenario could come into play for quarterback-needy teams if the Titans or Chargers wind up with the No. 1 selection.

 "Tennessee, I believe, even at the 1-hole, would stick with Cam Ward," Schefter said on the podcast. "I think that there's enough belief and conviction within that organization that they feel like right now -- and there's still eight games to go for the Titans this season -- they feel like they have a quarterback here. Cam Ward's had three head coaches and three coordinators in under two years. They want to give him some consistency."

 The "home run scenario" for Tennessee, Schefter said, would be the Dolphins, Jets or Cardinals landing the No. 2 pick and giving the Titans an additional asset to move up one slot. Tennessee could then bring in Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith -- Kiper's No. 1 player -- to join Ward and Smith's former college teammate, wide receiver Carnell Tate .

 Last week, Mestemaker deferred any talk about whether he would enter the 2027 draft, telling reporters that "there's nothing I can do about it right now."

 

 Entering the season, Kiper identified Mestemaker as among his "maybe" candidates for first-round consideration. Mestemaker, a North Texas transfer who followed coach Eric Morris to Oklahoma State, has since put up 3,239 passing yards and 30 passing touchdowns, plus another four rushing touchdowns, in his first 10 games for the Cowboys.

 There's an annual increase in value for quarterbacks in draft season. Schefter noted that Notre Dame 's CJ Carr , who also has college eligibility remaining, could be a draft riser because of his physical talent and his team's ceiling.

 "Quarterbacks are currency," he said. "If there's a quarterback you love, you take him."

 ESPN's Pete Thamel conducted a  midseason QB1 poll of 25 NFL scouts and executives  last month, asking who the top quarterback will be in next year's NFL draft. Seventeen of the 25 responses were for Mestemaker, with Carr finishing second with four votes.

title: Falcons insist winning still the goal despite trading Jessie Bates III
summary: Atlanta wanted to ensure trading away Jessie Bates III didn't send the wrong message to the team.
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Overcommunication. That has been the order of business over the past several days for Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski.

 That has included one-on-one meetings with players, small-group conversations with the team's player leadership committee and full team meetings. Stefanski has wanted to make it absolutely certain that the Falcons, despite trading two starters before the NFL trade deadline earlier this week, are not in any way giving up on this season.

 "I would tell you we've got a great group of leadership on this team," Stefanski said. "I've talked to them a lot over the last few days -- like I do all the time, but in particular now. I'm very, very confident in their leadership."

 On Monday, the Falcons traded All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Bates, aside from being arguably the best safety in the league, was also a team captain and one of the most respected veterans in the building.

 A day later, Atlanta traded starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens for reserve guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Neuzil was a Falcons success story, starting with the team as an undrafted free agent and working his way up to a starting role.

 The Falcons are 3-6. So, in that respect, it made perfect sense to get value back for two players who were set to become free agents in the offseason. With regards to Bates, a safety had not been acquired for a second-round pick since 2018. Few could blame Atlanta for making the move.

 

 "We believe the return gives us a meaningful opportunity to strengthen this roster over time," a team source said. "That does not mean Jessie stopped being an outstanding player. We are giving up something valuable and we understand that."

 On the other hand, the Falcons are in one of the most unique positions in the NFL. Their record is ugly, but they are a half-game out of first place in a weak NFC South. All four teams in the division are sitting at three wins apiece. Atlanta finishes its season playing its NFC South rivals back-to-back-to-back.

 So, there was also an argument for standing pat and making a good-faith run at the playoffs, where the Falcons have not been since 2017. Only the New York Jets have a longer drought.

 "We're still in it," quarterback Michael Penix Jr . said. "... We're so close in a lot of areas and I feel like in this organization we view that a lot. We use that a lot. We are so close.

 "I truly believe we have the team and the guys that's going to rally and flip the script because we got a lot of guys that care. Obviously, I feel like matchup wise, I feel like our team is one of the top teams in the league."

 The Falcons have shown glimpses of that, such as last month when they toppled the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers in an impressive performance. But since then, they have fallen to the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a full-on downpour and lost to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid.

 

 The schedule does not get any easier. The Kansas City Chiefs will come to town Sunday. After that, the Falcons have their bye week followed by a road game against the Minnesota Vikings , a home game against the Detroit Lions and then a trip to Cleveland. Those teams have a combined 23-10 record.

 It will be up to the team's leadership to keep the players focused on the task at hand. ESPN's FPI  is giving the Falcons only a 4.5% chance of making the playoffs, but the division remains wide open. The other three teams don't have easy schedules, either.

 Left tackle Jake Matthews , the longest-tenured Falcon and the only player left from the 2016 Super Bowl team, said Atlanta had a "really good practice" Wednesday "because everyone was kind of dialed in to 'Hey, this is our objective still and we fully expect to go out and play every weekend to win.'"

 "I think [Stefanski's] message and the point was kind of driven home that there's so much still ahead of us this season," Matthews said. "We need to double down."

title: NFL Week 11 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
summary: Eagles upsetting the Steelers? Big receiving day for Christian McCaffrey? Touchdown for Josh Downs? Let's predict 15 things for Week 11.
full_text:
Week 11 of the  2026 NFL season is underway after the Texans defeated the Colts on  Thursday night . But what will happen in the remaining 12 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

 First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs that could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

 Could the Eagles pull off an upset over the Steelers? Is 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey in for a big receiving day against the Vikings? Does Titans quarterback Cam Ward have fantasy potential against the Cowboys? Will we see another touchdown for wide receiver Josh Downs in a Chiefs uniform?

 Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Upset picks | Projected stat lines 
 Fantasy sleepers, surprises 
 TD scorers | Other predictions 

 
 

 Maldonado predicts two upsets 
 

 Philadelphia Eagles +4.5 (+180 moneyline) vs. Pittsburgh Steelers 

 Quarterback Aaron Rodgers hasn't given much reason to trust Pittsburgh laying points on the road Sunday . Philadelphia's specialty is playing more man coverage and sending extra rushers, both of which have bothered Rodgers in 2026. Plus, defensive tackle  Jalen Carter can attack an offensive line that just lost guard  Mason McCormick  ( ankle ).

 Eagles backup QB  Joe Milton taking sacks is the main concern for their offense, but he can still get positive yards as a scrambler. With wide receiver  DeVonta Smith  potentially returning from a hamstring injury, the Eagles have enough to win this by a field goal.

 
 

 

 Minnesota Vikings +3 (+138 moneyline) vs. San Francisco 49ers  in Mexico City 

 Minnesota's defense remains the strength in this Sunday night matchup . Coordinator Brian Flores brings pressure from different places, and 49ers QB  Brock Purdy  took five sacks against Dallas in Week 10 . The Vikings have also been excellent at forcing field goals near the end zone.

 

 Quarterback  Kirk Cousins faces a tough matchup himself in his second start for Minnesota, but he gives it a more reliable offense than before. In Mexico City, I trust the Vikings' defense to keep this tight and give Cousins a shot to win it late.

 

 Walder predicts three stat lines 
 

 George Karlaftis , Edge, Kansas City Chiefs : 2.5 sacks, 7 pressures, 31% pass rush win rate 

 It's hard to imagine a better matchup to record a sack than this. Karlaftis typically lines up opposite the left tackle, which means he'll face Arizona's  Jayden Williams -- who ranks dead last in pass block win rate at tackle but has missed the past two weeks with a knee injury -- or Williams' backup Josh Fryar .

 Karlaftis will be chasing down rookie QB  Carson Beck in his second career start -- Beck took five sacks (at over a 20% sack rate) in his debut against the Rams  -- or veteran journeyman  Josh Johnson . Plus, the Chiefs are 15.5-point favorites , so the Cardinals almost certainly will be behind and need to pass.

 
 

 Christian McCaffrey , RB, San Francisco 49ers : 9 receptions, 74 receiving yards, 1 receiving touchdown 

 I'm focusing on McCaffrey's receiving production because I think that will be the headline here. He is already an elite receiving back, but this Vikings matchup should result in heavy usage through the air.

 All running backs catch passes more frequently against zone coverage compared to man (almost twice as often), and Minnesota plays the second-highest rate of zone coverage in the league (74%). It also blitzes the most of any team, which would cause most running backs to stay in and block most of the time. But not McCaffrey, as he still runs a route 65% of the time when the opponent blitzes.

 So when Minnesota brings the heat in Mexico City, Purdy is going to be looking for his star running back ... a lot.

 

 
 

 Joe Burrow , QB, Cincinnati Bengals : 31-of-39, 378 passing yards, 3 touchdowns, 0 sacks, 91 QBR 

 I know this is chalky considering the heater Burrow is on, but I feel especially confident that he will put up numbers against the Commanders .

 Washington blitzes 42% of the time, the third-highest rate in the league, but somehow has a below average pass rush win rate. That is quite the indictment on its ability to disrupt the opposing quarterback. And it's an especially bad combination against Burrow, who is thriving even more when blitzed (86 QBR) than when not (77 QBR) in 2026.

 

 Burrow has also become quite adept at sack avoidance (4.4% sack rate), which is partially a reflection of better pass protection this season. Plus, the Commanders have the most pass-inducing defense in the league, based on NFL Next Gen Stats' opponent pass rate over expected.

 

 Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers 
 

 Ryan Flournoy , WR, Dallas Cowboys (37.8% rostered in ESPN leagues) 

 It's easy to overlook Flournoy as the Cowboys' WR3 behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , but he has been productive. Over the past six games, Flournoy has averaged 5.1 targets and 13.2 fantasy points per game.

 The Titans-Cowboys matchup has one of the highest totals on the slate. And Tennessee's defense has allowed the most receptions and fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.

 
 

 Cam Ward , QB, Tennessee Titans (26.0%) 

 Let's stick with the same game and go with Ward, who has scored at least 19 fantasy points in each of his past two games. He'll be without wide receiver  Wan'Dale Robinson  ( ankle ) but could get back rookie  Carnell Tate , who has missed the past two games due to a shoulder injury . Ward is a dual-threat quarterback with an excellent matchup against a Cowboys defense that has allowed the third-most fantasy points and third-most rushing yards per game to quarterbacks.

 

 
 

 Justice Hill , RB, Baltimore Ravens (18.7%) 

 Ravens running back  Derrick Henry has struggled recently, averaging just 3.0 yards per carry over his past five games. Hill, on the other hand, had at least eight touches and scored at least 8.0 fantasy points in each of those games, including 18.2 fantasy points against the Jaguars in Week 9 .

 
 Hill could continue to be more involved Sunday against the Panthers . Carolina has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to running backs this season.

 

 Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers 
 

 Josh Downs , WR, Kansas City Chiefs 

 After getting traded from the Colts , Downs caught a touchdown pass in his Chiefs debut against the Falcons . He finished with 53 receiving yards on five targets, operating as an outlet from slot alignments for quarterback  Patrick Mahomes . Plus, Downs can attack the third level on seams or wheel routes.

 Downs has a great matchup in Week 11 versus a Cardinals defense that has allowed 22 touchdown passes (tied for most in the league) and plays zone coverage on 67.5% of opponent dropbacks. Chiefs coach Andy Reid will have answers to scheme open Downs for a score.

 
 

 Javonte Williams , RB, Dallas Cowboys 

 While Williams has found the end zone only once in the past three games, he has nine rushing scores on the year and at least one goal-to-go carry in nine games. I'm expecting him to cash in on a low red zone attempt Sunday against the Titans. Tennessee has allowed 10 rushing touchdowns this season, tied for the 10th most in the NFL.

 

 
 

 Courtland Sutton , WR, Denver Broncos 

 

 Let's take Sutton in a positive matchup versus the Raiders' defense . He has only two touchdown receptions this season, but he has seen seven end zone targets from quarterback Bo Nix , including one in two of his past three games. And Las Vegas has given up 22 touchdown passes in 2026, tied with the Cardinals for the most in the league.

 

 Solak makes four more predictions 
 

 The Titans will beat the Cowboys 

 I don't particularly love the Cowboys…

title: Carmelo Anthony calls out Ravens' Humphrey over Baltimore 'criminals' remark
summary: Former NBA star Carmelo Anthony challenged Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey to do more than apologize after he said Baltimore was "best at making criminals."
full_text:
Basketball Hall of Famer Carmelo Anthony criticized the Ravens ' Marlon Humphrey for his disparaging remark about Baltimore, accepting the cornerback's apology but challenging him to do more for the city he represents.
Anthony, who grew up in West Baltimore, addressed Humphrey in a lengthy statement on Instagram on Friday, two days after the four-time Pro Bowler made a quip on his podcast that Baltimore was "best at making criminals."
In his post, Anthony described growing up on Myrtle Avenue, losing friends to violence and watching people he loved be "swallowed by a system that was built to swallow them." He said Humphrey's remarks were especially hurtful coming from a player who wears a Baltimore uniform.
"I've been sitting with this one for a couple of days, because Baltimore isn't a talking point to me. It's in my blood," wrote Anthony, a 10-time All-Star who played 19 seasons in the NBA.
"When one of our own stands on our name and says the best thing Baltimore makes is criminals, and then laughs that it'll get cut out, that doesn't get cut out for me," he wrote. "It doesn't get cut out for the kid in Baltimore who heard it. It doesn't get cut out for the mother working two jobs to keep her son off the corner."
Humphrey made the remark on an episode of "The Marlon Humphrey Show" that was released Wednesday. Asked what Baltimore was best at making, he mentioned "The Star-Spangled Banner" and National Bohemian beer before answering, "They're best at making criminals."
He received heavy fan backlash on social media Wednesday afternoon, and the podcast episode featuring Humphrey's "criminals" comment has since been deleted from his YouTube page. After Wednesday's practice, Humphrey said he regretted the remark.
The Ravens sent Humphrey home from the team facility Thursday and announced that he would be inactive for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers . Coach Jesse Minter said the punishment was for one game only and that Humphrey would not practice the rest of the week.
"He's very remorseful," Minter said Thursday. "I think he understands that words mean a lot, especially to people in this city."
In addressing Humphrey's apology, Anthony wrote: "Baltimore has been apologized to its whole life. Apologies don't build anything. Presence does."
Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott also was critical of Humphrey's remark, saying an apology was not enough. He invited Humphrey to sit down with him and some Baltimore citizens "who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made."
In his Instagram post Friday, Anthony urged Humphrey to accept Scott's invitation and even offered to accompany him.
"The Mayor opened a door. Walk through it," Anthony wrote. "And when you do, call me. I'll meet you there."

title: Bills TE Dalton Kincaid doubtful to play vs. Dolphins
summary: Bills starting tight end Dalton Kincaid, their leading receiver, is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Dolphins due to thumb and ankle injuries.
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- The Buffalo Bills on Friday listed starting tight end Dalton Kincaid as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins , one of several injuries that coach Joe Brady is dealing with ahead of a short week.
Starting cornerback Christian Benford and starting linebacker Dorian Williams have been ruled out of Sunday's game against the Dolphins, and safety Damar Hamlin , tight end Jackson Hawes and defensive lineman T.J. Sanders are all listed as questionable.
Kincaid, who is dealing with thumb and ankle injuries, is the Bills' leading receiver this season with 487 yards, which ranks seventh among NFL tight ends. His 32 receptions are second on the team.
If he isn't able to go, the Bills' best option at tight end would be Dawson Knox , who has caught 14 passes this year. Hawes and Keleki Latu are the only other tight ends on the Bills' roster; they've combined for three receptions on five targets this season.
The Bills use 13 personnel -- a package with three tight ends on the field -- on 29% of their offensive snaps, the second-highest rate in the NFL, and play more than 55% of their snaps with multiple tight ends.
Cornerback Dee Alford , who spent the week in concussion evaluation, was a full practice participant Friday and carries no injury designation into the weekend.
Alford's availability is a major deciding factor in how the Bills will handle life without Benford, who is out with a groin injury. In a pinch, Brady said Alford can bump outside from his regular nickel position to fill Benford's role while Jordan Hancock steps in to man the slot. The Bills could also turn to former first-round pick Maxwell Hairston , who began the year in the starting lineup but has since had his spot usurped by rookie Davison Igbinosun .
With Williams out, the Bills will turn primarily to rookie linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr .
The Bills next face the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

title: Why Amarius Mims is an underrated key to Bengals' success
summary: Joe Burrow is on an MVP trajectory, and a big reason is his OL, led by Amarius Mims.
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- One plane ride was all it took for Cincinnati Bengals  offensive tackle  Amarius Mims to realize enough was enough.

 In last year's Week 4 loss to the Denver Broncos , Mims turned in a performance that made his stomach turn -- seven pressures and 1.5 sacks allowed, according to Next Gen Stats, in a humbling 28-3 blowout.

 Mims watched the tape. A decision was made. He was never going to play that poorly again.

 Over a year later, Mims has more than lived up to his word. Through the first half of this season, Mims has developed into not only one of Cincinnati's best players but arguably the best right tackle in the NFL.

 His performance, along with that of the rest of the offensive line, has helped turn the Bengals' passing attack into the best in the NFL. Entering Monday's game against the Washington Commanders  (8:15 p.m., ET, ESPN), Cincinnati leads the league in passing yards per game (298.9). And as much as the team's big stars have contributed to that total, Mims also has been a big reason for that success.

 "It's crazy how my game has evolved, man," he said this week. "It's been light-years different. I'm not nowhere near the same guy I was when I first came in this building."

 The advanced metrics on Mims' play have been astounding. Per Next Gen Stats, Mims is second among all offensive tackles in one-on-one pass blocking rate. This season, he has been on an island on 87.6% of his total pass blocks. And yet, his pressure rate is the lowest among all tackles at 3.3%.

 

 For the third-year player out of Georgia, the growth stems from one hard game in Denver.

 After that loss to the Broncos, he told himself he could never again put that kind of performance on tape. And in a moment of deep self-reflection, Mims watched film from the best offensive tackles in the game to see what they did well.

 He also understood just how much he meant to the Bengals.

 "I just flipped into another mode of like, 'Hey man, this team needs me to be a big part of this offense,' and just realizing it's time for me to flip that switch and just turn into the guy I know I can be," Mims said.

 That is exactly what has happened this season, for both Mims and the entire offensive line. Mims and left tackle Orlando Brown Jr . are both ranked among the top 20 players in pass block win rate as offensive tackles. As a team, Cincinnati is ranked 19th in that category.

 While those might not seem like gaudy numbers, it's worth putting them into the proper context.

 No team in the NFL relies on pass blocking more than the Bengals. Cincinnati leads the NFL in designed pass play percentage (67.1%) and has the league's fewest rush attempts.

 Not only does that mean the offensive line is playing on its heels for most of the game, but defensive lines are also using more pass rush strategies than they would in typical situations.

 "When it comes time to when people just bring five [pass rushers], that's 5-on-5 and everyone's just got to win," said center Ted Karras , who added that quarterback Joe Burrow does a good job of recognizing that and getting rid of the ball quickly. "But when D-lines pin their ears back, it can be a little harder."

 

 But between the players' performance and the scheme from Cincinnati's coaching staff, the Bengals (7-2) are operating at levels of unprecedent success. They have scored 30 or more points in five straight games, which is the longest streak in franchise history, per ESPN Research.

 Burrow and Bengals coach Zac Taylor have repeatedly cited the team's pass blocking as a major factor for the offense's current form. One overlooked reason for the unit's success: the bond between the entire offensive line.

 "We got a lot of love and passion for the game of football and one another," Brown said. "To me, that's probably the strongest part of all of our games."

 This season, nobody has been better than Mims. He is vying to become Cincinnati's first All-Pro offensive lineman since Andrew Whitworth in 2015. But Mims has downplayed what any kind of personal success would mean to him.

 "Let me tell you -- I'm just about the team, man," Mims said. "I'm about winning first, honestly. And if accolades come, they come."

 According to Cincinnati's players and coaches, they should. Heading into this weekend's game against the Washington Commanders, Taylor offered the highest praise he doles out to any of his players.

 "The easiest phrase for me to say is I wouldn't trade him for anybody," Taylor said. "He's the one I want. I want Joe Burrow to be our quarterback, I want  Ja'Marr [Chase ] and Tee [Higgins ] playing receiver. I want Mims playing right tackle for us.

 "That's the simplest way I can put it."

title: Back at practice again, Bengals QB Burrow optimistic he'll be at full strength
summary: A full participant at practice for the second straight day despite the bug that he has battled, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is optimistic that he'll be at full strength when Cincinnati plays the Washington Commanders on "Monday Night Football."
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- With hushed tones and a plaid orange-and-black beanie nearly pulled over his eyes, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow was limited in his comments about the illness ailing him ahead of Monday's game against the Washington Commanders .
But importantly, Burrow was optimistic that he'll be at full strength when Cincinnati plays in its second primetime game and third showcase game in as many weeks.
"Getting better," Burrow said after Friday's practice.
The injury report confirmed Burrow's comments, too. He was a full participant for the second straight day despite the bug that he has battled in recent days.
Typically, Burrow talks to reporters following the first practice of the game week. But given his condition, the team bumped him an extra day as he tries to recover.
Wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase took his place instead and had a little fun with the switch. He wore Burrow's practice jersey to his news conference, opened with Burrow's trademark greeting (either one or two "hellos") and even answered a couple of questions as if he was Burrow.
But when it came time to get serious, Chase felt like Burrow was still in good shape.
"Overall, he looks good," Chase said Thursday. "I think everybody around the team is coming down with a little sickness. But overall, he still looks good, still feels the same."
Various members of the team have felt ill in recent days, starting with right guard Dalton Risner , who was added to the injury report shortly before the team's 38-18 win against the Pittsburgh Steelers last Sunday night. Risner eventually left the game because of knee injuries and has not practiced yet this week.
Burrow isn't the only starter this week who is under the weather. Cornerback Dax Hill missed his second straight practice as he also battles an illness. Myles Hinton , a backup tackle, returned to practice after being sick on Thursday.
Burrow's proven strategy to get better: sleep, hydrate and eat spicy foods.
And it helps that Cincinnati (7-2) has an extra day to prepare for the Commanders (3-5-1) given how the players have felt physically.
"A lot of sick guys early in the week, so I don't know if the energy would've been there if we were a Sunday game coming in on Wednesday," Burrow said. "But we had three days off. It was a little lower yesterday, guys coming off of that, but today guys got after it and we're ready to go."
The "Monday Night Football" contest will also mark Burrow's first regular-season game at Washington since 2020, since he suffered a season-ending ACL injury in his rookie season, an event that feels like a lifetime ago.
"It's been a long time," Burrow said. "It is crazy. This season has gone by quickly and the last six years have gone by very quickly. A lot has happened for sure."

title: Police investigate man's death after alleged altercation at 49ers-Cowboys game

full_text:
Police are investigating the death of a man who was allegedly involved in an altercation before Sunday's game between the Dallas Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers at AT&T Stadium.
According to the Tarrant County Medical Examiner's Office, Mario Narro, 36, died Wednesday in an Arlington hospital. Narro's family had contacted the Arlington Police Department on Tuesday to make a report.
Police were told Narro fell during an altercation with another fan around kickoff time. He remained for the entire game, but after complaining of pain, a friend flagged down paramedics at the stadium and Narro was transported to the hospital.
Police are in the early stages of the investigation and in the process of reviewing surveillance footage from AT&T Stadium. The Tarrant County Medical Examiner's Office will conduct an autopsy to determine the official cause of death.
Speaking on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Friday, Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones said he was unaware of what happened Sunday and that he had just received information about it.
"We had no record of an incident," Jones said, "and we'll be obviously looking into that."

title: Eugene Hilton Jr. breaks out his father's 'T-Y' touchdown celebration
summary: Eugene Hilton Jr. is the son of T.Y. Hilton, who made four Pro Bowls with the Indianapolis Colts.
full_text:
After Wisconsin  receiver Eugene Hilton Jr . opened the scoring in the Badgers' 42-10 Week 12 win against Purdue  on Saturday, he had a special celebration in mind: his dad's signature "T-Y" motion.

 

 Hilton is the son of former Pro Bowl wideout T.Y. Hilton , who racked up over 10,000 career receiving yards in an 11-year NFL career spent primarily with the Indianapolis Colts  and last with the Dallas Cowboys . After scores, the elder Hilton was known to break out a celebration that represented his name -- spreading his arms sideways to make a "T," and then putting them in the air to make a "Y."

 On Saturday, his son did the same thing -- and it's safe to say T.Y. noticed.

 "My son really scored and threw up the T-Y. Wowwwwww," he wrote on X , adding a number of emojis for emphasis. "Proud Moment!! Keep Balling!!"

 

 Hilton's touchdown against the Boilermakers, a 24-yard run on an end around, marked the third of his sophomore campaign and his first on the ground.

title: Raiders' Mark Davis unhappy with 'unfair' image of his father in 'Madden' movie
summary: Saying "I did the best I could to protect him," Raiders owner Mark Davis expressed frustration with the depiction of his father, the late Al Davis, in the new movie "Madden."
full_text:
Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis said he was "hurt" by the depiction of his father, the late Al Davis, in the movie "Madden" that was released on Prime Video this week.
"I did the best I could to protect him," Mark Davis told USA Today Sports on Friday. "It's absolutely a crime that they're able to treat people that have passed away and characterize them in ways that are unfair, and there's nobody around to protect their legacies. It's just unfair. I don't know what the purpose of the movie was to be real honest."
"Madden" tells the story of legendary football coach, broadcast and video game icon John Madden, with Nicolas Cage in the titular role and Christian Bale as Al Davis. The film has received criticism for some over-the-top portrayals of several notable sports figures, with The Associated Press review describing the performances as running the "gamut from 'SNL'-style parody to earnest drama."
"Cage's prosthetic-aided performance feels more like a well-meaning misfire than any kind of real travesty. This is more like a goofy, unfunny comedy that can't find the end zone, let alone the 50-yard line," AP reviewer Jake Coyle wrote.
Mark Davis echoed some of that review, calling "Madden" a cross between "Pulp Fiction," "Vacation" and "Saturday Night Live" -- and "not in a good way."
He said the filmmakers had reached out to him about aspects of the movie but that he was off-put by how it depicted his father's reaction to a massive injury to New England Patriots wide receiver Darryl Stingley during a 1978 preseason game against the Raiders. Mark Davis said the filmmakers said they wouldn't be able to change the scene.
"For them to put in the Darryl Stingley incident, that my dad was trying to talk John [Madden] out of going to see him -- that was just such a hurt to me personally because that's my father's legacy is how he treated people," Mark Davis told USA Today. "No matter whether they were Raiders or not, he cared about people. That's one of the redeeming qualities of my father throughout his life. And I just thought it was totally unfair for them to portray it that way."
Mark Davis focused his frustration on the filmmakers, saying "I don't blame Christian Bale. I don't blame Nicholas Cage. All they did was what the director and the writers told them to do."
Al Davis served as coach, general manager and owner of the Raiders. Inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1992, Davis became principal owner of the Raiders in 1972 and ran the team until his death in 2011.

title: Why is the Raiders' defense struggling, and how can it improve?
summary: The Raiders' defense has struggled mightly for weeks, but small steps of progress have been made.
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- The epitome of the Las Vegas Raiders ' defensive struggles was captured in one play during Week 10 's matchup against the Seattle Seahawks .

 With 2:43 left in the first quarter, the Seahawks faced a third-and-15 from Las Vegas' 34-yard line. The Raiders rushed four defenders, but none could bring down quarterback Drew Lock , who scrambled to the left sideline. Edge rusher Malcolm Koonce missed the tackle on Lock, and the backup-turned-starter saw wide receiver Cooper Kupp open in the end zone after he slipped past cornerback Eric Stokes for a 34-yard touchdown.

 "We've got to continue to attack the quarterback and not let him get the pass off either," coach Klint Kubiak said Monday. "[Stokes] gets highlighted on a play, but the fact is, it's a whole defensive effort of making sure that we don't give up those explosive plays."

 Despite Kubiak calling out the Raiders' effort, he believed the defense took steps forward in the 21-13 loss last week. And to some degree, he was right. The Raiders didn't allow 30-plus points, after doing so for six straight weeks, and forced two turnovers.

 

 Still, the issues that have plagued the Raiders under first-time defensive coordinator Rob Leonard were extremely noticeable. The Raiders gave up 150 rushing yards while no one in the secondary could contain wide receiver  Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who collected a season-high 171 yards on eight catches.

 With Leonard calling defensive plays, the Raiders' production hasn't been good despite having players like Maxx Crosby , linebackers Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker , and cornerback Taron Johnson in the lineup. Las Vegas enters Sunday's road matchup against the Denver Broncos ranked 31st in points allowed per game (28.9), defensive efficiency (36.75) and rushing yards per game (151.1). The Raiders have also given up a league-high 100 explosive plays.

 Kubiak has publicly expressed belief in Leonard, the defensive staff and the system in place. Nonetheless, the Raiders have to stack up good days or honest conversations about the defense's direction have to happen this offseason.

 "It's at the point of the year where every detail matters, and we all give a f---. I know everybody on defense gives a f---, and all the coaches and everybody involved really care," Crosby said. "So that's the great thing about what we have here. It's not like that's a problem, or like guys are going against each other, or anything like that. We just have to keep staying together and getting tighter and find solutions."

 Last week, Leonard said it was humbling to hear Kubiak tell reporters that he's standing behind the defensive staff.

 Kubiak had no prior relationship with Leonard before elevating him from run game coordinator/defensive line coach to coordinator in February. General manager John Spytek and pass game coordinator/defensive backs coach Joe Woods spoke highly of Leonard, prompting an interview. Kubiak was impressed by Leonard's plan for the defense and the support he had in the building.

 Kubiak's continued faith in Leonard's defensive operation stems from seeing it work earlier in the season. During the Raiders' 3-0 start, they were eighth in points allowed (18), 11th in total yards allowed (316.7), second in EPA (22.65), third in defensive efficiency (75.96) and first in opponents' QBR (27).

 The Raiders were even effective at pressuring the quarterback. They were tied for seventh in quarterback pressures (42), tied for fourth in sacks (10) and first in forced turnovers (nine). But there's a difference between playing against the Dolphins, Chargers and Saints, who have a combined record of 5-22, and the NFL's elite teams, who Las Vegas has faced in the past seven weeks.

 

 Since Week 4, the Raiders' defense has been a catastrophe. Las Vegas is ranked 31st in total yards allowed (414.4), 30th in time of possession and last in points allowed (33.2), total yards per play (6.6), rushing yards (166) and EPA by a defense (minus-78.87).

 Leonard said one of the things that has disrupted consistency is fatigue.

 "I'd say fatigue makes cowards of us all," Leonard said. "When you're on the field a long time, mistakes tend to happen more often. We'll just put it that way."

 But it's more than that.

 Despite the offseason acquisitions, the Raiders still had concerns at interior defensive line and in the secondary. Up front, Las Vegas doesn't have a three-down lineman who could consistently stop the run or create interior pressure. The lack of a run stopper up front has hurt the Raiders each week.

 The Raiders are 31st in run stop win rate by the interior line (24.3%). However, they are ninth in run stop win rate by edge defenders (24.3%). Dean leads the team in run stuffs (11), followed by Walker (eight) and Crosby (seven). Interior linemen: Tonka Hemingway , Adam Butler , Thomas Booker IV and  Folorunso Fatukasi  have a combined total of eight run stuffs.

 Of course, it's hard for any team to contain the Chiefs' Kenneth Walker III , who had 177 rushing yards against the Raiders early last month, or the Bills' James Cook III (22 carries for 95 yards in Week 6). But even the teams that have been average or a tier below at running the ball have had success.

 Before the Week 8 matchup against the Jets, New York was 26th in yards per attempt (3.6) and rushing yards per game (96.4). Las Vegas escaped with a win, but the defense allowed a staggering 166 rushing yards.

 

 The Seahawks are 23rd in rushing yards per attempt (3.9) but recorded 150 rushing yards against Las Vegas.

 "I think it comes down to something simple: grown man playing blocks," Walker said. "... Not pointing fingers or whatever the case may be, just winning your one-on-one, whoever is blocking you, just getting off a block and making the tackle."

 As for the secondary, the Raiders have young players receiving significant playing time. They have relied on second-year cornerback Darien Porter , who is still learning the position after spending most of his college career as a wide receiver, rookie safety Treydan Stukes , and a pair of Day 3 picks, cornerbacks Hezekiah Masses and Jermod McCoy .

 Not saying either of them will develop into quality players in the near future. But they have each endured their fair share of growing pains, which has been expected. It doesn't help that Stokes' performance in coverage has taken a step back from last season. He has allowed a completion rate of 60.4% and a passer rating of 110.7 as the nearest defender.

 Coverage and pass rush should be a perfect marriage for a functional defense. That hasn't been the case. On top of the Raiders' pass coverage issues, they have had a hard time attacking the quarterback. Las Vegas is 25th in pass rush win rate (45.4%) despite being tied for eighth in sacks (22) and tied for fifth in pressures (96). The issue is the time it takes for the Raiders to reach the quarterback.

 The Raiders are 30th in time to pressure (2.88 seconds) and last in opponents' time to throw (three seconds). It also doesn't help that the Raiders have yet to find someone to emerge as a secondary pass rusher opposite Crosby. Kwity Paye was meant to be that player. Since Paye's two-sack performance in the season-opening win against the Dolphins, he has recorded only one sack and nine pressures.

 Leonard's first season in a new role hasn't been pretty. But the Raiders see progress even though it might not have appeared that way from the outside. Kubiak believes he has the right coaches in the building to develop the talent on the roster. Meaning, patience is required, especially when it will take more than one season to add the necessary pieces so that the team's vision for the defense can fully come to fruition.

 "I know we can be better, but I think as a group and a collective, we're playing with a relentless style of play," Crosby said. "We've been getting, I feel like, at least two turnovers a week, and we just have to keep tightening up little…

title: Raiders TE Brock Bowers (ankle, quad) listed as questionable
summary: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) is questionable for Sunday's divisional matchup against the Denver Broncos, coach Klint Kubiak said Friday.
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) is questionable for Sunday's divisional matchup against the Denver Broncos , coach Klint Kubiak said Friday.
Bowers practiced for two straight days after not participating Wednesday and said he's "feeling all right."
Kubiak didn't say whether Bowers will work out pregame to determine his game status. When Bowers was asked if he felt optimistic about his availability for the Week 11 contest with playoff implications, he said: "We'll see."
"I don't know. We still have some conversations to have," Bowers added.
Bowers injured his right ankle on the opening drive of the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks . At the 11:31 mark, left tackle Kolton Miller and a Seahawks defender tumbled over Bowers' leg during an Ashton Jeanty rushing attempt. Bowers remained on the ground before walking off the field under his own power.
Bowers went into the medical tent and then returned to the field for Fernando Mendoza 's 10-yard touchdown run. Bowers headed to the locker room after that play and was listed as questionable to return by the team.
He returned with 13:30 to go in the second quarter and made a 12-yard reception on third down. Later in the quarter, Bowers went back to the locker room, where he stayed for the rest of the first half before ultimately being ruled out.
Bowers finished with two catches for 18 yards, upping his season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns. The Raiders' offense collapsed in his absence, totaling just 27 net yards in the second half.
"I really wanted to play, so I was just doing everything I could to get back out there, like just trying a new tape job and stuff," Bowers said while reflecting on last week's game. "Felt it each time I went back out there. It was tough."
The Raiders also face a kicker dilemma. Matt Gay (hip) is questionable to play. Gay didn't practice Thursday but was on the field Wednesday and Friday, and Kubiak said he practiced well.
With uncertainty surrounding Gay's injury, the Raiders worked out three kickers Thursday: Lucas Havrisik , Younghoe Koo and John Parker Romo . If needed, the Raiders could elevate practice squad kicker and undrafted rookie Kansei Matsuzawa .
"We have Plan B and a Plan C. We got Special K [Matsuzawa]," Kubiak said.

title: Drake Maye ankle injury: Is the Patriots' season over? Can Tommy DeVito step up?
summary: If the QB doesn't return in 2026, New England faces an uphill battle against some of the NFL's best teams.
full_text:
The outlook for the  New England Patriots ' 2026 season has been dramatically altered. After suffering an injury on the Patriots' first drive against the  Detroit Lions  on Sunday, quarterback Drake Maye did not fly back from Munich with the team out of caution. Sources have told ESPN, Maye fractured his right fibula -- an injury that won't require surgery but is expected to sideline him deep into the regular season, if he is able to return this year at all.

 The 5-5 Patriots haven't been among the AFC's elite in 2026, but were hoping to make a charge to the playoffs -- and Maye potentially finding his past runner-up MVP form was one of their silver linings.

 When Maye was taking care of the football and extending plays, the Patriots were explosive and flashed potential to hang with the best -- as a Week 4 win at the Buffalo Bills showed. But when Maye was not buttoned-up with his decision-making (he entered Sunday with 11 INTs) the Patriots struggled. When he was cleaner in that area, it was just enough to get by some of the league's lower-echelon teams, with close wins against the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins , who have won a combined three games this season.

 Coach Mike Vrabel often says it's hard to win when a team's best players don't play well, and simply put, Maye is the team's best offensive player.

 Entering Week 10, he ranked top five in the NFL in Total QBR (74.2), passing touchdowns (18), yards per attempt (8.4), rushing yards by a quarterback (219) and rushing touchdowns by a quarterback (3).

 Now potentially without Maye for weeks or even the season, the question is can the team make it back to the playoffs?

 ESPN Patriots reporter Mike Reiss answers some of the top questions about the trickle-down effect of Maye's injury and analyst Matt Bowen answers a fantasy question on what to expect if you have Patriots players in your lineup.

 

 

 Is the Patriots' 2026 season over? 
 When Vrabel was hired as head coach in January 2025, he said the team's goals were to win the division, host home playoff games and compete for championships. Their odds of doing that without Maye are closer to zero, starting with the current standings -- they are 5-5 while the AFC East rival Bills are 8-1.

 

 Here is the rest of the Patriots' schedule: they are on the bye in Week 11 before a road trip to face the winless  Los Angeles Chargers , then two huge home games in a span of five days -- vs. the Bills (Dec. 6) and the  Minnesota Vikings  (Dec. 10). Then they're at the Kansas City Chiefs and the New York Jets before finishing the year with home games against the Denver Broncos and the  Miami Dolphins .

 They have played poorly the past two weeks in blowout losses to the Packers and Lions, ravaged by injuries across the roster, but Maye's presence -- even as he battled through inconsistent play with turnovers -- gave them a sliver of hope.

 Consider what happened Sunday: After New England's opening drive when Maye was injured on the final play, the Patriots totaled seven points and gained 82 yards over 10 drives, averaging 1.9 yards per play (not including kneel down). New England punted on eight of those drives, with seven three-and-outs.

 Maye has been the driving force behind the passing game. Entering Sunday, Patriots pass catchers recorded 38.1% of their yards after the catch, the third-lowest total in the NFL behind the Texans (37.1%) and Giants (36.8%), per ESPN Research.

 The defense has also mightily struggled as of late, giving the offense little room for error. Since Week 7, the Patriots are giving up the second-most yards per game (411.5), behind only the 1-8 Tennessee Titans .

 With some of the NFL's elite teams on the horizon, life without Maye could look bleak.

 

 What is Drake Maye's possible recovery timeline? 
 Maye suffered no additional ligament damage, sources told ESPN, which leaves open the possibility, but hardly a certainty, that Maye could return toward the end of the season if New England is in playoff contention.

 The recovery timeline for fractured ankles has varied, depending on the severity.

 In January, Broncos QB Bo Nix suffered a broken ankle and underwent surgery two days later. The initial recovery timetable reported was 12 weeks . In April, he underwent a clean-up surgery to fix bone spurs. Nix, who had a history of ankle injuries, was ready for training camp in July.

 In September 2022, 49ers QB Trey Lance underwent surgery on his right ankle after suffering "a fibula fracture and ligament disruption" in a game. The injury ended his season and required a follow-up surgery in December of that year to remove hardware that was causing irritation. He was cleared to participate in OTAs the following April.

 In 2024, 49ers linebacker Fred Warner said he had been playing most of the season with a fractured bone in his ankle .

 

 What can the offense get out of Tommy DeVito ? 
 Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels has been through this before, most recently in 2016 when Tom Brady was serving a four-game NFL suspension and Jimmy Garoppolo and Jacoby Brissett stepped in to help the team to a 3-1 record. McDaniels' offense has flexibility to play to the specific strengths of the quarterback, with an obvious example coming with some designed runs for Brissett in 2016 that never would have been called with Brady.

 DeVito struggled Sunday when taking over for Maye, and Vrabel noted it was a tough position for him to be thrust into because backups don't receive many, if any, first-team repetitions during the week of practice.

 

 "There were some things that he missed, but also not having a ton of live action since training camp, and really, I think he'll be ready to go coming out of the bye," Vrabel said. "I think that he'll be able to look at some things and understand, whether that's being able to transfer up into the pocket, get us in the right play, get the ball out quicker or look at protections or rotation, whatever that may be. I think that'll all improve."

 DeVito had success with the deep ball in the preseason, and made improvements processing information on defensive coverages, so some of the things he has going for him are similar to Maye. And, of course, DeVito briefly caught fire with the  New York Giants  when thrust into a similar situation.

 In eight career starts (all with the Giants), DeVito is 3-5 with a 26.4 QBR, 65.3% completion rate, 1,170 passing yards for seven touchdowns, one interception and 34 sacks. He isn't as mobile as Maye, with only 36 rushes for 198 yards during those starts.

 Vrabel reflected optimism in the backup QB they signed to a  two-year contract with a maximum value of $7.4 million in March. 

 "I have a lot of confidence in Tommy," Vrabel said Monday. "I know his toughness is going to be through the charts, and his competitiveness will be exactly what we need."

 

 Could the Patriots explore other options at quarterback?  
 That is a longer-shot scenario in terms of signing someone to be the starter, mainly due to the intricacies of the offense and the time crunch -- and also because there aren't many, if any, capable starters available. A more likely option initially is to utilize the 17-player practice squad to add a third layer of quarterback depth behind DeVito and rookie Behren Morton , the seventh-round pick from Texas Tech.

 Another avenue to explore would be other teams' practice squads to see if there is a worthy option to sign to the 53-man roster in a backup role. There are 15 quarterbacks on practice squads, a group including Will Levis (Jets), Nick Mullens (Jaguars), Kyle Trask (Cowboys) Hendon Hooker (Titans), Jake Browning (Chargers) and Luke Altmyer (Lions).

 "I don't see that being the case right now, but we'll have conversations and we'll discuss it and we'll look and see," Vrabel said Monday about the possibility of adding a quarterback.

 On Friday, the Indianapolis Colts released QB Daniel Jones , who could also be an option for the…

title: Justin Reid posts Saints farewell as team releases safety
summary: The Saints have granted Justin Reid's request to be released, with the safety posting on social media: "In life and sports, things don't always go the way you planned or hoped they would."
full_text:
METAIRIE, La. -- The New Orleans Saints released Justin Reid on Friday, with the safety posting a goodbye on social media before the move was official.
Reid thanked the Saints organization, his teammates and fans in his post on X but did not say why he requested to be released.
"I genuinely enjoyed my time here and have nothing but love and respect for this city and the people who make it so special," Reid wrote.
"In life and sports, things don't always go the way you planned or hoped they would. Unfortunately this is one of those moments. But that doesn't change the love and respect I have for this organization and this city. I truly want to see this team and city thrive. No one deserves it more than New Orleans and the Saints."
Thank you New Orleans ⚜️ https://t.co/FNHDVM6l1A
Reid had requested his release earlier in the week and was not at practice this week.
"We had those conversations, good conversations. We'll keep those personal," Saints coach Kellen Moore said. "Love Justin, felt like this was obviously the best for everyone."
Reid is the second team captain to ask for his release in a year. Former Saints wide receiver Brandin Cooks was also granted his release a year ago, but Moore said those situations were not related.
Moore acknowledged "it's not a normal occurrence" but called it "two unique circumstances with veteran players" that are considered independent cases.
"There's a personal aspect to this thing, and again, I'm going to respect that privacy standpoint," Moore said. "We have those conversations. We do what's in the best interest of obviously everyone a part of it and also the team."
Moore said Jordan Howden , who has gotten increased snaps lately, will be ready to step up as a starter with Reid gone. Reid's snap count had decreased in recent weeks.
"Obviously, Jordan has played a little more the last few weeks, and I think he's earned those opportunities," Moore said. "Justin has done a lot of good things for this organization, he's battled. Obviously, we came down to this decision."

title: Giants' Abdul Carter on lack of sacks: 'I've got to do more'
summary: On the surface, the lack of sacks and hard numbers seem insufficient, but dig deeper and it's a different story.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The traditional numbers say one thing on New York Giants  edge rusher Abdul Carter . The advanced metrics say another. It has put Carter under the microscope about whether he's actually doing enough with the immense talent at his disposal. 
 
 Carter, the No. 3 overall pick out of Penn State in the 2025 NFL draft, has two sacks, three tackles for loss and eight quarterback hits this season. That ranks him tied for 99th, 156th and tied for 55th in those categories, respectively. Not exactly impressive.    
 
 "At the end of the day, I've got to do more, especially to get more sacks, get more production," Carter said. "But at the same time, as long as my main goal is focusing on winning." 
 
 On the surface, the lack of sacks and hard numbers seems insufficient. But dig deeper and a different story gets revealed. Carter has a 29.0% pass rush win rate, 16 forced incompletions, two interceptions created and 17 quick pressures (pressures in under 2.5 seconds). That ranks him second, first, tied for sixth and tied for eighth in those categories, respectively. 
 
 The advanced metrics depict a player making a significant impact, much like the coaches' tape.   
 
 "I don't go through all those stats and try to dig out every little metric on every guy. We get a general accounting of it," coach John Harbaugh said. "I definitely look at the team stats. But I'm looking at the tape. Myself, I'm grading every single guy. Plus, every coach is grading their position all the time. And he's grading out really well on my sheet, I can tell you that, and the coaches' sheet. He's a disruptive guy. I promise you they're accounting for him. And the sacks are just going to come." 
 
 
 
 Carter is getting double-teamed on a team-high 41% of opposing quarterback dropbacks. That indicates a level of respect. 
 
 But somewhere there seems to be a disconnect between the pressures/disruptive plays and sacks. 
 
 "I'm trying to figure that out," Carter said. 
 
 It doesn't help that opposing quarterbacks are getting the ball out in 2.70 seconds before the pass. Only the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have seen quarterbacks get the ball out quicker. The Giants also aren't known to have one of the better interior pass rushing groups. 
 
 So there aren't a lot of freebies for Carter and the edge rushing group. Fellow outside linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux is still looking for his first sack of the season. 
 
 The sacks are the most glaring omission from Carter's résumé. That's where pass rushers make their name and money. Carter has just six sacks in 26 games over his first two seasons. 
 
 It's not lost on the 23-year-old edge rusher. He's seen the critiques. Just the other day, he warned on social media that he's heard the noise and to watch out Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars . 
 
 
 
 Clearly, he's noticed the critics. And he's not backing down from the critiques. 
 
 "I hear everything," Carter told ESPN. "This is New York. This is not somewhere you can hide from the noise or block it out. So I embrace everything and I definitely use it as motivation." 
 
 It's commendable that Carter is not backing down from the challenge. That says something about his confidence, which appears to be undented. Carter, who tried to wear Lawrence Taylor's No. 56 upon his arrival in New York, told NJ.com this week he's still "going to be the greatest ever."   
 
 He knows that getting sacks is a big part of making that happen. 
 
 "I think it should be on my mind," Carter said of getting the quarterback on the ground. 
 
 He hasn't done it enough his first two seasons. New York Jets rookie David Bailey has more sacks (7.5) in one fewer year. Rookie inside linebacker Arvell Reese leads the Giants with 4.5 sacks this season. 
 
 Carter still needs more fine-tuning to his game to facilitate finishing plays. He's getting the quick pressures, but quarterbacks are getting the ball out quickly as a result. When he's not getting those immediate pressures, that is when it appears to be breaking down. There is no counter that is leading to sacks. 
 
 It doesn't seem to worry the Giants much. 
 
 "I believe the sacks will come," Harbaugh said. "There is no one answer. They're going to happen. Just go play football." 
 
 Former Giants linebacker and current radio host Carl Banks said recently on his podcast that it could benefit Carter if the Giants used him in games (twists, stunts and moving spots) to potentially get free runs at the quarterback. There haven't been many of those for Carter over the first nine games of this season. 
 
 The onus is on defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. His defenses have relied heavily on blitzes and Carter for most of their pressure this season. The Giants have blitzed at a 45.3% rate since Week 4, the second highest of any team. 
 
 "We're trying to put [Carter] in positions for him to get some touches on the quarterback, but he's doing everything he's supposed to do," Wilson said. "In the run game, he's been excellent. He's holding force. The ball isn't circling outside of him. So, I love where he's at. I just wish the production was a little bit more for him right now because he deserves it, especially the work that he's putting in." 
 
 While Carter's coaches are singing his praises, he knows it's going to take more to get the doubters on board. Two sacks in nine games isn't going to do it. Four sacks for the second straight season isn't going to impress any All-Pro or Pro Bowl voters. 
 
 The lack of traditional stats is notable. Even to Carter.   
 
 "It's definitely frustrating," he said. "But at the end of the day, it's not going to blind me from the main goal. And the main goal is to always going to be to win. But at the same time, I can always have that extra chip on my shoulder. I have to do more. I have to get more production. But I'm not going to chase. I'm not going to do something outside my job. 
 
 "As long as I'm doing everything to contribute to winning, I'll be all right. We just got to win. That's all."

title: Jets QB Geno Smith (ankle) cleared to start vs. Chargers
summary: Jets quarterback Geno Smith made it through the practice week with no setbacks and was cleared to face the Chargers.
full_text:
New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith , who said Wednesday that his plan is to play Sunday despite a balky left ankle, made it through the practice week with no setbacks and was cleared to face the Los Angeles Chargers .
After two days of limited practice, Smith was a full participant Friday and has no injury designation on the final report.
Before Friday's practice, coach Aaron Glenn said that Smith had looked "solid" on Wednesday and Thursday and that his prospects for playing were "very encouraging."
Smith injured his ankle in the third quarter of last Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills . He underwent X-rays at the stadium and an MRI exam Monday, which showed no significant injury, a source said.
He was seen walking with a limp Wednesday, but Smith stated matter-of-factly that he intended to play. The spiraling Jets (2-8) have lost five in a row.
Some media members and fans are calling for rookie Cade Klubnik , who replaced Smith last Sunday, but Glenn has made it clear that Smith is the undisputed starter. Glenn said that Smith is performing well and that it would be "disrespectful" to replace him for the sake of evaluating Klubnik, a fourth-round pick from Clemson.
The Jets hope Smith can lead the offense out of its funk -- nine straight quarters without a touchdown. They will be without their No. 3 and No. 4 receivers: rookie Omar Cooper Jr (ankle, hip) and Isaiah Williams (ribs).
Tim Patrick , a healthy scratch last week, could be in the No. 3 role against the Chargers. They also could elevate veteran Sterling Shepard from the practice squad.

title: Edge Jonathan Greenard loves to makes plays, despite Eagles' standing
summary: Greenard speaks on his injury-filled season and outlook for the second half of the year.
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA -- There were flashes during the Eagles' Week 9 loss to the New York Giants that suggested edge Jonathan Greenard was turning the corner, and the defense along with him.

 That included a rush on third down in the first quarter where he swatted tackle Andrew Thomas ' hands away, beat him around the edge and pummeled quarterback J.J. McCarthy as he turned to try to escape the pocket. Greenard rose to his feet and performed his signature high-kick sack celebration.

 It was the first time he was able to showcase it in an Eagles uniform. Dealing with pec and ankle injuries, Greenard has not been able to fully chase the lofty expectations that came after Philadelphia sent two third-round picks to the Minnesota Vikings for Greenard in April and then signed him to a four-year, $100 million extension .

 He has played six of nine games and has one sack, three QB hits and a tackle for loss, with the sack, TFL and two of the QB hits coming against New York.

 "Nobody was more optimistic than I was [coming to Philly], enthusiastic about all of this, than me. Unfortunate things happen and it's tried to derail me but it's not going to derail my motivation for this game," Greenard told ESPN. "I still love this game more than anything, I love making plays."

 

 It would be a nice story arc if Greenard were at full health and ready to play without limitation coming off the team's bye, but that's simply not the reality of his season.

 The left ankle injury he suffered while pressuring  Matthew Stafford  in Week 4 against the Los Angeles Rams lingers. It swelled up on him during a flight to Georgia last week as he returned home to take care of some things at his property, he said, and remains a limiting factor on the field. The physical demands of the NFL simply do not allow the healing time required to get to 100%.

 But there has been improvement, something that Greenard sensed against New York whether it was setting the edge against the run or effectively executing an inside pass rush.

 "Whatever move feels good we're going to find a way to get to that move and be physical, be myself as much as I can. I think slowly in that game I started getting that confidence back of, 'OK, I can do certain things with this move that I used to be able to do,'" he said.

 "I can finally run to the ball. With this foot I was only able to strike and make a tackle. I wasn't able to run for real in past times I've been in the game. But this past game it was like I can actually run more comfortable. It still bothers [me] but I can kind of do a lot more."

 That's good news for an Eagles defense that is tied for 29 th in sacks (16).

 Greenard, who had 24.5 sacks over a two-year stretch in 2023-24, was supposed to lead a pass rush featuring Jalyx Hunt ,  Nolan Smith Jr ., Arnold Ebiketie and  AJ Epenesa  but he injured his pec during an offseason weightlifting session at the team facility.

 

 "It's actually embarrassing to speak about how it happened but it's one of those things," said Greenard, who indicated he injured himself while doing chest fly reps. "Offseason, moving, was probably fatigued, tired, dehydrated, I just flew in. There were a lot of factors. I'm still trying to reason with it and figure out how that s--- happened but it just happens."

 Greenard avoided surgery but was sidelined all of training camp and the first two games of the regular season and was eased back into action upon his return.

 "He missed the whole training camp and missed the first part of the season and when he came back he got hurt again," said Ebiketie. "Having to deal with rehab and everything, it was hard. Now getting back to it, it's been good to see him out there doing his thing. I feel like it was just a matter of time."

 With Greenard more like his old self the defense morphed into form against the Giants, racking up nine quarterback hits, five sacks and 14 tackles for loss, offering hope that Greenard and the defense can have a resurgence over the second half of the season.

 "Anybody that knows me knows that I can play through anything. It's pretty bad if I can't go out there," he said. "I've never been a guy that's just been comfortable being paid and X, Y, Z. I understand how it looks from the optics, but I have never been that.

 "Whatever I've got to push through, whatever I've got to do to get to that point, you're gonna see me doing it."
